ll338-not-with-eyeservice.reason: Opens on a work-from-home chart; the answer (the eyes of the LORD are in every place, so work as to Him) only arrives in section two; ends on talk prompts and a weekly task.
ll338-not-with-eyeservice.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Who is watching when you work alone? Yahweh is. There is no unwatched room: His eyes are in every place, and the Master who went away is coming back to look at what you brought, not at how busy you looked. So the faithful worker does not work for the eyes of people. He works heartily, as to the Lord (Colossians 3:23). Here is how the Word shows it.
ll338-not-with-eyeservice.example: ONE AFTERNOON, TWO WORKERS. Say two people work from their kitchens on the same Tuesday. One answers every message within a minute so she looks busy, then lets the real report slide to Friday. The other is slow to reply for an hour because she is finishing the report, then answers plainly and sends it done. The first is working for the eyes on her screen. The second is working for the eyes in every place, and she brings the fruit.
ll338-not-with-eyeservice.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Who is watching when you work alone? The Lord whose eyes are in every place, beholding the evil and the good (Proverbs 15:3). That is a warning to the one who coasts and a comfort to the honest worker nobody thanks, because the Father who sees in secret rewards openly (Matthew 6:4). So do the task you do worst when unwatched as though the Master stood at your shoulder, because He does, and bring the fruit. One day you want to hear "Well done, thou good and faithful servant".

teen.open: Who is watching when nobody is around? Yahweh is. He sees every room, so you can work for Him, not just for the people who check on you.
teen.close: So when you are alone with the work, you are not really alone. Yahweh sees it. Do it well for Him, and let what you finish speak for you.

senior.open: The title asks who is watching when you work alone. The Word answers plainly: the eyes of the LORD are in every place, and faithful work is done as unto Him, not for the eyes of men.
senior.close: So the answer stands. Yahweh sees the work done out of sight, and He rewards it openly. Work heartily as to Him, and let your fruit, not your appearance, be your report.

ll332-give-me-this-mountain.reason: Opens on a radio newsletter about midlife; Caleb's answer (strength kept by Yahweh, fruit in old age) is spread through the middle; ends on talk prompts, not on the answer.
ll332-give-me-this-mountain.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Is your strongest season still ahead of you? For the one who wholly follows Yahweh, the second half is not meant to be decline. It is meant to bear fruit. Caleb was promised a mountain at forty, waited forty-five years through other people's fear, and at eighty-five said his strength was the same and asked for the hardest hill. The strength was Yahweh's, kept for him. Here is how the Word shows it.
ll332-give-me-this-mountain.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Is your strongest season still ahead of you? Caleb's answer is yes, when the strength is Yahweh's and the asking is for what He already spoke. The waiting years were not wasted; they were kept. The gifts set down in the busy years can be picked back up. The tired one is fed and rested, not scolded. And the promise for the second half is fruit, not decline: they shall still bring forth fruit in old age (Psalms 92:14). Ask for your mountain, and your children will learn to ask too.

teen.open: Do your best years come early and then fade? Caleb was eighty-five and still strong, because his strength came from Yahweh, not from being young.
teen.close: So your strongest season is not only behind the people you love. With Yahweh, the later years can be the fruitful ones. Watch how they ask for their mountain, and learn it.

senior.open: The title asks whether your strongest season is still ahead. Caleb answers it at eighty-five: the LORD had kept him alive and kept his strength, because he wholly followed Him.
senior.close: So the second half need not be a slow decline. Those who wait on the LORD renew their strength, and they still bring forth fruit in old age. Ask Him for the mountain He named, and pass the boldness on.

ll341-whoso-removeth-stones.reason: The air-traffic story and the Word's answer (a small part under a great load is never small; stop when the witnesses disagree; build and change with care) are spread across sections; ends on talk prompts.
ll341-whoso-removeth-stones.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. What happens when one small part stops the whole system? Everything that leans on it stops too, because a small part that carries a great load is never small. As the reported outage showed, one overloaded part can overload the parts around it until the readings no longer agree, and then the honest thing is to stop. The Word teaches us to build, change and plan with that in mind. Here is how.
ll341-whoso-removeth-stones.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. What happens when one small part stops the whole system? The whole stands still, as a little fire kindles a great matter (James 3:5). The Word does not tell us to stop building. It tells us to take care: do not send everything through one part, stop when the witnesses disagree instead of guessing, prove a change before you make it, and write the plan for the bad day on a good one. Then rest in the One by whom all things consist, who never stops.

teen.open: Can one small broken part shut everything down? Yes. When a small part carries a big load, its failure can stop the whole system.
teen.close: So small parts matter a lot. Test changes before you make them, stop when things do not add up, and trust Jesus, who holds everything together and never stops.

senior.open: The title asks what happens when one small part stops a whole system. Everything leaning on it stops as well, for a small part that carries a great load is never truly small.
senior.close: So the Word answers plainly. Expect that any built thing can fail; change it with care, halt when the evidence disagrees, and plan for the hard day ahead of time. Then rest in the One who keeps us and neither slumbers nor sleeps.

ll340-wisdom-is-profitable-to-direct.reason: The blunt-iron section answers early (strategy is pointing effort, not adding it), but the lesson ends on a summary of what the Word adds and talk prompts, not on where the effort should point.
ll340-wisdom-is-profitable-to-direct.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Working harder will not fix a dull edge, so where is your effort pointing? The man with the blunt axe puts to more strength and gets no further. Wisdom is profitable to direct (Ecclesiastes 10:10). The fix is not more effort; it is pointing the effort, first toward what honors Yahweh, then the rest in order. Here is how the Word shows it.
ll340-wisdom-is-profitable-to-direct.example: MORE HOURS, SAME BAG. Say a family takes on Saturday shifts and brings home an extra $400 a month. But the same months bring $400 more in late fees and things bought in a hurry. They sowed much and brought in little. More strength did not help; the bag had holes. Stopping to consider their ways, putting the first portion first and patching the holes, does what the extra Saturdays could not.
ll340-wisdom-is-profitable-to-direct.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Where is your effort pointing? The Word asks you to stop swinging long enough to find out. Consider your ways, as Haggai said. Put the first thing first: honor the LORD with the firstfruits, and the rest can be directed. Wait for the fruit instead of eating the seed. Consider the field before you buy it. Keep the edge sharp. And remember that where your treasure goes, your heart follows (Matthew 6:21). Effort pointed that way is never wasted swinging.

teen.close: So trying harder is not always the answer. Stop and ask where your effort is going. Put Yahweh first, then point the rest where it really helps.

senior.close: So the title's question has a plain answer. A dull edge is not fixed by more strength but by wisdom that directs. Honor the LORD first with the increase, consider your ways, and point what remains with patience.

ll339-the-profit-of-the-earth-is-for-all.reason: Lays out reported IPO figures and the Word's standard (corners of the field, same-day wages, Isaiah 5:8) but by design never says whether the gain reaches the field; ends on talk prompts.
ll339-the-profit-of-the-earth-is-for-all.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Does the money from a stock sale ever reach the field? Not by itself. The figures here are reported, not proven, and a pledge to give is not a payment, so this lesson does not guess. What the Word does answer is whether it should: every fortune stands on a field of land, labor and customers, and "the profit of the earth is for all" (Ecclesiastes 5:9). Here is the standard the Word holds every fortune to.
ll339-the-profit-of-the-earth-is-for-all.example: THE SAME DAY, TWO ROADS. In the reported sale, each founder sold about $280 million in stock, the banks earned $550 million in fees, and two cloud companies stand to be paid twice, as owners and as landlords. Every one of those sums moved in a single season. Set beside them the Word's three questions for any harvest: were the corners left for the poor and stranger, was the worker paid before the sun went down, and is the field being joined to field until no place is left?
ll339-the-profit-of-the-earth-is-for-all.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Does the money from a stock sale ever reach the field? Only when someone chooses to send it there. The Word does not let gain reap to the edge: it leaves the corners, pays the worker the same day, makes the one who threshes a partaker of his hope, and warns those who lay field to field. That is not envy; the labourer and the risk-taker are worthy too. It is the standard, and it starts with your own field and your own pledge. The pattern is Jesus, who became poor so that what He had would reach us.

teen.open: When a company sells shares and people get rich, does any of it reach the workers? Not on its own. The Word says it should, because even the king eats from the field.
teen.close: So the money only reaches the field when people choose to share it. The Word says leave the corners, pay workers on time, and be like Jesus, who gave what He had.

senior.open: The title asks whether the money from a stock sale ever reaches the field. The lesson does not guess at this one sale; it holds every such fortune to the Word's own standard: the profit of the earth is for all.
senior.close: So the answer is plain. The gain reaches the field only when it is sent there on purpose: corners left, wages paid the same day, pledges kept. That standard binds the great fortune and our own household alike, after the pattern of Jesus, who became poor for our sakes.

ll334-this-i-recall-to-my-mind.reason: The answer (the past does not reopen, but Yahweh changes what it means) is scattered across David, Jeremiah, Joseph and Peter; its clearest form comes in the last section, then talk prompts follow.
ll334-this-i-recall-to-my-mind.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Can a hard past be rewritten, or does Yahweh make something else of it? The Word does not show the past being prayed back and replaced. David prayed while the matter was open, and when it was done his hope went forward. What Yahweh does is better: He keeps the past, cleanses the conscience, and changes what the memory means. Here is how the Word shows it.
ll334-this-i-recall-to-my-mind.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Can a hard past be rewritten? No, and you do not need it to be. Yahweh makes something else of it. Jeremiah remembered the affliction and called up the mercies on purpose. Joseph named a son for being fruitful in the land of his affliction. The comfort you received becomes comfort you give. And Peter's worst night stayed, but Jesus turned three denials into three charges to feed His sheep. The memory stayed. Its meaning changed. That is what redeemed means.

teen.open: Can you erase a hard thing that happened? No. But Yahweh can change what it means, so it does not stay only a wound.
teen.close: So your past is not rewritten. It is redeemed. Peter still remembered his failure, but Jesus gave him a job to do with it. Yahweh can do that with yours.

senior.open: The title asks whether a hard past can be rewritten. The Word shows that what happened stays happened, as David knew at his child's death, but that Yahweh changes what the memory means.
senior.close: So the answer is settled. The years are not undone; they are redeemed. Call His mercies to mind as Jeremiah did, let your comfort reach someone else, and see in Peter how Jesus turns a remembered failure into a charge.

ll333-heavenly-cheat-codes-life-his-way.reason: The code (the Word, open and kept and done) comes early, but the title's question about a rigged game is only answered in section eight on the real cheater; ends on talk prompts.
ll333-heavenly-cheat-codes-life-his-way.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Is life really a game someone else has rigged? There is a real cheater: the Word says the adversary deceives the whole world. But he has already lost in the open, and the winning code is not hidden. It is the Word of Yahweh, near you, hidden in the heart and done with the hands. Those who live it keep coming out ahead, so it only looks like cheating. Here is how the Word shows it.
ll333-heavenly-cheat-codes-life-his-way.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Is life a game someone else has rigged? The one who cheats is real, a liar from the beginning, but he was spoiled and made a show of openly. So the children of Yahweh can play straight and still win. The code is the Word: not hidden, kept in the heart, answered with "It is written", and done. Winning His way is not always the bigger house. It is the victory that overcomes the world, even our faith, and the Blood of the Lamb with the word of our testimony.

teen.open: Does it feel like life is rigged? There is a real cheater, the enemy who lies. But he has already lost, and Yahweh gave you the winning code: His Word.
teen.close: So life is not rigged against you. Learn the Word, keep it in your heart, and do what it says. That is the code, and it is no secret.

senior.open: The title asks whether life is a game rigged by someone else. The Word names a real deceiver, yet shows him already defeated, and it puts the winning code in plain view: the Word, kept and done.
senior.close: So the answer is plain. The deceiver cheats, but he has lost; greater is He that is in you. Hide the Word in your heart, answer with what is written, and the victory is faith, by the Blood of the Lamb.

ll331-it-doth-not-yet-appear-what-we-sha.reason: Both halves are answered (naked and not ashamed; sin brought shame, fear, hiding and death) but only after the frame, and the lesson ends on future glory and talk prompts rather than landing both parts.
ll331-it-doth-not-yet-appear-what-we-sha.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Were we made naked and unashamed, and what did sin really take? Yes. The Word says they were naked and "were not ashamed" (Genesis 2:25): no shame, no fear, no hiding. Sin took exactly those things away. Shame, fear and hiding came first, and then death passed upon all. The Word does not say more than that, so neither do we. Here is what it does say, and what Jesus restores.
ll331-it-doth-not-yet-appear-what-we-sha.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Were we made naked and unashamed, and what did sin take? We were made very good, upright, with no shame and nothing to hide. Sin took that and brought fear, hiding, toil and death. But Yahweh covered them the same day, Jesus carried the curse, and there is now no condemnation in Him. What is coming is more than Eden: raised incorruptible, bearing the image of the heavenly. So bring your shame to Him instead of hiding it. We are sons now, and we shall be like Him.

teen.open: Were Adam and Eve made with nothing to hide? Yes. They were naked and not ashamed. Sin brought shame, fear and hiding, and then death.
teen.close: So sin took away the no-shame life. But Jesus took the curse, and one day we will be like Him. You do not have to hide from Yahweh now.

senior.open: The title asks whether we were made naked and unashamed, and what sin took. The Word answers: they were naked and not ashamed, and sin brought shame, fear and hiding, and then death.
senior.close: So the loss was real, and so is the remedy. Yahweh covered them the same day; Jesus bore the curse; and at the last trump we shall be changed. What sin took, He restores beyond Eden.

ll1-the-perfect-yahweh-expects.reason: Opens by calling the never-make-a-mistake reading a misreading and defining teleios as whole and mature; ends on "The standard was never flawless. The expectation is whole."

ll2-the-energy-you-were-given.reason: States early that the stress response is the largest hidden drain on a finite energy budget, and ends on "worry drains you, rest repairs you" with the Word's call to rest.

ll3-bodybuilding-christ.reason: The cell story turns from asocial survival to cooperation within the first third and ties it to Genesis 2:18; ends on "It was not good for the man to be alone... You are a member."

ll4-dying-to-live.reason: Answers in the opening (by refusing to die for the whole, the cancer cell destroys the whole and itself) and ends on dying to self as the doorway to real life and fruit.

ll5-take-no-thought-for-tomorrow.reason: Says early that the survival switch cannot tell a lion from a worry and keeps ringing for dangers that never arrive; ends on Jesus's "Take no thought for the morrow. Your Father knows."

ll6-think-on-these-things.reason: Opens on the mind ruling the body and moves straight to Philippians 4:8 as what to dwell on; ends on what you behold you become and the mind fixed on Him at rest.

ll7-let-peace-be-the-umpire.reason: Gives Colossians 3:15 (peace as umpire, under the Word) in the first paragraph and ends on "let His peace make the call" under His Word.

ll9-the-lord-looks-on-the-heart.reason: Says early that appearance is a deceptive witness and the LORD looks on the heart (1 Samuel 16:7); ends on the Physician who tends the hidden man of the heart.

ll10-strength-and-honour-are-her-clothin.reason: Names "strong, not skinny" and Proverbs 31:17,25 early, and ends on the practical charge to build strength at any age with "Strength and honour are your clothing."

ll11-fearfully-and-wonderfully-made.reason: Answers the template question directly (you are not a copy; fearfully and wonderfully made, Psalm 139) and ends on being designed on purpose by the One who knew you in the womb.

ll8-not-by-might-a-new-body-coming.reason: Names the body's limit early and gives two answers (power by His Spirit; wearing out is a doorway to a new body); ends on "Your power is His Spirit" and 2 Corinthians 4:16.

ll12-if-one-member-suffers.reason: Opens on the kinetic chain where one stiff joint disorders the whole, ties it to 1 Corinthians 12, and ends on tending the weak link in both bodies.

ll13-a-sound-mind.reason: Opens by saying a failing mind is not a punishment and the one in Christ rests on His grip; ends on stewarding the mind and entrusting the rest to the One who never forgets your name.

ll14-ten-healed-one-whole.reason: Opens on the story of the ten; the answer (turning back to give thanks turns a blessing into an encounter) only comes past the middle, though the ending lands it.
ll14-ten-healed-one-whole.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. What separates a blessing from an encounter with Yahweh? Turning back. All ten men were healed on the road of obedience, but only one came back to the feet of Jesus to give thanks with a loud voice, and only he heard "thy faith hath made thee whole" (Luke 17:19). The blessing came to all ten. The wholeness met the one who returned. Here is how the story shows it.
ll14-ten-healed-one-whole.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. What separates a blessing from an encounter? The nine kept their healing and kept walking. The one turned back, fell at His feet, and gave thanks, and he went home whole: body, soul and standing before Yahweh. Celebration is not a receipt you issue when things go well; it is the posture that turns a blessing into an encounter. So do not let a blessing carry you past the Blesser. Turn back, say thank You out loud, and meet Him.

teen.open: Ten men got healed, but only one came back to thank Jesus. That turning back is what made the difference.
teen.close: So a blessing is something you receive. An encounter happens when you turn back and thank the One who gave it. Be the one who comes back.

senior.open: The title asks what separates a blessing from an encounter with Yahweh. In Luke 17, all ten were cleansed, but only the one who returned to give thanks was told his faith had made him whole.
senior.close: So the difference is the return. Blessed people forget quickest, as the psalm warns. Come back to Him with thanks, and the blessing becomes a meeting with the Blesser, who is better than any blessing.

ll15-seasoned-with-salt.reason: Walks TALK and the compass letter by letter; the answer (fitting words, real questions, listening, warmth and grace draw people in; quadrant mismatch shuts them down) is never gathered; ends on teaching children.
ll15-seasoned-with-salt.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Why do some conversations draw people in while others shut them down? The ones that draw people in are fitly spoken, ask real questions, listen before answering, carry a light touch, and leave the hearer fed with grace. The ones that shut people down answer before hearing, grab the topic instead of asking, or meet a person in the wrong season: a task when they wanted to be together, a push when they needed a boundary. Here is how the Word and the research line up.
ll15-seasoned-with-salt.example: THE SAME DINNER, TWO WAYS. Say a teenager comes home and says the day was rough. One parent answers at once with three things to fix. The other asks what happened, listens, and then asks which part bothered most. The first parent ran a task when the moment called for connection, and the door closes. The second drew out deep water with a follow-up question, the strongest proof of listening there is, and the door opens.
ll15-seasoned-with-salt.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Why do some conversations draw people in while others shut them down? Because people open to a word fitly spoken, to questions that draw out the deep water, to someone swift to hear and slow to speak, to warmth, and to speech that ministers grace to the hearer. They close when we answer before we hear or miss which season this moment is. And all of it must be done in love, or it is only technique. Let your speech be seasoned with salt, so the other person leaves better than they came.

teen.open: Why do some talks pull you in and others make you shut down? Good talks ask real questions, listen, stay kind, and fit the moment.
teen.close: So people open up when you ask, listen, and speak with grace. They close up when you talk over them or miss what they need right now. Season your words with salt.

senior.open: The title asks why some conversations draw people in and others shut them down. The research and the Word agree: fitting words, genuine questions, real listening, warmth and kindness open people; hasty answers and mismatched purposes close them.
senior.close: So the answer is plain. A conversation draws a person in when it is fitly spoken, patient to hear, and full of grace for the hearer. Learn the skills gladly, but use them in love, so that every person, even the one who can do nothing for you, is answered well.

ll16-rule-your-spirit-repair-the-bond.reason: Opens with the ruled spirit (never react to the reaction; Proverbs 16:32) as who holds the room, and ends on "the ruled spirit wins the room, the fast repair keeps the house."

ll17-taste-and-see.reason: Answers at once that taste is the one knowledge no one can hand you (without contact you only know about Him), lays out the trials, and ends on "Taste, and you will see."

ll18-the-flinch-comes-first.reason: States early from Ephesians 4:26 that the flinch is not the failure (Yahweh built the alarm), and ends on letting it ring, searching the story, and choosing trust.

ll19-not-ignorant-of-his-devices.reason: Answers in the opening that ignorance of the devices is the advantage and yeses are worked outside-in, names each device with its defense, and ends on "not ignorant of his devices, and not users of them either."

ll20-the-ladder-and-the-door.reason: Says early that real is not safe, but the title's answer (whoever admits and expels owns that door; Jesus is the Door and the Ladder) only arrives at claims three and four, deep in a long lesson.
ll20-the-ladder-and-the-door.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Hyperspace felt real, so why does the door still matter? Because real is not the same as safe. The Word does not call that realm imaginary; it calls its spirits familiar spirits and warns that they come dressed as light. Whoever can admit you, refuse you, terrify you and expel you owns that door. Jesus said He is the Door, and He is the Ladder between heaven and earth. Here is how the Word shows it.
ll20-the-ladder-and-the-door.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Why does the door still matter if hyperspace felt real? Because the realm behind the wrong doors is real, and it runs the thief's economy: it admits, refuses and expels on its own schedule, and those who climb up some other way are not its guests. No man ascends; the Son came down. The Ladder is Christ, and the Door is Christ, whose keeper laid down His life for the ones who enter. The hunger that sent people looking is real too, and it has an address. Through Him His sheep go in and out, and find pasture.

teen.open: If that other realm feels so real, why does it matter which door you use? Because real does not mean safe. Jesus is the only safe Door.
teen.close: So the door matters most of all. Other doors are run by spirits that lock you out or hurt you. Jesus is the Door and the Ladder, and through Him you go in and out freely.

senior.open: The title asks why the door still matters if hyperspace felt real. The Word grants that the unseen realm is real, but warns that real is not safe, and that only one Door is kept by the One who laid down His life.
senior.close: So the answer is plain. The wrong doors are owned by those who admit and expel at will; the true Door is Christ, and so is the Ladder. The hunger for a realer world is honored, and it is answered in Him, through whom His sheep go in and out.

ll21-hidden-vs-known.reason: Spends its first half on Maslow and touch; why every heart hides the same thing (it is common to man, and shame's first act was hiding from Love) only arrives in the last third, though the ending lands.
ll21-hidden-vs-known.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Why does every heart hide the same thing? Because the hiding is common to man: not enough, unlovable if truly seen, secretly failing, secretly afraid. And the instinct goes back to the garden, where the first thing shame ever did was hide from Love among the trees. Knowing others hide the same thing is comfort, but it is only company. The Word offers an exchange that removes it. Here is how the Word shows it.
ll21-hidden-vs-known.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Why does every heart hide the same thing? Because every heart carries the shame Adam hid in the trees, and "There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man" (1 Corinthians 10:13). But Yahweh still comes walking and calling, "Where art thou?" not to shame you but to bring you back into fellowship. Confess, and He forgives and covers; walk in the light, and the Blood cleanses. You were made to belong, and the Word was made flesh so you could be touched. Known beats hidden. Forgiven beats co-hidden. Come out of the trees.

teen.open: Why does everyone hide the same fears? Because we all carry the same shame Adam felt when he hid from Yahweh in the garden.
teen.close: So you are not the only one hiding. But you do not have to stay hidden. Tell Yahweh the truth. He forgives, covers it, and gives you joy instead.

senior.open: The title asks why every heart hides the same thing. The Word answers that these struggles are common to man, and that hiding has been shame's first move since Adam hid among the trees.
senior.close: So the answer is settled. Every heart hides because every heart has known shame. Mutual recognition is only company; confession brings forgiveness, covering, and joy. Yahweh still calls, "Where art thou?" Come out of the trees.

ll22-goshen-and-the-watch.reason: After a short intake note, answers with Nehemiah 4:9 (prayer and the watch as one obedience) and the two governors against countdown and fear; ends on Esther, fully provisioned, fully surrendered, afraid of nothing.

ll23-the-blessed-hope.reason: Opens by laying out the camps and charts; the answer (the calendar is the Father's, and the commands every camp shares are watch, work, do not be deceived or troubled) arrives only in the third movement.
ll23-the-blessed-hope.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Everyone has a chart, so who is right about the end? No chart holds the date. When the disciples asked for the timeline, Jesus answered that the times and seasons are the Father's, and gave them a commission instead (Acts 1:7-8). What the Word is loudest about is the same for every believer: watch, work until He comes, do not be deceived, and do not be troubled. Here is how the Word shows it.
ll23-the-blessed-hope.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Who is right about the end? The One who said "Surely I come quickly." His return is certain and personal; the calendar is the Father's alone. So weigh every chart by what the Word commands and by its fruit: does it comfort or terrorize, purify or panic, send you to witness or to the bunker? Watch, occupy till He comes, refuse date-panic, and stay prepared and hoping. That is certainty about the Person, patience about the calendar, and joy about the ending, where Yahweh wipes away all tears.

teen.open: Lots of people have charts about the end of the world. Who is right? Jesus said the date belongs to the Father. Our job is to watch, work, and not be afraid.
teen.close: So you do not need the perfect chart. Jesus is surely coming back. Stay ready, keep doing His work, ignore date-panic, and look forward to the happy ending.

senior.open: The title asks who is right about the end among so many charts. Jesus answered that question Himself: the times and seasons are in the Father's power, and our part is to be His witnesses.
senior.close: So the answer is settled. His coming is certain; its hour is not ours to know. Test every teaching by whether it comforts and purifies, and live watchful, working and at peace, looking for that blessed hope.

ll24-yahweh-is-the-only-way.reason: Answers at once with John 14:6 and Acts 4:12, lays out the three data-points and the evidence, and ends on "Yahweh is the only Way. And He is calling you by name."

You aim for excellence, but you do it as to the Lord, not for the room (Colossians 3:23-24). Work chased for applause is a treadmill; work offered to Him is rest and fire at once. And you own and produce as a steward whose hand is open, never as a servant of money (Matthew 6:24). Here is how the Word reads this age.
ll48-world-class-as-unto-the-lord-work-o.example: TWO WAYS TO SIGN THE FRONT. Say two young people each build a small business. The first needs every client and rival to see he is the best, and money becomes the goal he serves. The second works just as hard, but for an Audience of One, counts the cost before he builds (Luke 14:28), and plans from the start to have something to give to him that needeth (Ephesians 4:28). Both are excellent. Only the second is free.
ll48-world-class-as-unto-the-lord-work-o.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. You win without losing your soul by changing who you play for. Refuse "good enough," but work for the Audience of One, whose opinion is final and already received your work. Own and produce, remembering it is He that gives the power to get wealth (Deuteronomy 8:18) and that your increase is for giving. Keep your integrity when the crisis comes, wear your scar tissue without shame (Proverbs 24:16), and take the long view. That is how you stay world-class, and at peace, as unto the Lord.

teen.open: Even machines are competing for jobs now. How do you do your best without letting the race eat you up? Work hard for Yahweh, not for applause.
teen.close: So aim high, but do it for Yahweh, not to impress people. Build something real, use it to help others, do not be ashamed of your failures, and be patient. That is how you win and stay free.

senior.open: The title asks how one can compete in a global, even machine-driven, arena without surrendering the soul to the hustle. The lesson's answer is excellence offered as to the Lord, and ownership held as a steward rather than a servant of mammon.
senior.close: So the answer is the Audience of One. Work with all your might, own and produce with an open hand, prove your integrity in the trial, count the cost, and let what He gives you the power to get become blessing for family and community.

ll49-mastery-without-manipulation-lifes-.reason: Long run of Greene's counsel; 'seek first' appears mid-section two and the guardrail (mastery without manipulation, servant greatness) only at section three; ends on the sublime, not on the guardrail.
ll49-mastery-without-manipulation-lifes-.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Greene says learn by doing, and Yahweh says seek Him first, so where does mastery get its guardrail? From seeking the Kingdom first (Matthew 6:33), which puts every craft and ambition in its right place beneath Him. Learning by doing is biblical (James 1:22). But the guardrail is love: you may master a skill, never a person. In the Kingdom, greatness is strength laid underneath others to lift them, not leverage held over them (Matthew 20:26-28). Here is where the Word keeps and corrects Greene.
ll49-mastery-without-manipulation-lifes-.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Mastery gets its guardrail from the One you seek first. Keep what is true: recover your task and do it, focus, find a mentor, master envy by rejoicing with others (Romans 12:15), and keep a sober mind. Refuse what is not: no manipulation, no actor's mask, no harnessing the dark side, because love works no ill to its neighbour (Romans 13:10). Seek first the Kingdom, and your life's task is added by His hand rather than clawed for. Then even your skill points home to the Father of lights (James 1:17).

teen.open: Robert Greene says you get good at something by doing it. The Bible agrees, but it adds the most important part: put Yahweh first, and never use people to get ahead.
teen.close: So practice hard, find a mentor, and be happy when others win. But put Yahweh first, and never trick or use anyone to get ahead. Real greatness serves people.

senior.open: The title sets Greene's counsel to learn by doing beside the Lord's command to seek Him first. The lesson's answer is that Matthew 6:33 orders all mastery, and love is the guardrail that forbids manipulation.
senior.close: So the answer is mastery under the Kingdom. Learn by doing, focus, and receive counsel, but refuse every law of power that would deceive or dominate, for the greatest among you is the servant (Matthew 20:26-28), and all skill is His gift first.

ll50-the-mind-of-christ-thinking-yahwehs.reason: Opens on the program's aim, but the plain answer to 'built for more than your own reasoning' (yes: Spiritual Intelligence, the mind of Christ received by the Spirit, 1 Corinthians 2) is buried in a very long first pillar.
ll50-the-mind-of-christ-thinking-yahwehs.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Could your thoughts be built for more than your own reasoning? Yes. Your human reasoning is real but finite, and the tools it makes are derivative. Yahweh made you to receive more: His understanding, given by His Spirit, so that "we have the mind of Christ" (1 Corinthians 2:16). You train that mind by feeding daily on His Word, resting safe in the Father, standing on the identity He gave, and proving it by doing. Here are the five pillars.
ll50-the-mind-of-christ-thinking-yahwehs.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Your thoughts were built for more than your own reasoning: they were built to receive the mind of Christ. So you surrender your reasoning to His higher ways (Isaiah 55:8-9), feed daily on His Word until it re-shapes how you think, rest your mind on the Father who casts out fear, and stand on the identity He gave you. Then you prove it the only way a will is proven, by doing it (Romans 12:2; James 2:17). Not a feeling, not a slogan: a renewed mind, shining as light through good works.

teen.open: Is your brain only meant to figure things out on its own? No. Yahweh made you to receive His way of thinking through His Spirit. The Bible says we have the mind of Christ.
teen.close: So your mind was made for more than your own ideas. Read His Word every day, trust Him when you are afraid, remember who He made you, and then actually do what He says. That is how you show it is real.

senior.open: The title asks whether the mind was built for more than its own reasoning. The lesson's answer is yes: beyond human and artificial intelligence stands the understanding Yahweh gives by His Spirit, the mind of Christ (1 Corinthians 2:12-16).
senior.close: So the answer is a received mind, not merely a sharpened one. Humbled beneath His thoughts, formed by His Word day by day, kept in peace by the Father, settled in His image, it is proven in obedient works (James 1:22).

ll47-navigating-the-age-faith-critical-t.reason: First lines give the answer (spiritual maturity: faith AND critical thinking) and the five truths; the ending maps it all as Made, taught, tested, awed, and sent, faith and clear thinking together.

ll51-the-mind-of-christ-situationally-ho.reason: Opening states the renewed mind stops answering everyone the same way and gives each the fitting word (Colossians 4:6); the close says plainly 'do not reach for one flat tone' and how to find the fitting word.

ll52-how-a-lie-gets-wired-in-neuroplasti.reason: Opening answers plainly: a lie wins by repetition, and the mind mistakes familiarity for truth; the final one-line summary lands both the wiring and the Word's re-wiring of the heart.

ll54-the-same-word-different-soil-the-pa.reason: Opens well on soil as the only variable, but the test the title asks for (fruit, not feeling, marks good ground; hearing without doing is self-deception) arrives only in the good-ground and James sections; ends on an open question.
ll54-the-same-word-different-soil-the-pa.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Same seed, four outcomes: is your heart soil that bears fruit, or soil that just feels moved? The seed is the same Word for everyone, so the difference is the soil. Feeling moved is not the test; the stony ground received the Word with joy and still withered. The mark of good ground is fruit: the Word heard, understood, and done. Here is how Jesus shows the four soils.
ll54-the-same-word-different-soil-the-pa.example: ONE SERMON, TWO WEEKS. Say two people hear the same message on forgiveness and both leave in tears. One goes home, the feeling fades by Wednesday, and nothing changes. The other studies the passage again that week, finds the brother he has been avoiding, and makes it right. Both were moved on Sunday. Only one bore fruit, and only fruit shows the seed was truly received.
ll54-the-same-word-different-soil-the-pa.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Is your heart soil that bears fruit, or soil that just feels moved? You can tell by the fruit, not the feeling, the attendance, or the amen. Hearing without doing is self-deception (James 1:22). So become good ground on purpose: hear, study to understand the whole Word (2 Timothy 2:15), grow roots in private, pull the thorns of worry and money-love, and do what you heard. The heart is not fixed. The Holy Spirit can plow a hard path, and the same Word is falling on you today.

teen.open: Two people can hear the same sermon and end up totally different. Feeling moved is not the same as changing. Real change shows up as fruit.
teen.close: So do not stop at feeling something in church. Study what you heard, keep at it when it gets hard, and actually do it. That is what good soil looks like, and the Holy Spirit can soften any heart.

senior.open: The title asks whether the heart is soil that bears fruit or merely soil that feels moved. The lesson's answer from the parable is that the seed is the same for all; only fruit, not emotion, shows the Word was truly received.
senior.close: So the answer is measured by fruit. Hear, understand by study, keep the Word through trial and against the thorns, and do it. No heart is fixed; a wayside path can still be plowed into good ground.

ll55-the-connector-not-the-expert-the-bo.reason: Opening states the answer (the leader's value is connecting experts and making the room smarter together), the body text follows at once (1 Corinthians 12:21), and 'So land it here' closes on exactly that.

ll53-the-emotional-cycles-of-brain-and-b.reason: Opening names emotions as a gift that rides the body's rhythms, but what Yahweh says to do (rest and feed like Elijah, bring it to Him, rule your spirit, no big verdicts when depleted) only comes in the last third.
ll53-the-emotional-cycles-of-brain-and-b.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Why do your feelings ride your body's clock, and what does Yahweh say to do about it? Because you are embodied: poor sleep, hunger and hormones really do move your mood. Feeling is not sin, and it is not a master. Yahweh's answer is to care for the body, bring the feeling honestly to Him, and rule your spirit by the renewed mind. He met a shattered Elijah first with sleep and a meal (1 Kings 19:5-7). Here is how.
ll53-the-emotional-cycles-of-brain-and-b.example: THE SAME WORD, TWO NIGHTS. Say a coworker makes a careless remark. After a full night's sleep and a real breakfast, you shrug it off. After four hours of sleep and no lunch, the same remark feels like an attack, and you are ready to quit by three o'clock. The remark did not change; your body did. That is the moment to eat, rest, pray it out, and wait before you sign any verdict.
ll53-the-emotional-cycles-of-brain-and-b.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Your feelings ride your body's clock because Yahweh made you a real body, and Jesus Himself wept. But the body sets the stage; it does not write the script. So do what He did for Elijah: rest and eat. Then do not deny the feeling; pour it out to Him (Psalm 62:8). Do not obey it either; rule your spirit (Proverbs 16:32), with the self-control the Holy Spirit grows in you. Feelings move like weather. Who He is and whose you are is the climate behind them.

teen.open: Ever notice you get upset faster when you are tired or hungry? That is real. Your feelings are tied to your body, and Yahweh cares about both.
teen.close: So when your feelings are loud, check the basics first: sleep, food, rest. Then tell Yahweh honestly how you feel, and do not let the feeling make your choices. It will pass.

senior.open: The title asks why feelings follow the body's rhythms and what Yahweh would have us do. The lesson's answer is that emotion is embodied, a gift neither to deny nor to obey, and He tends the body first, as with Elijah.
senior.close: So the answer is stewardship. Rest and nourish the body, pour out the heart before Him, rule the spirit by the renewed mind, and make no great decision in the depleted hour. The weather passes; His truth remains.

ll57-power-to-tread-the-authority-he-gav.reason: Opens on the seventy's joy and spends most of its length on the authority given (Luke 10:19); the title's answer (rejoice rather that your names are written in heaven, Luke 10:20) arrives near the end.
ll57-power-to-tread-the-authority-he-gav.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Authority over darkness, or being known: which joy does Jesus say matters most? Being known. The authority is real; He gives it, and it is carried in His name (Luke 10:19). But He told the rejoicing seventy to rejoice rather that their names are written in heaven (Luke 10:20). Joy anchored in power rises and falls with the mission. Joy anchored in His book cannot be touched. Here is how the passage shows both.
ll57-power-to-tread-the-authority-he-gav.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Jesus does not cancel the authority; He re-anchors the joy. You carry real authority in His name, exercised by submitting to Yahweh, resisting the devil (James 4:7), and wielding the Word, from a victory already won (Colossians 2:15). But power is not where your joy lives, because a power-joy curdles into pride and sinks in a quiet week. The joy that matters most is that your name is written in heaven, known by the King Himself. Rejoice in that, and let the treading end where Scripture ends it: in peace (Romans 16:20).

teen.open: Jesus gives His followers real power over darkness. But He said the best thing to be happy about is something else: that He knows your name.
teen.close: So yes, you have real authority in Jesus' name. But do not build your joy on that. Be glad because your name is written in heaven. That never changes, even on a quiet week.

senior.open: The title sets the authority Jesus gives over the enemy beside the joy of being known by Him. The lesson's answer, from Luke 10:20, is that the authority is real but the deeper joy is a name written in heaven.
senior.close: So the answer is a re-anchored joy. Exercise the delegated authority humbly, under submission and with the Word, but rest your gladness on what cannot be shaken: your name in His book, and an enemy already under His feet.

ll58-the-wind-you-can-hear-perceiving-th.reason: First paragraph states it plainly from John 14:16-17 (perception of the Spirit is real and relationship-gated); the closing gathers 'yes' with how (witness, voice, fruit) and how it is tested (1 John 4:1).

ll56-the-person-of-the-holy-spirit-seek-.reason: Opens on the Azonwu/Pascal conversation and the Spirit as a Person; the title's answer (stop hunting demons, host the King; authority comes by submission and intimacy) arrives only mid-lesson in the deliverance section.
ll56-the-person-of-the-holy-spirit-seek-.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Are you chasing demons or hosting the King? The Word points you away from the chase. Authority over darkness does not come from studying the enemy or confronting it loudly. It comes from submitting to Yahweh and living near the Holy Spirit, the Person who fills you, the way Jesus lived in total dependence on Him. Where His light fills the room, darkness cannot stay. Here is how the Word shows it.
ll56-the-person-of-the-holy-spirit-seek-.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Are you chasing demons or hosting the King? The lesson has shown the answer from every side. The Spirit is a Person to lean on, as Jesus leaned on Him. Authority runs in James's order: submit to Yahweh first, resist, and the enemy flees (James 4:7). Rest replaces rush, and broken vessels carry His glory. So fix your eyes on the Deliverer, not on deliverance. A temple full of His light has no room left for the dark.

teen.open: Some people get obsessed with demons and spiritual fights. The Bible points you somewhere better: stay close to the Holy Spirit, and the darkness has no room.
teen.close: So you do not have to hunt demons. Stay close to the Holy Spirit and submit to Yahweh first. Where His light fills you, darkness has to leave.

senior.open: The question is whether our spiritual life centers on the enemy or on the Lord. Scripture answers clearly: authority grows from submission and nearness to the Holy Spirit, not from fixation on the dark.
senior.close: So the answer is plain. We are called to host the King, not chase demons. Submit to Yahweh, lean on His Spirit as Jesus did, and the darkness cannot share that space.

ll59-not-by-measure-all-of-him-from-day-.reason: States the answer in the first lines (John 3:34, 'not by measure') and plainly by line ~20 ('all the potential is resident from that day'); final lines gather it home: all of Him from day one; the variable is our yield.

ll61-the-audit-fruit-not-photographs-acc.reason: Opens on Dave Anderson's video and two rails; the plain answer (judge by the state of the flock and open handling of money, by fruit not access) only arrives with Ezekiel 34 and 2 Corinthians 8 well into the text.
ll61-the-audit-fruit-not-photographs-acc.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Is your leader feeding the flock or feeding himself? You can tell by fruit, not by photographs. Yahweh judges shepherds by the state of the flock: are the weak strengthened, the sick healed, the lost sought (Ezekiel 34:2-4)? And money raised in the people's name must be handled openly, honest in the sight of men (2 Corinthians 8:20-21). You test the fruit. You never pronounce on a soul. Here is the audit the Word gave first.
ll61-the-audit-fruit-not-photographs-acc.example: TWO REPORTS, ONE TEST. Say two ministries both raise money for a struggling neighborhood. One sends out photographs: the leader with officials, the leader at a gala. The other publishes what happened: who was helped, what the funds paid for, and who besides the leader checked the books. The photographs show access. The report shows the state of the flock. The Word asks for the second kind, the way the apostles appointed men of honest report over the widows' food (Acts 6:3).
ll61-the-audit-fruit-not-photographs-acc.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Is your leader feeding the flock or feeding himself? Look at what the Word measures: the condition of the flock, not the leader's access; money moved in the open with witnesses, as Paul did; the poor pleaded for, never used. Test that fruit honestly, refuse the broad brush that smears faithful shepherds, and leave every heart's verdict to the Lord who knows His own. Then turn the same audit on yourself, because you too will give account of your stewardship.

teen.open: How can you tell if a leader really cares about people or just about himself? The Bible says look at the fruit: are the people actually better off?
teen.close: So check the fruit, not the photos. A good shepherd leaves the flock healthier and handles money in the open. And leave judging hearts to Yahweh.

senior.open: Whether a leader feeds the flock or himself is a question Scripture has always answered by fruit. Yahweh measures shepherds by the condition of the people in their care.
senior.close: So the answer is the one Ezekiel gave long ago. A faithful shepherd is known by the state of his flock and by open hands with what is entrusted to him, while every heart's verdict stays with the Lord.

ll60-fearfully-and-wonderfully-maintaine.reason: Spends its first half reporting the doctors' thyroid teaching; the answer to 'without fear or food-religion' (test like Daniel, eat with thanksgiving, refuse both ditches) only comes in the Word's frame near the end.
ll60-fearfully-and-wonderfully-maintaine.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. How do you tend the temple without fear or food-religion? You measure instead of guessing, and you treat any change to your plate as stewardship, never as holiness. Daniel asked for a set test and let the results speak (Daniel 1:12-15). Paul says food received with thanksgiving is good, and that the kingdom is not meat and drink (1 Timothy 4:4-5; Romans 14:17). Here is the counsel, and then the Word's frame around it.
ll60-fearfully-and-wonderfully-maintaine.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. How do you tend the temple without fear or food-religion? The lesson's answer is one motion. Test like Daniel and weigh the numbers with your own physician. Adjust what you eat as real results and sound counsel lead, and receive every meal with thanksgiving. Refuse both ditches: neglect on one side, and on the other a plate that becomes a pulpit or a mirror that becomes an idol. Your body is His; tend it with care, and keep your crown in fearing the LORD.

teen.open: Taking care of your body matters, because it belongs to Yahweh. But that does not mean being scared of food or acting like some foods make you holy.
teen.close: So get the facts, follow good counsel, and thank Yahweh for your food. Care for your body without fear, and without judging anyone else's plate.

senior.open: Caring for the body is part of honoring Yahweh, who bought it with a price. The question is how to do it without anxiety and without turning food into a religion.
senior.close: The answer is measured stewardship. Test and consult your physician, adjust as the results lead, give thanks for every meal, and keep your hope fixed on fearing the LORD rather than on any diet or mirror.

ll62-the-age-of-counterfeits-meekness-ov.reason: The answer (control without Yahweh's authority is rebellion; meekness declines to force what you could force) is implicit and comes in the middle; the lesson ends on David's prayer for self-search rather than the title's question.
ll62-the-age-of-counterfeits-meekness-ov.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Is your influence really yours to wield? Not as your own. Trying to control people or outcomes without Yahweh's authority, even with prayer words, is the rebellion Samuel called as the sin of witchcraft (1 Samuel 15:23). The way out is meekness: power surrendered, choosing not to force what you could force, so Yahweh rules the outcome. Here is how to test which one you are using.
ll62-the-age-of-counterfeits-meekness-ov.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Is your influence really yours to wield? The lesson's answer is no, not to bend people toward your own agenda. Test it by source, fruit, community and frame: does it exalt Jesus, does it bear the fruit of the Spirit, does it flow from relationship rather than transaction? Then take the meek way Jesus called His own (Matthew 11:29). Hold your power open in His hands, and let Him search your heart where your own audit cannot reach.

teen.open: Ever used pressure, guilt, or even Bible words to get people to do what you want? That is control, not faith, and Yahweh calls it rebellion.
teen.close: So your influence is not yours to push around. Be meek like Jesus: strong, but not forcing things. Let Yahweh handle the outcome.

senior.open: Influence is a trust from Yahweh, not a tool for our own agenda. Scripture names control without His authority, even dressed in spiritual words, as rebellion.
senior.close: So the answer is that influence must be held, not wielded. Meekness, power surrendered to Yahweh, is the only safe way to carry authority, and we ask Him to search the heart we cannot fully audit ourselves.

ll63-the-family-in-the-field-offense-def.reason: Opens by asking why the fight exists; the reasons (prove, refine, form, discipline, turn evil to good) come only after a long armour section, though the final lines do gather the answer.
ll63-the-family-in-the-field-offense-def.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. If you belong to Yahweh, why is there still a fight, and what has He given you to fight with? He allows only what passes His hand, within limits He sets, and always for a purpose: to prove and refine faith, to show what is in the heart, and to turn evil into good. For the fight He gave armour to stand in, and the Blood, the Word, your testimony and praise to push back. Here is how the Word lays it out.
ll63-the-family-in-the-field-offense-def.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Why does Yahweh allow the fight, and what did He place in your hands? The enemy is on a leash, as Job's story shows, and nothing reaches you that has not first passed His hand. What He permits refines your faith, forms your heart, and bends toward good, often on a longer clock and down a longer family line than you can see. Stand in the armour. Fight with the Blood, the Word, your testimony and praise. You fight from victory, not for it.

teen.open: Being part of Yahweh's family does not mean life has no battles. He lets the fight happen for a reason, and He gives you real weapons.
teen.close: So the fight is real, but Yahweh controls how far it goes. He uses it to make your faith stronger. Stand firm, and fight with the Word, prayer, and praise.

senior.open: Many faithful people ask why trials come to those who belong to Yahweh. The Word answers with reasons, not shrugs, and it names the weapons He has supplied.
senior.close: The answer, then, is settled. Nothing reaches His children except what His hand permits, always for refining and for good, and He has armed us to stand and to overcome by the Blood and the Word.

ll64-as-thy-soul-prospereth-spirit-soul-.reason: Line two answers it ('even as': prosperity is promised to keep pace with the soul); the final paragraph lands it: a Father who loves you too much to let your circumstances outrun your soul.

ll65-processed-for-righteousness-works-w.reason: Opens on the soul's worth and the assay; the plain answer (only two righteousnesses, ours as filthy rags or His by faith, and the Son looks for His) comes a third in, then works-vs-words takes the middle before the end lands it.
ll65-processed-for-righteousness-works-w.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Whose righteousness are you really wearing when Yahweh tests the heart? There are only two kinds: your own, which never passes (Isaiah 64:6), and His, received by faith in Christ (Philippians 3:9). The Son, who holds all judgment, looks for His righteousness worn by faith. Your works and your words both show which one you have on, because both come from the same heart. Here is how the Word lays out the test.
ll65-processed-for-righteousness-works-w.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Whose righteousness are you really wearing? The lesson has shown that the test is fair and the answer is plain. Yahweh reads the whole life, because the hands and the tongue are two buckets from one well, the heart. You are not saved by cleaning up the buckets; you are saved by grace through faith. But a heart wearing His righteousness shows it in works that do the Father's will and words that bless. So give Him the spring. He is proving your heart, and He came to make it new.

teen.open: When Yahweh tests your heart, the real question is whose goodness you are relying on: your own, or Jesus's, given to you by faith.
teen.close: So you cannot earn it by being extra good. Trust Jesus, and let Him change your heart. Then what you do and what you say will both show it.

senior.open: Scripture speaks of only two kinds of righteousness: our own, which cannot stand, and Christ's, received by faith. The question is which one we are truly wearing.
senior.close: So the answer rests in Christ alone. The Son looks for His own righteousness worn by faith, and a heart that has received it will show it, in deeds that do the Father's will and in words that bless rather than defile.

ll66-watch-and-pray-the-secret-place-and.reason: First sentence gives the answer (watch and pray: know the predators so they cannot devour), named predators follow at once, and the close lands it: the saint who knows the wolves, kept in the secret place, is not surprised.

ll67-made-in-his-image-we-make-why-ai-is.reason: Opens on why man makes and the borrowed genius; the bright line 'AI is not a soul' arrives about a third in; the ending is strong but the reader waits for the plain no.
ll67-made-in-his-image-we-make-why-ai-is.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Can a machine have a soul? No. Man became a living soul when Yahweh breathed the breath of life into him, and man alone bears His image (Genesis 2:7; Genesis 1:27). A machine receives neither. We make because we are made in a Maker's image, but what we make is the work of our hands. It can process and produce; it cannot know Yahweh or be born again. Here is where the gift stops, and where the Mind of Christ goes further.
ll67-made-in-his-image-we-make-why-ai-is.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Can a machine have a soul? The lesson's answer stands: no. You can make a thing that thinks, with a mind you did not make, but only Yahweh breathes a living soul. So keep the order. Rule your tools, thank the Giver of the mind that built them, and bow to no created thing. And remember the ascent no machine can share: the believer rises not by a smarter tool but by the Mind of Christ, which the Spirit gives to a reborn soul.

teen.open: AI can be amazing, but can it have a soul? The Bible says no. Only Yahweh breathes life into a soul, and He did it for people, not machines.
teen.close: So build cool things and use them well, but never treat a machine like a person or a god. You have a soul Jesus can save. It does not.

senior.open: Artificial intelligence is a remarkable work of human hands, but Scripture is clear that it is not a soul. Only Yahweh breathed the breath of life into man.
senior.close: So the line holds. The machine may serve, but it cannot be redeemed or know Yahweh. Our hope is not in a sharper tool but in the Mind of Christ given to the reborn soul.

ll68-out-of-the-way-consecration-and-the.reason: Answer is implicit in the opening metaphor (self as straws blocking the flow) but never said plainly; seven sections follow, and the end returns to decrease only in its last two sentences after an altar call.
ll68-out-of-the-way-consecration-and-the.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Are you the obstacle to Yahweh's work in you? You can be. Your own ambitions, past experiences, need for control and trust in your own reasoning can block the flow of His power like straws in a cup. Getting out of the way is not self-hatred and not doing nothing. It is decreasing so He can increase (John 3:30). Here are the ways the Word shows it, from pruning to the broken bread.
ll68-out-of-the-way-consecration-and-the.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Are you the obstacle to Yahweh's work in you? Only when self stays in the channel. The lesson showed the way out: let Him prune the fruitful branch, listen as a witness rather than steer as a director, obey even when it costs your old success, and wait for His sending before using your power. Decrease is not disappearance. It is the bread in the Master's hands, blessed and broken and given, feeding more than it ever could whole.

teen.open: Sometimes the thing slowing down what Yahweh wants to do in you is you: your plans, your pride, your need to be in control.
teen.close: So getting out of the way does not mean you disappear. It means letting Jesus lead. When you let go, He can use your life to help way more people.

senior.open: It is a searching question whether we ourselves stand in the way of Yahweh's work. Scripture answers that our self-will can block the flow, and that decreasing clears the channel.
senior.close: So the answer is yes, we can be the obstacle, and no, the remedy is not to vanish. It is to decrease, as John said, and let our lives be blessed, broken, and given in His hands.

ll69-faithful-over-a-few-things-stewards.reason: Opens on Zach's program disclaimer and 'the rich get richer'; the plain answer (in the Kingdom, having means using) arrives mid-lesson; the end lands increase and joy rather than the having-is-using answer itself.
ll69-faithful-over-a-few-things-stewards.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Does having more mean using what you have? In the Kingdom, yes. In the parable of the talents, the servant who buried his talent still possessed it, yet the master calls him the one who has not (Matthew 25:29). Having is not holding; having is using what is in your hand. Increase follows faithfulness with what you were given, and the reward is bigger trust and the joy of your Lord. Here is how the parable shows it.
ll69-faithful-over-a-few-things-stewards.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Does having more mean using what you have? The parable says yes. The servants who put their talents to work were given more; the one who buried his out of fear lost even what he held. So steward what is already in your hand, the small account, the small audience, the present job, from a true picture of a good Father. Increase follows faithfulness. And the prize the faithful enter is the one the parable names twice: the joy of their Lord.

teen.open: Want more from Yahweh? Jesus's story of the talents says to start by using what He has already given you, not hiding it.
teen.close: So use what you have, even if it seems small: your time, your skills, your money. Yahweh trusts faithful people with more, and He shares His joy with them.

senior.open: In the parable of the talents, Jesus teaches that having is measured by use. The servant who buried his portion was counted as having nothing.
senior.close: So the answer is that faithfulness with little is what opens the door to more. Steward what you hold well, without fear, and the reward is greater trust and the joy of the Lord.

ll71-the-two-gates-and-the-father-of-the.reason: Names 'one mechanism' early but only explains why the gates are close (institutions feeding their own metrics; a shared supply line from classroom to prison) in the pipeline section and the final sentence.
ll71-the-two-gates-and-the-father-of-the.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Why may the prison door and the classroom door be closer than you think? Because they run on one mechanism: institutions feeding their own metrics while the flock goes unstrengthened (Ezekiel 34:4). One gate pulls people in; the other turns children aside from the skill they asked for. A child steered off the track early is, as this lesson puts it, nearer the far gate later. The two gates share a supply line. Here is how the Word reads both.
ll71-the-two-gates-and-the-father-of-the.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Why are the two doors closer than they look? Because the turning-aside at the near gate feeds the far one. That is why an elective is never just an elective, and why liberty proclaimed at enrollment costs a written email instead of what it costs at the prison door. So the lesson's assignment is double: fight the gates in the light, on paper, with grace, and be the family Yahweh sets the solitary in. Every child seated and taught at the near gate is one the far gate never receives.

teen.open: A school saying no to a class and a prison system might seem unrelated. This lesson shows how one can quietly lead toward the other.
teen.close: So small choices about who gets into which class really matter. Speak up, in writing and kindly, and be family to kids who need it. That keeps doors open.

senior.open: It may seem a stretch to link a classroom placement with a prison cell. Scripture and this family's own record show the same mechanism behind both.
senior.close: So the two gates are close because one supplies the other. Opening the near door, in the light and with persistence, and setting the fatherless in families, is how the far door stays closed.

ll70-the-bridegrooms-answer-only-the-fat.reason: Opens on the challenge and Matthew 24:36, then walks seven wedding parallels; the actual answer (the Father names the day by covenant order, a chosen deference, not a lack) arrives only near the end.
ll70-the-bridegrooms-answer-only-the-fat.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Why would the Son not know the day? Because He is speaking as the Bridegroom, and in that covenant the Father names the wedding day. Scripture itself says the times are in the Father's own power (Acts 1:7). This is order, not a missing capacity. The eternal Son chose to live in submission to the Father's sending, while all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge are hid in Him (Colossians 2:3). Here is the wedding pattern behind His answer.
ll70-the-bridegrooms-answer-only-the-fat.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Why would the Son not know the day? The lesson's answer is that He answered as a betrothed groom answers: my Father names the day. The price is paid, the cup is shared, the place is being prepared, and the Spirit is the pledge in your heart. His deference is the shape of His love and mission, not a gap in His Godhead, for all the fulness dwells in Him (Colossians 2:9). So the Bride's part is not date-guessing but lamp-keeping: watch, and answer Him with the Book's last prayer (Revelation 22:20).

teen.open: Jesus said only the Father knows the day He returns. Does that mean Jesus is less than Yahweh? No. He was talking like a groom in a Jewish wedding.
teen.close: So Jesus was not missing anything. In a wedding, the father sets the date, and Jesus honored that. Our job is not guessing the day but staying ready.

senior.open: The saying that only the Father knows the day has troubled many. Read inside Jesus's wedding teaching, it reveals covenant order rather than any lack in the Son.
senior.close: So the answer is that the Son spoke as the Bridegroom who leaves the day to His Father. It is chosen deference within the Godhead, and it calls us to watchful readiness.

ll72-the-berean-foundation.reason: Acts 17:11 answers the title in the first lines (received with readiness, searched daily); the closing assignment lands it exactly: receive gladly, then open the Book and check, firsthand.

ll74-church-hurt-the-counterfeit-comfort.reason: The answer (what they did is not what Yahweh is) appears a quarter in, then Karen's long story runs; the end does gather it but closes on a salvation invitation and a turn to leaders, not the title's question.
ll74-church-hurt-the-counterfeit-comfort.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Your family performed at church, but was that what Yahweh is like? No. What those people did is not what Yahweh is. Jesus condemned outward show over inward cruelty (Matthew 23:27-28), and Paul says such hypocrisy causes His name to be blasphemed (Romans 2:24). You do not have to defend them to keep Him. When father and mother forsake you, the LORD takes you up (Psalm 27:10). Here is how one wounded woman stood back up.
ll74-church-hurt-the-counterfeit-comfort.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Was the performance what Yahweh is like? The lesson's answer is no, and Karen's road shows it. The Father she ran from is the One who runs to the returning child (Luke 15:20), stays near the brokenhearted, and washes what was. Such were some of you, past tense (1 Corinthians 6:11). So the wounded can separate the two: their act was never His picture. And standing back up means letting the Blood restore you and your testimony become a weapon.

teen.open: If people at church acted one way in public and were cruel at home, that is not what Yahweh is like. Jesus was really hard on fakes like that.
teen.close: So do not judge Yahweh by people who faked it. He runs toward you, He forgives fully, and He can rebuild what was broken. Your story can help someone else.

senior.open: Many have been wounded by people who performed faith in public and wounded at home. Scripture is clear that such conduct misrepresents Yahweh and that He holds the performer accountable.
senior.close: So the answer is that their performance never portrayed Him. The wounded may separate the two, receive His cleansing and restoration, and stand again, with a testimony that strengthens others.

ll75-the-greater-yeshua.reason: Builds the Joshua/Jesus name and the unfinished north at length; who finishes the work (the Greater Yeshua binds the strong man, then hands the assignment on) is implied late, and the lesson ends on an open question to the reader.
ll75-the-greater-yeshua.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Joshua left very much land unpossessed (Joshua 13:1). Who finishes the work? The Greater Yeshua, Jesus, who carries the same name. He opened His ministry in the uncleared north, bound the strong man, and took the ground not by killing the Canaanite but by healing her daughter. Then He handed the work to His followers, to the uttermost part of the earth (Acts 1:8). Here is how the Word draws the map.
ll75-the-greater-yeshua.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Who finishes the work Joshua left undone? Jesus does. The first Yeshua cleared land with a sword and left the strong men standing. The Greater Yeshua binds the strong man and spoils his house (Matthew 12:29), and leaves the Canaanite standing, saved. Then, with all power given to Him, He sends you into the unfinished land, which is now the whole earth. So follow Him into your own unpossessed north, the place in your life or house the conquest never reached, and let Him take it.

teen.open: Joshua never finished taking the Promised Land. So who finishes the job? Jesus, whose name is the same name as Joshua.
teen.close: So Jesus finishes what Joshua could not. He beats the real enemy and sets people free. Then He sends you to help, starting with the parts of your own life He has not taken over yet.

senior.open: Joshua grew old with much land still unpossessed. The New Testament shows the One bearing the same name completing that work in a far greater way.
senior.close: So the answer is the Greater Yeshua. He binds the strong man, saves even those Israel once drove out, and commissions His people to carry the work to every nation and into every unsurrendered part of life.

ll73-the-house-of-el-and-the-only-saviou.reason: Opens on Superman's Kal-El and the El names; the answer (Yahweh alone, no other name given for salvation) is reached in the Acts 4:12 section and only lands again in the final sentence after many long sections.
ll73-the-house-of-el-and-the-only-saviou.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Whose name are you really calling on? The Word leaves one answer. Many stories borrow its words and shapes, but Yahweh is not one El among many; He is the only One. And there is none other name under heaven by which we must be saved (Acts 4:12), the name of Jesus, who saved not by being unhurtable but by laying His life down. Here is how to trace borrowed light back to its source.
ll73-the-house-of-el-and-the-only-saviou.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Whose name are you really calling on? The lesson has shown it from every angle. A hero who cannot be hurt pays nothing; Jesus paid with His blood. Every counterfeit offers something good from the wrong giver, so ask whether the giver owns what he offers. Only Yahweh does. So enjoy a story, then trace its borrowed light home, and keep your trust where the psalm keeps it: on the name of the LORD (Psalm 20:7). His is the one name that saves.

teen.open: Superheroes borrow a lot from the Bible. But when you need saving, whose name do you call? There is only one name that actually saves: Jesus.
teen.close: So enjoy the movies, but know the difference. Heroes in stories cannot save you. Jesus gave His life for you, and His is the only name that saves.

senior.open: Our culture is full of saviors borrowed from the shapes of Scripture. The question that matters is whose name we actually trust and call upon.
senior.close: So the answer is the one Peter gave. There is no other name given among men whereby we must be saved. Every borrowed rescue story points, at best, back to Him.

ll76-the-sky-the-speculation-and-the-tes.reason: Covers the creator's claims, strange biblical angels and boundaries first; the one settling question (what gospel does it bring, Galatians 1:8) arrives only in the last fifth.
ll76-the-sky-the-speculation-and-the-tes.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. What does Scripture say about angels and UFOs, and what one question settles every claim? Biblical angels are stranger than greeting cards, but the Word never addresses lights in the sky, and we do not invent what it has not said (Deuteronomy 29:29). The settling question is not what it is, but what gospel it brings. Even an angel preaching another gospel is refused (Galatians 1:8). Here is how to keep a steady heart.
ll76-the-sky-the-speculation-and-the-tes.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. What settles every claim about a strange sky? Not identifying the object, which the Word declines to do, but testing the message: does it bring another gospel? If so, refuse it, even from a genuine angel (Galatians 1:8). That lets you hold total certainty about the test and honest uncertainty about the object. So do not fear what the culture fears. Whatever is or is not up there was made by Him, is held together by Him, and has no gospel to offer you.

teen.open: UFO talk can feel scary. The Bible does not tell us what those lights are, but it gives one test that works on any claim: what message does it bring?
teen.close: So you do not need to figure out every strange thing in the sky. Just ask what gospel it brings. If it is not Jesus's good news, do not believe it.

senior.open: Talk of disclosures and strange sightings unsettles many. Scripture does not identify such things, but it gives a test that settles every claim in advance.
senior.close: So the steady answer is this. We need not name the object to judge the message. Any voice that brings another gospel is refused, and nothing in the sky changes who holds all things together.

ll77-the-king-over-the-children-of-pride.reason: The scales-as-pride answer (Job 41:15: what feels like a shield is the thing that blinds and smothers) arrives about a third in; the very long lesson ends on worthy/worthwhile rather than returning to scales and sight.
ll77-the-king-over-the-children-of-pride.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Might your scales be your shield? They may feel like one. Job 41 says of leviathan, the king over all the children of pride, that his scales are his pride, sealed so tight no air comes between them (Job 41:15-16). Pride feels like protection, but it is the plating that keeps you from seeing and slowly smothers you, and you cannot pull it off from the inside. Here is what the Word shows about pride, sight, and the way out.
ll77-the-king-over-the-children-of-pride.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Are your scales your shield? The lesson's answer is that pride only looks like armour. It keeps correction out and air out, and it blinds a man who still feels sure, as it blinded credentialed Saul until the scales fell from his eyes when the Lord met him (Acts 9:18). So stop trusting the instrument. Humble yourself under His mighty hand and let Him lift you (1 Peter 5:6). He is always worthy, you are always worthwhile, and pride has nowhere left to stand.

teen.open: Pride can feel like protection, like nobody can get to you. But the Bible says it works like scales over your eyes that keep you from seeing clearly.
teen.close: So pride is not a shield; it is a blindfold. Let Yahweh humble you and open your eyes, like Paul. You are already valuable to Him, so you do not need pride.

senior.open: Pride often presents itself as strength and self-protection. Job 41 tells us plainly that the scales are pride, sealed so tight that no air comes through.
senior.close: So the answer is that what pride calls a shield is in truth a blindness. Only an encounter with the Lord removes it, and the way up is always the way of humility.

ll80-the-four-warnings-of-a-hardening-he.reason: Walks four gates of Judas's hardening first; the answer to what separates the two endings (the direction of the sorrow, 2 Corinthians 7:10) arrives in Gate Four and the Peter section, two-thirds through.
ll80-the-four-warnings-of-a-hardening-he.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Judas and Peter both failed Jesus on the same night. What separates remorse that destroys from sorrow that restores? Direction. Remorse circles the failure and the shame, and its subject is me. Godly sorrow runs to His mercy, and its subject is Him (2 Corinthians 7:10). The difference was never the size of the sin. Here is how a heart hardens step by step, and how to keep yours soft.
