ll80-the-four-warnings-of-a-hardening-he.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. What separated the two endings? Not the sin; Peter's denial was the more public failure. It was where each man took his sorrow. Judas felt real horror and tried to pay for it himself, and it ended in death. Peter wept bitterly and turned toward the Lord, and it ended in Feed my sheep (John 21:17). So examine yourself without terror, and take what you find straight to Him. He is faithful and just to forgive and cleanse (1 John 1:9).

teen.open: Judas and Peter both let Jesus down on the same night. One gave up, and one came back. The difference was where they took their sorrow.
teen.close: So when you mess up, do not just feel awful and hide. Run to Jesus with it. He forgives, and He can still use you, just like He used Peter.

senior.open: Two disciples failed the Lord on the same night, and their endings could not be more different. Scripture names what separated them: the direction of their sorrow.
senior.close: So the answer is that sorrow which turns toward His mercy restores, while sorrow that turns only on oneself destroys. Bring every failure to Him, for He remains faithful to forgive.

ll78-the-snare-of-the-fear-of-man.reason: Opens on the psychology of shyness; the answer (yes: 2 Timothy 1:7 says the fear was not issued by Yahweh, so its sentence can be tested against a verse that outranks it) comes a quarter in and is spread through the five beliefs.
ll78-the-snare-of-the-fear-of-man.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Your mind says don't speak. Can one verse test that voice before you stay silent? Yes. Yahweh has not given you the spirit of fear, but of power, love and a sound mind (2 Timothy 1:7). So the fear did not come from Him and carries none of His authority. It is a snare, a trap you can be out of (Proverbs 29:25). Put the sentence that stops you beside a verse that outranks it. Here is how.
ll78-the-snare-of-the-fear-of-man.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Can one verse test the voice that says don't speak? It can, because that voice did not come from Yahweh (2 Timothy 1:7). Write down the exact sentence that stopped you, set the verse that answers it beside it, and say both aloud. Then turn your attention to the person in front of you (Philippians 2:4). The feeling may still come, as Moses' slow tongue stayed slow. But He promised to be with your mouth, and a sound mind no longer takes orders from the fear.

teen.open: That voice in your head saying do not speak up does not come from Yahweh. The Bible says He did not give you a spirit of fear.
teen.close: So when fear says stay quiet, check it against what Yahweh says. Then focus on the other person, not yourself. You might still feel nervous, but He is with you.

senior.open: Many of us have held back a word because an inner voice said to stay silent. Scripture gives us a way to test that voice before obeying it.
senior.close: So the answer is yes. The spirit of fear is not from Yahweh, and its claims can be weighed against His Word. The feeling may remain, but it need no longer give the orders.

ll79-justice-and-righteousness-travel-to.reason: Thesis answers it in line one (a gospel that keeps righteousness and drops justice is holed); after twelve movements it ends on family discussion prompts and a weekly checklist, so the reader does not finish on the answer.
ll79-justice-and-righteousness-travel-to.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Can a gospel be sound and still be missing something? Yes. Jesus told men who tithed every herb that they had omitted the weightier matters, judgment and mercy, and should have done both (Matthew 23:23). Salvation is by grace, not works, and it is the priority; but we are created unto good works (Ephesians 2:8-10). Yahweh even called judging the cause of the poor knowing Him (Jeremiah 22:16). A whole gospel keeps righteousness and justice together, in deed and in truth.

teen.close: So a gospel can be true and still have a hole in it. Being saved by grace is first. But caring for people who are treated unfairly is part of knowing Yahweh, too.

senior.close: So the answer is yes. A gospel may be correct in what it says and still omit the weightier matters. Grace saves us apart from works, yet we are created unto good works, and justice for the neglected belongs among them.

ll81-tongues-weighed-word-first.reason: The answers (understood languages at Pentecost, Paul governed rather than banned, no spiritual tier, charity senior) are scattered across labeled sections, and the ending turns to praying in the Spirit rather than gathering them.
ll81-tongues-weighed-word-first.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. What do Pentecost, Corinth and Paul's rules show about tongues? At Pentecost the hearers understood the gospel in their own languages (Acts 2:6-11). At Corinth, when the gift turned chaotic, Paul did not ban it; he governed it: two or three, in turn, with an interpreter, because Yahweh is not the author of confusion (1 Corinthians 14:27-33). And the gift is never a spiritual rank. Charity stays senior. Here is the text, read plainly.
ll81-tongues-weighed-word-first.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. What do Pentecost, Corinth and Paul's rules show about Yahweh's gift? It is real and given for others to understand. In the assembly it is ordered, interpreted or held, and never forbidden (1 Corinthians 14:39-40). Not all speak with tongues, so no one is lesser without it and no one may be pushed to perform it. Without charity even tongues are sounding brass. And no believer is short-changed, because the Spirit already intercedes for you beyond words (Romans 8:26).

teen.open: Tongues can start arguments. The Bible keeps it simple: it is a real gift, Paul set rules for using it in church, and it never makes anyone better than others.
teen.close: So tongues are a gift from Yahweh, used in order and with love. If you do not have it, you are not missing out. The Holy Spirit already prays for you.

senior.open: Few topics stir more debate among believers than tongues. Read plainly, Pentecost, Corinth, and Paul's instructions give a clear and peaceable picture of the gift.
senior.close: So the text shows a genuine gift, governed for order and understanding, never a mark of rank, and always beneath love. Every believer is already upheld by the Spirit's intercession.

ll82-love-fulfils-the-law-wake-up-and-ge.reason: The open-forever debt of love is named in the second section (Romans 13:8), but the lesson ends on the wardrobe line 'Dress like it', so the reader does not finish on the debt the title asks about.
ll82-love-fulfils-the-law-wake-up-and-ge.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Can a debt stay open forever? Yes, one can, and Paul says it should. Every other debt is meant to be paid off and closed. The debt of love to one another is meant to stay open, and you pay on it every day in conduct that does your neighbour no harm. Here is how Romans 13 shows it, and why the clock and the clothing belong to the same payment.
ll82-love-fulfils-the-law-wake-up-and-ge.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Can a debt stay open forever? The debt of love does, by design (Romans 13:8). It is not paid in feeling but in conduct that "worketh no ill to his neighbour", and that is how the law is fulfilled. The clock says the day is nearer than when you believed, so the payment is due now. The clothing is already issued: put on the Lord Jesus Christ and cut the flesh's supply line. Then every day you make another payment on the one debt you will never want closed.

teen.open: Can a debt stay open forever? Paul says one should. You can pay off everything else, but you always owe people love, and you pay it in how you treat them.
teen.close: So yes, one debt stays open for good: love. You pay on it every day by doing no harm to the people around you, and by dressing in what Jesus already gave you.

senior.open: The title asks whether a debt can stay open forever. Romans 13 answers yes: every other debt is made to be closed, but the debt of love to one another is made to stay open and be paid daily in conduct.
senior.close: So the debt of love is the one account that never closes. It is paid in conduct, not sentiment, made more urgent by the hour, and carried in clothing the Lord Himself has already provided.

ll83-keep-thy-heart-the-conditions-of-gr.reason: The title's three questions (who guards, what you let in, how growth comes) are each answered, but scattered across a long verse-chain; the summary only arrives in two closing sentences.
ll83-keep-thy-heart-the-conditions-of-gr.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Your heart is the spring your whole life flows from (Proverbs 4:23). Who stands guard over it? The peace of Yahweh does, posted like a garrison through Christ Jesus (Philippians 4:7); your part is the gates. What do you let in? Only what passes the Philippians 4:8 checkpoint at the eye and the ear. And how is growth earned? By meeting the conditions the Word states, before you open it and, most of all, by doing it after you close it.
ll83-keep-thy-heart-the-conditions-of-gr.example: ONE EVENING, TWO GATES. Say you sit down to read at night. Before you open the Book you ask Him to open your eyes (Psalm 119:18), and you have already decided what will not go before your eyes afterward (Psalm 101:3). You read one command. The next morning you do it, at work, in one conversation. That is the whole pattern in small: a guarded gate, a met condition, and a deed where the blessing lands (James 1:25).
ll83-keep-thy-heart-the-conditions-of-gr.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Who stands guard, what you let in, and how growth is earned now have plain answers. Yahweh's peace keeps your heart and mind through Christ Jesus, so you are not the garrison. You keep the gates, letting in only what is true, honest, just, pure, lovely and of good report, and you take every thought captive inside the walls. Growth comes on stated terms: hunger and a meek, praying heart before the reading, and doing after it. Guard the source, meet the conditions, and the life that flows out of the spring will grow.

teen.open: Your heart is like a spring, and what goes in comes out in your life. Yahweh's peace stands guard. Your job is the gates: what you watch and hear.
teen.close: So He guards your heart, you guard your eyes and ears, and you grow by actually doing what you read, not just reading it.

senior.open: The title names three questions. Yahweh's peace keeps the heart as a posted guard; you keep the gates of eye and ear by the Philippians 4:8 test; and growth comes on the conditions the Word sets before and after study.
senior.close: So the answer is a shared watch. He stations the sentry, you keep the gates, and growth is won by meeting His conditions, above all by doing the Word once the Book is closed.

ll84-blessed-and-highly-favored-before-d.reason: Opens by saying the slogan is wrong without saying what favour is; the plain definition (presence and assignment, not exemption) only arrives in the second-to-last section after a long roll of examples.
ll84-blessed-and-highly-favored-before-d.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Can you be favoured by Yahweh without an easy life? Yes. In the Word, favour is not comfort or exemption. It is being chosen before time for a purpose, with His presence carrying you through the trial that purpose requires, never around it. Joseph had favour inside the prison, Noah had it while the world laughed, and Mary had it all the way to the cross. Here is the whole record.
ll84-blessed-and-highly-favored-before-d.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Favour without the easy life is not a contradiction; it is the normal shape of favour in the Word. You were blessed in Christ before the foundation of the world (Ephesians 1:3-4), carried through hard seasons that are His love and not His absence (Hebrews 12:6), and crowned after time. Joseph, Noah and Mary each had favour in the cost, not instead of it. So if you are in the prison, the wait, or under the sword, do not conclude the favour lifted. Read your season with the right definition.

teen.open: Can you be favoured by Yahweh and still have a hard life? Yes. Joseph had His favour while he was in prison. Favour means He is with you, not that life is easy.
teen.close: So favour is not a free pass. It is Yahweh choosing you, staying with you through the hard part, and finishing your story well.

senior.open: The title asks whether favour can come without the easy life. The Word answers yes: favour is presence and assignment, given before time began, and it carries its people through trial rather than around it.
senior.close: So favour and hardship are not opposites. Joseph, Noah and Mary each carried favour through cost, and the latter end of every such season belongs to Yahweh.

ll85-the-kings-code-sheep-hear-goats-of-.reason: Who counts as His sheep (those who agree with Him and keep His commandments) and why they hear (His law written on their hearts) are both answered, but only after the code, the test, and the GOAT warning; ends on a this-week task.
ll85-the-kings-code-sheep-hear-goats-of-.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Who does Yahweh count as His sheep, and how do they hear His voice? Not the most gifted, but those who agree with Him, shown by keeping His commandments (1 John 2:3-4). They hear because He has written His law on their hearts (Jeremiah 31:33), and they know His voice from walking with Him. Being the greatest of all time in the world is not enough. Here is how the Word draws the line.
ll85-the-kings-code-sheep-hear-goats-of-.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Who are His sheep, and how do they hear? His sheep are the ones who agree with Him, and the if/then of 1 John 2:3-4 shows it: they keep His commandments. They hear His voice because His law is written inside them and because they have walked with that voice long enough to flee a stranger's (John 10:5, 27). That is why greatness in the world cannot save anyone: He disputes the relationship, not the resume. The relief is that you do not need to be the best. You need to be His, and to do what He says.

teen.open: Who are Yahweh's sheep? Not the most talented people. His sheep agree with Him and do what He says, and they know His voice because He wrote His law on their hearts.
teen.close: So you do not have to be the greatest at anything. You have to be His. His sheep hear Him and show it by doing what He says.

senior.open: The title asks who Yahweh counts as His sheep and how they hear. The answer is agreement, not achievement: His sheep keep His commandments, and they hear because His law is written in their hearts.
senior.close: So gifts and greatness decide nothing at the separation. His sheep are known by agreement shown in obedience, and they hear because He wrote the code on them and they have walked with His voice.

ll87-two-ways-two-wisdoms-how-the-word-m.reason: The three blinders and how sight comes are answered in movements two and three, but the lesson opens on two ways and ends on the four soils with 'Part 2 walks the soils', not on why people cannot see.
ll87-two-ways-two-wisdoms-how-the-word-m.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Why can't some people see the Way? The Word names three blinders. One is hostile: the mind is blinded so the gospel's light will not shine in (2 Corinthians 4:4). One is moral: people love darkness because their deeds are evil (John 3:19-20). One is built in: the natural man cannot receive what is spiritually discerned (1 Corinthians 2:14). Sight comes by new birth, a clean heart, asking, and the Word itself, which enlightens the eyes.
ll87-two-ways-two-wisdoms-how-the-word-m.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Why can't some people see the Way? Because of three different blinders: a hostile blinding of the mind, a love of darkness that no explanation fixes, and a natural mind that cannot discern spiritual things. None of them is cured by trying harder to see. Sight begins with new birth, comes to the pure in heart, is asked for over the open Book, and grows while you seek first His kingdom. And the Word is the light itself: its commandment is "pure, enlightening the eyes" (Psalms 19:8). Stay in it as a doer, and the Way comes into focus as you walk it.

teen.open: Why can't some people see the Way? The Bible names three reasons: their minds are blinded, they love the dark, or they are trying to understand spiritual things without the Spirit.
teen.close: So seeing the Way does not come from being smart. It comes from being born again, asking Him to open your eyes, and living in His Word, which turns on the light.

senior.open: The title asks why some cannot see the Way. The Word names three distinct blinders: a hostile blinding of the mind, a moral love of darkness, and the natural man's inability to discern spiritual things.
senior.close: So blindness has three causes, and none yields to effort alone. Sight is given through new birth, a clean heart, and the Word itself, which converts the soul and enlightens the eyes of those who keep doing it.

ll86-luke-research-meets-inspiration-son.reason: The reason Luke shows his homework (so the reader may know the certainty; faith on tested testimony) is given in the first section, but the ending moves to the Nazareth reflex and never returns to the research question.
ll86-luke-research-meets-inspiration-son.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Why would a Gospel show its homework? So that you can know the certainty of what you were taught. Luke weighed earlier accounts, traced the eyewitness chain, and wrote in order, and he says why: certainty (Luke 1:1-4). Faith here is not a leap past evidence. It stands on tested testimony, and the Book is not embarrassed by research or by inspiration.
ll86-luke-research-meets-inspiration-son.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Why did Luke show his homework? So that Theophilus, and you, "mightest know the certainty of those things" you were taught. He named his sources, his witnesses and his method, and the Holy Spirit carried that research into the Word. What the research makes certain is the very thing Nazareth could not bear: a Son of man who came to seek and to save the lost, with a mercy meant for all people. Stand on that verified testimony, and let the certainty it gives you reach the outsider too.

teen.open: Why would a Gospel show its homework? Luke tells us: so we can be sure. He checked the eyewitnesses and wrote it all in order, so your faith stands on real testimony.
teen.close: So Luke did the research so you could be certain. And what he made certain is that Jesus came to find the lost, including the people others leave out.

senior.open: The title asks why a Gospel would show its research. Luke answers in his opening sentence: so that his reader might know the certainty of what he had been taught, resting on witnesses traced from the beginning.
senior.close: So Luke's method serves his purpose: certainty grounded in tested testimony. And that certainty holds the Son of man who seeks the lost, with grace extended to all people.

ll89-the-most-hated-verse-wilful-sin-the.reason: Opening says the Holy Spirit uses the verse not to condemn but to bring you to the truth; ending gives the two-question test ('run TO the sacrifice, or FROM the verse') and lands 'Hide under it' with 1 John 1:9.

ll91-the-authors-own-code-searched-out-t.reason: Asks whose molecule was repurposed in the first paragraph and answers in section ONE (Yahweh authored DNA and you); the closing 'THE WHOLE OF IT' opens 'The code is His and so are you'.

ll92-yahweh-standardized-love-obedience-.reason: First paragraph answers plainly (love is not a mood but a standard bound to obedience, John 14:15); section NINE ties thoughts and the temple together and ends 'Love Him, and you will obey Him.'

ll88-four-soils-heart-conditions-and-the.reason: Asks and answers the title question in the first paragraph (not the seed or the Sower but the soil), but ends on a recap of Part 1 (two ways, blinders, the engine) instead of the soil answer.
ll88-four-soils-heart-conditions-and-the.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Why does the same Word grow in one heart and die in another? Not because the seed differs or the Sower fails, but because the ground does. The hardened heart lets it be taken before it gets in. The shallow heart receives it with joy but has no root. The divided heart grows it alongside cares, riches and pleasures until it brings no fruit to perfection. The good ground is an honest heart that keeps the Word and bears fruit with patience. And soil can change: break up your fallow ground, for it is time to seek the LORD (Hosea 10:12).

teen.close: So the same Word grows or dies because of the heart it lands in: hard, shallow, crowded, or honest. And Yahweh can change your soil. Ask Him, and keep what you hear.

senior.close: So the difference is never the seed but the soil: hardened, shallow, divided, or honest and good. And because Yahweh gives a new heart, no ground is fixed in its category for good.

ll93-come-let-us-reason-truth-in-any-lan.reason: Opens on Yahweh's invitation to reason (Isaiah 1:18) and answers the language question in section ONE (the meaning did not change); 'THE WHOLE OF IT' lands both halves of the title.

ll95-know-the-state-of-thy-flocks-best-b.reason: Opens on the Best Buy report; the title's answer (read your flock and the times like Issachar, but never set your heart on the rally) is spread over sections TWO and SIX and only gathered in a closing list.
ll95-know-the-state-of-thy-flocks-best-b.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Your business reads the crowd. Does your faith read the times? It should, and the Word shows how. Be diligent to know the state of your flock (Proverbs 27:23), like the sons of Issachar who understood the times and knew what to do (1 Chronicles 12:32). That means knowing what your people actually need right now. But reading the times is not chasing the crowd's hype. Here is the shepherd's eye, from a retail headline to the Word.
ll95-know-the-state-of-thy-flocks-best-b.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Does your faith read the times? A shepherd's faith does. It knows the state of the flock, meets people where they are, stays present, and works diligently as to the Lord, through hard seasons that work patience, experience and hope. But it reads the times without being ruled by them. The crowd that bid the stock up on hype sold it on results, and riches fly away like an eagle. So read your people closely, serve them where they are, and build on Yahweh, because except the LORD build the house, the labour is in vain (Psalms 127:1).

teen.open: A good business pays attention to what people need. Your faith should too: know your people and the times, like the sons of Issachar did, without chasing the hype.
teen.close: So yes, read the times. Know what the people around you need and serve them. Just do not build your heart on the crowd. Build on Yahweh.

senior.open: The title asks whether faith reads the times as a good business reads its customers. The Word says it should: know the state of your flocks, as the sons of Issachar understood their times, while never chasing the crowd's rally.
senior.close: So faith reads the times as a shepherd reads a flock: closely, patiently, and for the sake of those it serves. But it builds on Yahweh, not on the rally, because every good season is His.

ll94-lord-of-hosts-the-two-ways-sealed-i.reason: First paragraph answers the name question plainly (LORD of HOSTS, plural, commander of them all); 'THE WHOLE OF IT' opens on that name and ends 'Now, while it is still time, choose His way', with study as eating.

ll96-doers-of-the-word-competence-by-doi.reason: THE THESIS opens with the answer (competence in the Word comes by doing, not hearing or reading); the close 'Hearing informs; doing FORMS... the doer is blessed in his deed' lands it.

ll90-no-respecter-of-persons-the-image-t.reason: The plain answer (yes: Yahweh does not exempt an injustice because it followed procedure, Isaiah 10:1-2) only arrives in section THREE after framing; ends on a long summary list and Micah 6:8, not the title's question.
ll90-no-respecter-of-persons-the-image-t.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Can a vote be unjust if the law says it is legal? Yes. Yahweh pronounced woe on lawmakers who write unrighteous decrees that turn aside the needy from judgment (Isaiah 10:1-2). He does not excuse an injustice because it followed proper procedure. His standard sits above every statute: every person bears His image, and partiality in either direction is sin. Here is how the Word weighs it.
ll90-no-respecter-of-persons-the-image-t.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Can a vote be unjust when the law calls it legal? The Word answers yes. A decree that turns aside the needy stands under Isaiah's woe, whoever writes it, and moving a people's boundary to bury their voice is the heart Yahweh cursed at the ancient landmark. So measure every law by His standard, not the reverse: honour the image in every voter, refuse partiality on every side, speak documented harm plainly and unverified claims honestly, and plead for the voiceless by righteous means. Then rest in this: the Judge of all the earth will do right (Genesis 18:25).

teen.open: Can something be unfair even if it is legal? Yes. Yahweh warned lawmakers who wrote unfair laws to push the poor aside. Legal is not the same as just.
teen.close: So a law or a vote can be legal and still wrong. Yahweh's standard is higher than any law: every person bears His image, and no one gets favored. Stand for that, the right way.

senior.open: The title asks whether a vote can be unjust when the law permits it. Scripture answers that it can: Isaiah pronounced woe on those who decree unrighteous decrees, and Yahweh does not excuse injustice for following procedure.
senior.close: So legality is not the final measure. Every decree answers to Yahweh's standard of the image and of impartial judgment, and the believer works for just laws and changed hearts, trusting the Judge of all the earth to do right.

ll97-a-just-weight-for-work-money-and-wo.reason: Opens on the Blue Angels contract story; the one principle that answers the title (a single just weight applied to work, money, words, and every person) is spread over seven sections and only gathered in a closing list.
ll97-a-just-weight-for-work-money-and-wo.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. How do you weigh fairness in work, money, and words? With one just weight, used the same way everywhere. Honour faithful work. Ask for an honest account of money that is not yours. Check every claim before you repeat it, including your own. And judge every person by one standard without convicting a heart only Yahweh can see. Here is how one reported story tests all four.
ll97-a-just-weight-for-work-money-and-wo.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. How do you weigh fairness in work, money, and words? With the same honest weight for all three, because divers weights are alike abomination to the LORD (Proverbs 20:10). Forty-three years of faithful work deserve honour. Doubled public cost deserves an accounting, not a verdict. Every claim deserves checking, as the Congressman correction showed when the correction itself was wrong. And the scale may not be shaded toward the mighty or toward the sympathetic (Leviticus 19:15). Ask for a just process, not vengeance, and rest your security on the Lord, not on a contract.

teen.open: How do you know what is fair with work, money, and words? Use one honest measure for all of them, and for every person, no matter who they are.
teen.close: So fairness means the same honest scale everywhere: honor good work, ask honest questions about money, check what you hear before you say it, and treat everyone by one standard.

senior.open: The title asks how fairness is weighed in work, money, and words. The Word's answer is one just weight: the same honest measure for service, for stewardship, for speech, and for every person alike.
senior.close: So fairness is a single scale held steady: faithful service honoured, public money accounted for, every claim verified, and no thumb on the balance for the mighty or the sympathetic. The outcome is committed to the Lord.

ll99-watch-and-be-ready-no-date-setting-.reason: First paragraph and section ONE answer plainly (no chart, headline or A.I. milestone names the day; stay ready instead); 'THE WHOLE OF IT' opens 'prophecy is for readiness rather than prediction'.

ll98-the-just-judge-equal-justice-and-a-.reason: The verdict on the 26-year case (a real, grievous disparity that is sin, named without inflating the multiple) only comes in sections THREE and FOUR; the close is a summary list that never says plainly whether it was fair.
ll98-the-just-judge-equal-justice-and-a-.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Is a 26-year sentence fair when another man got time served for the same crime, before the same judge, on the same points? No. Where that partiality is real, Yahweh's Word calls it sin and we do not soften it (Proverbs 24:23). But the same Word requires a just weight for the numbers too. You name the real wrong at its true size, without inflating it. Here is how both happen at once.
ll98-the-just-judge-equal-justice-and-a-.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Was the 26-year sentence fair? Measured against the Judge of all the earth, no. Two men with the same plea, the same prior and the same points received 26 years and time served, and that is a grievous disparity. The documented national pattern is real too: roughly 13 to 20 percent longer for the same offence. Say it at that true measure, with the prosecutor's stated context included, and the wrong is harder to dismiss, not easier. Then plead the cause without vengeance, and rest it before the court where Yahweh judges the judges.

teen.open: Is it fair for one man to get 26 years and another time served for the same crime? No. Yahweh hates unequal justice. But we also tell the truth about the numbers.
teen.close: So that sentence was not fair, and Yahweh calls that kind of partiality sin. Say so honestly, with the real numbers, and trust Him as the final Judge.

senior.open: The title asks whether such a sentence is fair. By Yahweh's standard it is not: real partiality in judgment is sin. Yet the same standard requires an honest weight on every number used to describe it.
senior.close: So the disparity is named plainly as the sin it is, and measured truly rather than inflated. That honesty strengthens the plea for equal justice, which finally rests with the Judge who judges every court.

ll100-guard-the-little-ones-children-the.reason: The answer to who sets the hook (whatever is built to hook a child for profit, and also the careless things we set before them) is a single line in section TWO; the lesson opens on the settlement and ends on the general duty.
ll100-guard-the-little-ones-children-the.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Who is really setting the hook for your child? Anything built to hook a child's attention for profit, and Jesus put that under His millstone warning (Matthew 18:6). But the uncomfortable half is that the careless things we ourselves set before them stand under it too. So the guard cannot be a company's default setting. It is you, teaching diligently, and it is the child learning to be mastered by nothing.
ll100-guard-the-little-ones-children-the.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Who is setting the hook for your child? The lesson answers both ways. Systems built to hold a child for profit stand under the millstone warning, and so does whatever careless thing we put in front of them. That is why the answer cannot stop at blaming a platform. Time limits and hidden counts are useful outward walls, but no settlement raises a child. You guard the eye and the heart, teach them the Word as you sit, walk, lie down and rise, and help them grow the inward wall that travels with them: being mastered by nothing.

teen.open: Who is setting the hook? Apps built to keep you scrolling for profit, and sometimes the stuff people around you hand you. Jesus takes harm to kids very seriously.
teen.close: So the hook can come from an app or from careless choices close to home. The best guard is one you carry inside: let nothing be your master, and live for Yahweh's approval, not likes.

senior.open: The title asks who is really setting the hook. Scripture's answer is broad and humbling: whatever is built to hook a child for profit stands under the millstone warning, and so does anything careless we ourselves place before them.
senior.close: So the hook has more than one hand behind it, and the guard must be nearer than any platform. Parents and elders teach diligently, guard the eye and the heart, and help each child become mastered by nothing.

ll101-the-real-champion-action-not-theor.reason: First paragraph answers it (Jesus REALLY DID IT, in ACTIONS, not theory; die once, live forever); 'THE WHOLE OF IT' lands action over theory, the resurrection, and His mind handed to us.

ll102-bold-as-a-lion-boldness-from-right.reason: First paragraph gives the answer from Proverbs 28:1 (guilt manufactures its own pursuers; the righteous stand on a settled account); the close opens 'Guilt flees; righteousness stands' and ends 'Never sourced in self.'

ll103-his-kings-reigning-under-the-king-.reason: Opens 'the whole question is WHOSE' and answers in ONE (HIS kings, made, never self-made); the close lands it: 'Kingship is received from Him and held in worship, never self-crowned.'

ll104-study-your-ways-how-yahweh-weighs-.reason: First paragraph answers it (love Yahweh by what you do; verbalising matters but is not the measure); the final line lands it: 'not your verbalising and not your feeling. It is your WAY, weighed by His Word.'

ll105-doing-the-word-rewires-you-daily-i.reason: Opens with a list of four questions; the title's answer (daily reading is not doing; only the doer is built on rock, and doing reshapes you) only arrives in section FOUR, though the close lands 'meditate AND do'.
ll105-doing-the-word-rewires-you-daily-i.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. You read it every day, but are you doing it? That is the real question, because reading is not doing. Both men in Jesus' parable heard His sayings; only the one who did them built on rock (Matthew 7:24-26). Daily, attentive intake hides the Word in your heart and renews your mind. Doing it is what turns that intake into a person reshaped, with a knowing that reading alone cannot give.
ll105-doing-the-word-rewires-you-daily-i.example: ONE VERSE, TWO MORNINGS. Say you read "Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly" on Monday and nod. On Tuesday you read it again, and this time, before a hard conversation, you stop and speak the way that verse asks. The first morning added a fact you know about the verse. The second added a step you have walked. Repeat that step for months, and what took effort starts to run as second nature: senses exercised by use (Hebrews 5:14).
ll105-doing-the-word-rewires-you-daily-i.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Are you doing what you read every day? The lesson's answer is that the doing is the point. Daily, attentive reading hides the Word in the deep heart, and the Word works in you, alive. But only the doer is blessed in his deed, and only the doer builds on rock. Doing is also how you come to know it, the way the psalmist understood more than the ancients because he kept the precepts (Psalms 119:100). So meditate in order to do, as Joshua 1:8 orders it, and keep doing it until it is second nature.

teen.open: Reading the Bible every day is good. But are you doing what it says? That is what actually changes you. Hearing is not the same as building on rock.
teen.close: So keep reading daily, and then do one thing it says. The doing is what turns it into who you are, until it becomes second nature.

senior.open: The title asks whether daily reading has become daily doing. Scripture separates the two plainly: both builders heard, but only the doer built on rock. Attention takes the Word in; obedience is what reshapes the person.
senior.close: So the measure of a daily habit is not the reading but the doing. Meditate in order to observe to do, and the practice, kept over time, becomes the settled character Yahweh is building.

ll106-wise-as-serpents-harmless-as-doves.reason: Section ONE hints at it (one half alone makes 'a cynic or a mark'), but the how (know his exposed ways, starve the flesh he works, let the Word divide soul from spirit, only His will) is scattered; ends on a list.
ll106-wise-as-serpents-harmless-as-doves.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. How do you stay shrewd without becoming the target? You keep both halves together: wise unto good, simple concerning evil (Romans 16:19). You learn the enemy's ways from what Yahweh has already exposed, not by tasting them. And you deny the flesh, which is the ground he works, so he has nothing to work with. The Word then shows you which pull is which. Here is how each piece fits.
ll106-wise-as-serpents-harmless-as-doves.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. How do you stay shrewd without becoming the target? Not by being cleverer than the enemy, but by holding Jesus' two halves together. Know the devices Yahweh has already exposed, and never mistake the roaring counterfeit for the Lion who prevailed. Submit to Him first, then resist. Starve the flesh, because that is the ground the serpent works. Let the Word divide soul from spirit so you can tell his pull from the Spirit's leading. And lean on Him, not your own cleverness. The shrewd and harmless walk one directed way, and there is little left in them for the enemy to grab.

teen.open: How do you stay smart about evil without getting hooked by it? Jesus says be wise as serpents and harmless as doves. You need both, not just one.
teen.close: So stay sharp about the enemy's tricks, stay clean in your own heart, and follow Yahweh's one way. When you starve the flesh, the enemy has nothing to grab.

senior.open: The title asks how shrewdness avoids becoming a vulnerability. Scripture's answer is the pairing itself: wise unto good and simple concerning evil, with the flesh denied so the enemy finds no ground.
senior.close: So the safeguard is not cleverness but surrender. Know his exposed devices, deny the flesh he works through, let the Word discern soul from spirit, and walk the one way Yahweh directs.

ll108-why-we-name-him-low-the-typography.reason: First paragraph answers (conviction, not quirk) and the case follows; 'THE WHOLE OF IT' restates every reason and ends 'The honour is Yahweh's... His alone.' Note: title says four reasons, the lesson gives five.

ll107-what-the-word-gives-love-truth-lig.reason: The title asks what would happen if you received the Word as He intends; the lesson lists gifts and the one way to receive them across eight sections but never gathers the 'what would happen' plainly; ends on the two strategies.
ll107-what-the-word-gives-love-truth-lig.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. What would happen if you received Yahweh's Word the way He intends? Your mind would have a filter: you would think on what is true, honest, just, pure and lovely, and be kept in perfect peace (Isaiah 26:3). Your life would bear fruit: love, joy, peace and the rest, an abundant life the thief cannot steal. And you would be fed Love, Truth, Light, Knowledge and Understanding. All of it comes one way: received humbly, taught by the Spirit, asked for in faith, and done.
ll107-what-the-word-gives-love-truth-lig.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. What happens when you receive the Word the way Yahweh intends? The filter sets your thoughts on things true and lovely, and your mind, stayed on Him, is kept in peace. The fruit grows: love, joy, peace, longsuffering, and joy that is full. The feeding line runs straight from His mouth: Love that is shed abroad in your heart, Truth that makes you free, Light that enters with His words, and wisdom given liberally without reproach. And you can tell the two strategies apart: the enemy steals, lies and blinds, while Yahweh gives, frees and orders. Receive it meekly, ask in faith, do it, and overcome.

teen.open: What if you took in Yahweh's Word the way He means it? Your thoughts would get a filter, your life would grow real fruit like joy and peace, and you would be fed truth and light.
teen.close: So receiving the Word His way changes what you think, what you feel, and what you know. Take it in humbly, ask Him for help, and do what it says.

senior.open: The title asks what receiving the Word as Yahweh intends would produce. The lesson answers in three parts: a filter for thought, the fruit of the Spirit in experience, and a steady supply of Love, Truth, Light, Knowledge and Understanding.
senior.close: So the Word received rightly orders the mind, bears fruit in the life, and supplies what only Yahweh gives. The posture is one: meekness, the Spirit's teaching, faith in asking, and obedience in doing.

ll109-how-we-know-yahwehs-love-taste-see.reason: First paragraph answers yes (His Love is given to be EXPERIENCED through every sense, at every age); the close lands taste, see, hear, feel. Note: title says five senses, the lesson teaches four (touch and feel together).

ll110-wolf-vs-lion-the-enemys-two-tactic.reason: First paragraph answers 'both' and why (stealth within, intimidation without, each needing a different counter); 'THE WHOLE OF IT' lands both tactics and the one Shepherd.

ll111-the-just-weight-yahwehs-unchanging.reason: Opens on inflation news; the plain answer (trust Yahweh's just weight, fixed because He changes not, Malachi 3:6) is only stated at the hinge of sections TWO and THREE, though the close lands it.
ll111-the-just-weight-yahwehs-unchanging.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. When the scale keeps sliding, what measure can you trust? Only one that does not move, and only Yahweh's does not move, because He does not change (Malachi 3:6). He commands one just weight, the same for buying and selling, for the poor and the mighty. Build your money, your mercy and your daily choices on that measure, not on a standard that shifts to flatter whoever holds it.
ll111-the-just-weight-yahwehs-unchanging.example: ONE BAG, ONE WEIGHT. Say you sell eggs at a market and keep two weights in your bag. With your neighbour you use the heavy one when you buy and the light one when you sell. Each trade looks small. Over a year it adds up, and you have built on a moving measure (Deuteronomy 25:13). Now throw the second weight out. Every trade uses the same stone, whoever is across the table. That is the just weight Yahweh delights in, and the promise on it is lengthened days (Deuteronomy 25:15).
ll111-the-just-weight-yahwehs-unchanging.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. When the scale keeps sliding, the measure you can trust is the one signed "I am the LORD your God", because the One behind it does not change. The world moves its goalposts and calls it progress; Scripture calls a moving measure an abomination. So keep one just weight yourself, whoever is on the scale. Lay up treasure that moth, rust and inflation cannot reach. Live content with a Provider who has said He will never leave you. Stay faithful in the least. And when real mercy comes, bless the Healer who gave it.

teen.open: When the rules keep changing, what can you trust? Yahweh's measure, because He never changes. He wants one honest standard, the same for everyone.
teen.close: So when the world's standards slide, hold on to Yahweh's. Be honest the same way every time, trust Him to provide, and thank Him for the good things He gives.

senior.open: The title asks what measure can be trusted when the scale keeps sliding. Scripture answers with Yahweh's just weight, fixed because He Himself does not change, and applied the same to every person.
senior.close: So the trustworthy measure is the unchanging One's. Keep it in your own dealings, store treasure where nothing erodes it, rest content in His provision, and give thanks to Him for every real mercy.

ll112-foxes-wolves-and-bears-the-enemys-.reason: Section ONE answers right after the question (He teaches through what He made; each creature names a tactic and a size; you cannot fight what you cannot name); the close lands both the why and the giant.

ll114-what-makes-having-you-better-coven.reason: The answer (provision is real and commanded, but a husband brings himself: love, care, knowledge, honour, a safe temper, service, presence) is spread over eleven sections; the 'alone' answer only comes in ELEVEN.
ll114-what-makes-having-you-better-coven.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. What does a husband really bring? Provision is real, commanded and honourable (1 Timothy 5:8), but it is one command on a longer list. Yahweh made the wife because it was not good for the man to be alone (Genesis 2:18), so a husband's value is measured where aloneness is answered. He brings himself: love that gives itself, care like his own body, knowledge of her, honour, a safe temper, and service. A marriage is a covenant, not a contract.
ll114-what-makes-having-you-better-coven.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. What does a husband really bring? A paycheck, yes, and the Word honours the man who carries it. But a paycheck can be outsourced, and a husband cannot. He brings a covenant presence: love at the cross-standard, nourishing and cherishing care, a knowledge of her and the children that only attention builds, honour as a joint heir, a temper that is safe to live with, and hands that a towel would not embarrass. Two are better than one, and with Yahweh as the third cord they are not quickly broken. That is what makes having him better.

teen.open: What does a good husband bring? Money matters, and the Bible says providing is important. But Yahweh made marriage so nobody is alone, so a husband mostly brings himself.
teen.close: So a husband brings more than money: love, care, attention, respect, a kind temper, and help with the work. That is a covenant, not a deal.

senior.open: The title asks what a husband truly brings. The Word honours provision as commanded and costly, yet measures the marriage as a covenant, where his value lies in answering her aloneness with his whole self.
senior.close: So the account is never settled by the paycheck alone. A husband brings provision and presence together: self-giving love, care, knowledge, honour, a governed temper, and humble service, with Yahweh as the third cord.

ll113-the-spirit-is-willing-but-the-fles.reason: How to tell flesh from spirit (fruit, aim, leadership) arrives in section FOUR and the wall in FIVE; who keeps it standing (you rule your spirit, but by His Spirit's work) is only gathered in the long final paragraph.
ll113-the-spirit-is-willing-but-the-fles.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. How do you tell tired flesh from a willing spirit? Not by which one feels spiritual, but by three tests: what it grows (fruit), where the mind is aimed, and who is leading (Galatians 5:22; Romans 8:5, 14). Tired flesh is real, so tend it. And who keeps the wall standing? You are called to rule your own spirit (Proverbs 25:28), but the strength comes from His Spirit, and He finishes the work.
ll113-the-spirit-is-willing-but-the-fles.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. How do you tell them apart, and who keeps the wall standing? Tell them apart by fruit rather than feeling: flesh grows strife and wrath; the Spirit grows love, joy, peace and temperance. Check where your mind is aimed and who is leading. When the flesh is simply tired, tend it, the way Heaven fed Elijah first. Then guard the wall: watch and pray, cut the supply line, refuse the evil report, and rule your spirit. But you are not holding it up alone. Not by might, nor by power, but by His Spirit (Zechariah 4:6), and He who began the work will perform it.

teen.open: How do you tell if you are just tired or actually giving in? Look at what it grows, where your mind is pointed, and who is leading you. Your body matters, but it does not get to rule.
teen.close: So rest when you are tired, and check the fruit when you are tempted. You guard your heart, but Yahweh's Spirit gives the strength and keeps building you.

senior.open: The title asks how to distinguish weary flesh from a willing spirit, and who keeps the wall. Scripture's tests are fruit, aim and leadership; the wall is yours to rule, yet held up by His Spirit.
senior.close: So the flesh is tended honestly but never obeyed as master, and the two are told apart by fruit, aim and leading. The wall stands by watching and praying, with His Spirit supplying the strength He promised.

ll115-meek-and-quiet-strength-the-orname.reason: Opens on a viral teaching and its comment thread; the plain answer (meek is not weak, quiet is not silent, deceit is not meekness) is spread over several sections; the ending lands it well.
ll115-meek-and-quiet-strength-the-orname.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Is meek and quiet weakness? No. Meek is strength with the reins in Yahweh's hand, not the absence of force: Moses was the meekest man on earth, and Jesus called Himself meek. Quiet is a settled soul, not a shut mouth. And the ornament Peter prices is guileless, so a soft voice laid over hidden deceit is not meekness at all. Here is how the Word shows it.
ll115-meek-and-quiet-strength-the-orname.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Is meek and quiet weakness? The Word says no, from Moses to the Lord Himself. Meekness is force that answers to Yahweh and hands the fight to the Judge instead of the argument (1 Peter 2:23). Quietness is a weaned soul that has stopped demanding. Neither is fear, neither is silence about harm, and neither hides a knife. That ornament is commanded to every believer, and Yahweh Himself prices it high.

teen.open: Does being meek and quiet mean being weak? No. Meek means strong, but under Yahweh's control. Quiet means a calm heart, not never speaking.
teen.close: So meek and quiet is not weakness. It is real strength that trusts Yahweh to judge, a settled heart, and an honest one with nothing hidden.

senior.open: The title asks whether a meek and quiet spirit is weakness. The Word answers no: meekness is strength governed by Yahweh, and quietness is a soul at rest, not a silenced one.
senior.close: So the answer stands plainly. A meek and quiet spirit is strength under His control, a settled and guileless heart, commanded to men and women alike and valued highly in His sight.

ll116-the-thirty-day-experiment-action-p.reason: Opens on the man's story; the answer (do first, then you will know, John 7:17) comes in section one and the results are scattered through later sections; ends on John 7:17 and grace.
ll116-the-thirty-day-experiment-action-p.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. What happens if you act before you believe? Jesus already answered it: do His will, and you will know (John 7:17). A man who did not believe prayed, gave thanks, read the Word and applied it for thirty days. The Word did its own work. He forgave a friend, an eight-year habit faded, trouble came, and he crossed from pretending to seeking with all his heart. Here is how the Word explains each step.
ll116-the-thirty-day-experiment-action-p.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. What if you act before you believe? You find out. The order Yahweh built is do, then know. The power was never in the man's sincerity; it was in a living Word that reads the heart and finishes its errand. So expect it to aim at a relationship first, expect resistance once you turn, and do not stop at day thirty. The Father runs to you while you are still a great way off (Luke 15:20).

teen.open: What if you start doing what the Word says before you are sure Yahweh is real? Jesus said you will find out (John 7:17). Doing comes first, knowing follows.
teen.close: So acting before you believe is how you find out. The Word is alive and does the work. Keep going past day thirty, and know the Father is already running toward you.

senior.open: The title asks what happens when someone acts on the Word before believing it. Jesus answers it in John 7:17: the one who will do His will shall know. Doing precedes knowing.
senior.close: So the question answers itself in the account. Acting before believing opens the door, because the Word is alive and works on the one who handles it, and the Father meets the seeker long before he arrives.

ll118-ninety-seven-percent-testing-a-vir.reason: Opens on method and the six claims; the plain answer (the number has no source, the research runs the opposite way, the Word's test is the fear of Yahweh) arrives mid-lesson; the closing section lands it.
ll118-ninety-seven-percent-testing-a-vir.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Is the viral ninety-seven percent number telling you the truth about women and marriage? No. It traces to no study at all, and the published research runs the other way: women who finish college marry more and divorce less. A few things in the clip are real, like later marriage, and they are stated plainly. But Yahweh's test for a wife was never a diploma or the lack of one. It is the fear of Yahweh (Proverbs 31:30).
ll118-ninety-seven-percent-testing-a-vir.example: THE NUMBER AGAINST THE RECORD. The clip says almost no college woman is fit to marry. The Pew Research Center, reporting Census data in 2023, found that among forty-year-olds, eighteen percent of women with a bachelor's degree or more had never married, against about a third of women with a high school diploma or less. The Bureau of Labor Statistics found about forty-one percent of those women's first marriages ended in divorce, against at least half without a degree. The arrow points backwards.
ll118-ninety-seven-percent-testing-a-vir.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Is the viral number telling you the truth? No. It is a rumour with a decimal point, testifying against millions of neighbours, and Yahweh calls a false weight an abomination (Proverbs 11:1). The true parts are stated plainly, the one open question is named, and the over-reach is corrected. Then the Word hands you the real test, for a woman with three degrees or none: look at the heart and the fruit over time (1 Samuel 16:7; Matthew 7:20).

teen.open: Is that viral number about college women and marriage true? No. Nobody can find where it came from, and real research points the other way.
teen.close: So do not trust a number just because it sounds sure. Ask who counted it. And remember Yahweh looks at the heart, not a diploma.

senior.open: The title asks whether a viral statistic about women and marriage tells the truth. It does not: the figure has no source, and the published research on marrying and staying married runs opposite to it.
senior.close: So the answer is plain. The number was never a measurement, and the Word's own test, the fear of Yahweh seen in fruit over time, works the same on every woman, with a degree or without one.

ll117-no-two-children-grow-up-in-the-sam.reason: Opens on the claim and confirms it in section two, but the full answer (research cannot pin causes, Yahweh authored each child, the Father is the same to every child) comes only near the end.
ll117-no-two-children-grow-up-in-the-sam.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Do children in the same house have different childhoods? Yes. The research confirms siblings differ, but admits it cannot pin down why. The Word has shown it since Cain and Abel, and names Yahweh as the One who formed each child on purpose. So a parent's job is to see each child, not to treat them all the same. And where every earthly parent varies, the Father does not.
ll117-no-two-children-grow-up-in-the-sam.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Same house, different childhood? Yes, and the Word said it first. The research admits the difference is real and the causes are not pinned. Yahweh shows it is His signature, since He does not make copies. So parents are called to see each child, refuse favouritism, and stop provoking. And every child is seen by a Father who is no respecter of persons, who ran to one son and walked out to the other on the same night with the same love (Luke 15:20, 28).

teen.open: Can brothers and sisters grow up in the same house and still have different childhoods? Yes. Yahweh made each of you different on purpose.
teen.close: So yes, your childhood was different from your sibling's. That is not a mistake. Yahweh sees each of you, and His love does not change from one child to another.

senior.open: The title asks whether children raised under one roof truly have different childhoods. They do. Research confirms it without being able to explain it, and the Word shows Yahweh forming each child individually.
senior.close: So the question finds its answer. No parent can be the same to every child, but the Father is, and He sees each one. That truth makes room for honest forgiveness and for brothers and sisters to stop keeping score.

ll119-abstention-if-i-am-an-option-do-no.reason: Opens on the spoken declaration and frames it as claims to test; the answer (people may weigh you, but Yahweh chose you before any list) builds across many sections and is gathered only in the final paragraph.
ll119-abstention-if-i-am-an-option-do-no.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Am I just an option to them? People may weigh you, rank you, or keep you in reserve. But that is not what settles your worth. Yahweh chose you before the foundation of the world, before there was any list to be on (Ephesians 1:4). Jesus Himself was refused by the builders and became the head of the corner. The Word also adds a correction: weigh a commitment fully before you make it, never after.
ll119-abstention-if-i-am-an-option-do-no.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Am I just an option to them? To some people, maybe. To Yahweh, never. Men disallowed Jesus, and Yahweh called Him chosen and precious (1 Peter 2:4). You were bought with His blood, not silver, so no one's ranking can reprice you. So refuse to be kept as a maybe after a covenant is made, but keep the door, the kindness and the long-suffering. Do not ask a person to settle a worth only Yahweh settles. He already has: called, chosen, faithful (Revelation 17:14).

teen.open: Ever feel like you are just one option on someone's list? Here is the truth: Yahweh chose you before there was any list at all.
teen.close: So you are not just an option. People may pass you over, like they did Jesus, but Yahweh already chose you. Stay kind, and let Him settle your worth.

senior.open: The title asks whether you are merely an option to others. Others may weigh you, but the Word places your worth elsewhere: Yahweh chose you before the foundation of the world, apart from any comparison.
senior.close: So the answer is settled where no ballot reaches. You may be weighed by people, as Jesus was, but you were chosen by Yahweh and bought with His blood. Keep kindness and patience, and let Him hold the verdict.

ll120-it-is-written-keep-the-policy-in-y.reason: Opens on the full library story; the answer to the title (a written standard is a weight and must pay out as it collects, Proverbs 11:1) only arrives in the third section; the final paragraph lands it.
ll120-it-is-written-keep-the-policy-in-y.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. What does Yahweh's standard say about fair weights? A written policy is a weight, and it must be applied the same way going out as coming in. The library took full value when the book was lost and promised full value back when it was found. Refusing the refund tipped the balance one way, and Yahweh calls a false balance an abomination but delights in a just weight (Proverbs 11:1).
ll120-it-is-written-keep-the-policy-in-y.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. What does Yahweh's standard say about fair weights? A standard must pay out exactly as it collects, and bending it against someone small is forbidden, since Yahweh pleads their cause Himself (Proverbs 22:23). So keep the written thing ready, appeal softly and privately from it, and honour the one who corrects it well. Then name the act and release the person, because the just weight is His delight and the victory is already His.

teen.open: Is it fair to charge someone for a lost book and then refuse the refund your own rules promise? No. Yahweh wants the same scale both ways.
teen.close: So a fair weight means a rule works the same both ways. Know what is written, speak up kindly, and do not judge the person's heart.

senior.open: The title asks what Yahweh's standard says about fair weights. A written rule is a weight, and His standard requires it to be applied the same way whether it collects or pays out.
senior.close: So the answer is plain. Yahweh delights in a just weight, defends the one with no leverage, and honours a correction rightly made and well received. The written standard, kept close and spoken gently, carries the day.

ll122-does-she-feel-like-your-favorite-p.reason: Opens on the mentor story; the three Word-based steps the title promises (remember, repent, do the first works from Revelation 2:5) only arrive in the middle; the ending gathers them well.
ll122-does-she-feel-like-your-favorite-p.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Does your spouse feel like your favorite person? Loving her is not the same as her being able to tell. The Word asks for love in deed and in truth, not only in word (1 John 3:18). When the warmth has quietly drained into running a house together, Yahweh gives three steps to close the gap: remember where you started, repent of the drift, and do the first works (Revelation 2:5).
ll122-does-she-feel-like-your-favorite-p.example: THE GOOD NEWS CALL. Say that in your first year you called her first with every piece of good news. Now the news goes to a coworker, and she hears it second, over dinner. Remember: you used to call her first. Repent: agree that this drift is a real loss, not just a busy season. Do the first works: this week, when something good happens, she is the first call. You do not wait to feel it first. The deed comes first, and the warmth follows.
ll122-does-she-feel-like-your-favorite-p.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Does your spouse feel like your favorite person? Ask it of yourself, never as a bill to her, and answer it with your hands. Prefer her in honour (Romans 12:10). Be her friend again. Protect her name when she is not in the room. Then take the three steps: remember, repent, do the first works, without waiting for the feelings. Keep the Lord first, so this love has a source that does not run dry, and home becomes the place you cannot wait to reach.

teen.open: It is one thing to love someone and another for them to feel it. Here are three steps from the Word for closing that gap: remember, repent, and do the first works.
teen.close: So love has to show up in what you do. Remember what you used to do, turn back, and start doing it again, even before the feeling returns.

senior.open: The title asks whether your spouse feels like your favorite person. The Word calls for love shown in deed and in truth, and gives three steps when it has cooled: remember, repent, and do the first works.
senior.close: So the gap between love said and love felt closes by doing. Prefer your spouse in honour, be a friend again, and keep the Lord first, so the love has a source that does not run dry.

ll124-equipped-to-win-the-hour-you-are-l.reason: States early that the losing hour is when to know you are equipped, but why Yahweh's love came first only arrives two-thirds in (Jeremiah 31:3), and who you are is stated near the end.
ll124-equipped-to-win-the-hour-you-are-l.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Are you losing right now? Then this is the hour you most need to remember who you are, because a man who forgets who he is in the middle of a loss stays lost after it. You are a royal priesthood, equipped now, not later (1 Peter 2:9). And Yahweh's love came first: He loved you with an everlasting love before you were formed (Jeremiah 31:3). So your failure cannot cancel it.
ll124-equipped-to-win-the-hour-you-are-l.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Losing right now? This is the hour to remember who you are. The loss is real, but it is a stage, not a verdict, and Yahweh's word to ruins is "Again I will build thee" (Jeremiah 31:4). His love was in place before you were formed, so your record never earned it and cannot cancel it. Your equipment is issued, not made by you. Put down offence and pride, leave the leaking cisterns, and having done all, stand.

teen.open: Losing right now? That is exactly when you need to remember who you are. Yahweh loved you before you were even born, so a loss cannot cancel that.
teen.close: So in the middle of losing, remember: Yahweh's love came first, He builds again, and He has already equipped you. Drop the grudges and pride, and stand.

senior.open: The title speaks to the hour of loss. The Word says that is the very hour to remember who you are, because Yahweh's everlasting love predates your failure and your equipment is His gift.
senior.close: So the answer holds even mid-struggle. His love came before your record, so it cannot be undone by it. He promises to build again, He issues the equipment, and your part is to lay down offence and pride and stand.

ll123-would-you-sign-that-contract-the-a.reason: Opens on a long account of the debate; the answer (as a contract no, which is why Yahweh made a covenant; the manner forfeited the argument) comes in pieces across the lesson and is only gathered at the end.
ll123-would-you-sign-that-contract-the-a.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Would you sign a contract built to reward its own breaking? As a bargain for expected return, no sensible person would. That is exactly why Yahweh never made marriage a contract. He made a covenant, knowingly, with a people He had already said would break it (Deuteronomy 31:16). And a vow kept only while it is safe was never a vow. The angry debate in this clip cost both men the argument.
ll123-would-you-sign-that-contract-the-a.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Would you sign a contract built to reward its own breaking? As a contract, no, and the question is fair. But marriage is a covenant, and Yahweh Himself entered one with a party He knew would break it. Caesar keeps the paper; Yahweh holds the covenant (Matthew 22:21). The covenant-keeper swears to his own hurt and changes not (Psalm 15:4). And whoever answers it, answer with charity, because a right position shouted in contempt is only noise (1 Corinthians 13:1).

teen.open: Would you agree to a deal the other side gets paid to break? As a deal, probably not. But Yahweh made marriage a covenant, not a deal.
teen.close: So marriage is not a bet on whether the other person keeps their side. It is a promise you keep, like Yahweh keeps His. And arguing with insults wins nobody over.

senior.open: The title asks whether anyone would sign a contract that rewards its own breaking. As a contract, no. That is why the Word frames marriage as covenant, which Yahweh Himself entered knowing it would be broken.
senior.close: So the question has its answer. Civil terms may be unfavourable, but a covenant does not rest on the other party's incentives. And even a sound answer is lost when it is delivered in anger and contempt.

ll121-know-your-own-post-her-provision-h.reason: Confirms early that a woman has a real post, but the core answer to the title (the beam comes out first; prove your own work and learn your own post) only arrives in the last third.
ll121-know-your-own-post-her-provision-h.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Can you be an expert in everyone else's job and blind to your own? Yes, and the Word calls it the beam in your own eye (Matthew 7:3-5). The clip is right that a woman has a real post from Yahweh: real provision and a real guard over her house. It is wrong to call any person worthless. And it falls into the very fault it names. The answer for everyone is to prove your own work.
ll121-know-your-own-post-her-provision-h.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Expert in everyone else's job, blind to your own? The Word's answer is an order of operations: first cast out the beam, then you can see clearly to help with the mote. A woman's post is real, with provision and a watch over her house. She is made in Yahweh's image and never worthless. So stop reciting the other person's duties. Prove your own work (Galatians 6:4), keep the floor of justice, mercy and humility, and let your fruit speak.

teen.open: Ever know exactly what everyone else should do, but not your own part? Jesus called that a beam in your own eye. Fix your part first.
teen.close: So learn your own job before grading someone else's. Do your own work well, speak with respect, and let what you do speak for you.

senior.open: The title asks about knowing others' duties while neglecting your own. The Word names it the beam in one's own eye, and it affirms that a woman has a real post of provision and guarding.
senior.close: So the answer is to tend your own post first. Remove the beam, refuse contempt for anyone made in Yahweh's image, and prove your own work, letting faithful fruit make the case words could not.

ll125-rules-of-engagement-the-warfare-th.reason: The who-fights and who-closes-the-door answers are scattered across many sections (James 4:7, Acts 19, Ephesians 4:27, Deuteronomy 29:29); the ending is a list of rules plus a confession, not a gathered answer.
ll125-rules-of-engagement-the-warfare-th.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Who gets to fight spiritual battles? The believer who is submitted to Yahweh first and sent by Him, fighting with weapons that are not carnal (James 4:7; 2 Corinthians 10:4). Borrowed authority fails, as Acts 19 shows. Who closes the door? You do. An open door is place you gave (Ephesians 4:27), and it closes through forgiveness, confession and a cleaned house. The Word forbids railing and inherited guilt, and leaves the enemy's org chart alone.
ll125-rules-of-engagement-the-warfare-th.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Who gets to fight, and who closes the door? The one who submits before resisting, is sent rather than self-appointed, and goes with counsel, not alone. The door is closed by the one who opened it: forgive, confess, renounce, and keep your house by the Test. The Word forbids railing at powers and forbids teaching a believer he carries guilt the Blood did not cover. Where the Word is silent, stay silent. And stand unafraid: the battle is Yahweh's, and Jesus already spoiled the principalities at the cross (Colossians 2:15).

teen.open: Who is allowed to fight spiritual battles? Someone who submits to Yahweh first and goes where He sends. And the doors you opened, you close: by forgiving and confessing.
teen.close: So submit to Yahweh first, do not go it alone, and close your own doors by forgiving and confessing. You do not need to be afraid. Jesus already won.

senior.open: The title asks who may fight spiritual battles and who closes the door. The Word answers: the believer submitted to Yahweh and sent by Him fights, and the one who gave place closes it, through confession, forgiveness and holiness.
senior.close: So the rules are plain. Submit, then resist; go only when sent, with counsel; close your own doors; never rail, and never preach inherited guilt. Where the Word is silent, rest there. The victory was won at the cross.

ll126-feelings-are-fruit-not-root-belief.reason: First paragraph states it plainly (emotions are the fruit of belief; change the belief, and Scripture agrees); the final paragraph opens 'Feelings are fruit' and ends 'the feeling follows the agreement'.

ll127-the-firsts-what-yahweh-did-in-each.reason: Opens on reading the spine and the goal (Genesis 3:8 to Revelation 21:3), but never says plainly that He never stopped wanting the walk; the answer stays implicit under dating method and the century list.
ll127-the-firsts-what-yahweh-did-in-each.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Did Yahweh ever stop wanting to walk with us? No. The Book opens with Him walking in a garden in the cool of the day (Genesis 3:8) and ends with Him moving in for good (Revelation 21:3). Every first in between, from the covering of skins to the empty tomb, is the repair that closes the distance, not a change of heart. Love cannot be forced, so He knocks and waits (Revelation 3:20). Here is that history, century by century.
ll127-the-firsts-what-yahweh-did-in-each.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Did Yahweh ever stop wanting to walk with us? Not for one century. After the fall He made the covering Himself (Genesis 3:21) and named the Seed to come (Genesis 3:15). He gave His name, moved into a tent, promised a covenant written on hearts, and then came in flesh. The final promise in the Book is the first picture in it. What He wanted in the garden is what He is still building toward: to dwell with you, ordinary days included.

teen.open: Did Yahweh ever give up on walking with people? No. The Bible starts with Him walking in a garden and ends with Him moving in for good.
teen.close: Every big first in history was Yahweh fixing the gap, not leaving. He still wants an ordinary walk with you, every day.

senior.open: The title asks whether Yahweh ever stopped wanting to walk with us. The Scriptures answer no: they open with Him walking in the garden (Genesis 3:8) and close with Him dwelling with His people (Revelation 21:3).
senior.close: So the answer holds through every century. What lies between those two verses is repair, patient and costly, because love must be freely given; the desire behind it never changed.

ll128-the-prudent-man-studies-systematic.reason: Opens on Darrell's two thoughts and Hosea 14:9; the how (study builds a trained sense by use, the words abide and change the defaults) is spread across a very long middle and only gathered in the final summary.
ll128-the-prudent-man-studies-systematic.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. How does a prudent person learn to see trouble coming? By study that is steady and systematic, precept upon precept, checking daily whether a thing is so (Isaiah 28:10; Acts 17:11). That study teaches you Yahweh's Ways, and His words abide in your heart until you recognise the shape of trouble in time to move (Proverbs 22:3). It is a sense trained by use (Hebrews 5:14), not luck and not a vision. Here is how the Word builds it.
ll128-the-prudent-man-studies-systematic.example: THE SHAPE YOU RECOGNISE. Say an offer comes to you in a hurry, with a promise that sounds too good. The simple man believes it and finds out later. A man who has studied "The simple believeth every word: but the prudent man looketh well to his going." (Proverbs 14:15), and who knows that safety is in a multitude of counsellors (Proverbs 11:14), has seen that shape before. He slows down, asks, and steps aside. Afterward he can name what he would have done, and did not do.
ll128-the-prudent-man-studies-systematic.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. How do the prudent learn Yahweh's Ways before the storm hits? They study as workmen, they do what they learn, and the words they studied abide in the heart, where the defaults run. So when trouble shows its shape, they recognise it and move. The storm still comes to every house (Matthew 7:25-27); what differs is the rock underneath. Ask Him for His Ways by name (Psalms 25:4), dwell rather than visit, and be willing and obedient.

teen.open: How do you see trouble coming before it hits? You learn Yahweh's Ways by studying His Word a little at a time, until you recognise trouble's shape.
teen.close: Storms still come to everyone. But the person who studies and does the Word has a rock under them, and learns to step aside in time.

senior.open: The title asks how the prudent come to see trouble before it arrives. Scripture's answer is study: careful, daily and systematic, until His Ways are learned and the senses are trained by use (Hebrews 5:14).
senior.close: So prudence is not a temperament one is born with; Proverbs gives it to the simple who will learn. Study that turns into doing builds the foundation the storm cannot move.

ll130-three-days-and-three-nights-what-h.reason: Opens by splitting the question into three claims without answering; the answer (victory dated at the cross, the three days were possession, power destroyed but person not) arrives in sections four to seven and is only gathered in the last lines.
ll130-three-days-and-three-nights-what-h.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Did Jesus defeat the devil in the place of the dead? The victory was won at the cross, not in a fight below. Jesus said "It is finished" before He died, and Paul places the triumph at His cross (Colossians 2:14-15). In the realm of the dead He preached, led captivity captive, held the keys, and rose: a Victor taking possession, not a combatant trading blows. The Word does not narrate those hours, so neither do we.
ll130-three-days-and-three-nights-what-h.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Did Jesus defeat the devil in the place of the dead? He had already won before He got there. Through His death He put out of commission the one who had the power of death (Hebrews 2:14), and the three days were the Victor walking through territory already lost. The person is not yet destroyed; that execution is still future (Revelation 20:10). So you fight from victory, not for it, and the fear of death that held you is broken (Hebrews 2:15).

teen.open: Did Jesus beat the devil in the place of the dead? The Bible says the win happened at the cross. The three days were Him taking over ground already won.
teen.close: So the devil's power is broken, but he is not gone yet. You stand on a victory Jesus already won, and you do not have to fear death.

senior.open: The title asks whether Jesus defeated the devil in the place of the dead. The Word dates the victory at the cross, where He said it was finished and triumphed over the powers openly (Colossians 2:15).
senior.close: So the verdict is past, while the binding and the final fire are still ahead. The adversary's power was broken through the death of Jesus; his end is written. We stand on ground already taken.

ll129-you-have-a-destiny-the-giver-the-w.reason: Movement One answers early (Yahweh, the Greater, blesses the lesser and gives before we ask), after a sourcing paragraph; the ending is a summary list closing on a fragment of Psalms 84:11, not on the answer.
ll129-you-have-a-destiny-the-giver-the-w.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Who is blessing you before you ask? Yahweh is. The lesser is blessed of the better, and He is the Greater, so blessing runs downhill from Him to you. He knows what you need before you ask (Matthew 6:8), and having given His own Son, He will freely give the rest (Romans 8:32). Prayer is not prying something out of a reluctant hand. Here is how the gift is received.
ll129-you-have-a-destiny-the-giver-the-w.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Who is blessing you before you ask? The Father who already knows and already gave. Faith is the window His blessing comes through; covenant, not long or clever words, is what a short prayer stands on; and a heart of flesh, which He gives in exchange for stone, is what still receives. So say one true sentence to Him, bring Him the hard place, and trust the One who gives grace and glory (Psalms 84:11).

teen.open: Who blesses you before you even ask? Yahweh does. He is the Giver, and He already knows what you need.
teen.close: You do not have to beg or use fancy words. Trust Him, bring Him the hard places in your heart, and let Him give.

senior.open: The title asks who blesses us before we ask. Scripture answers that Yahweh, the Greater, blesses the lesser, and He knows our needs before we speak (Matthew 6:8).
senior.close: So prayer rests on a Giver who has already given His Son. Faith receives, the covenant carries the prayer, and a heart He has softened is able to take in what He gives.
