ll131-joy-is-not-happiness-three-days-on.reason: First paragraph answers plainly (happiness reads the day; strength is wired to the joy OF the LORD, which the weather cannot touch, Nehemiah 8:10); ends 'Happiness is weather. Joy is the power line. Strength is on the power line.'

ll132-the-whole-salvation-plan-inside-ge.reason: Opening asserts the plan is legible from the beginning and Part Four shows Genesis 3:15; 'What this means for you' lands it, but the lesson ends on Part Nine's list of supporting witnesses instead.
ll132-the-whole-salvation-plan-inside-ge.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Was the rescue a late idea? No. The Father, the Spirit and the speaking Word are at work in the first verses of Genesis, before any enemy appears. On the very day of the fall, Yahweh sought the man first and announced the whole rescue to the serpent's face (Genesis 3:15): the Seed, the war, the wound and the crushed head. Then Genesis shows the plan unfolding, chapter by chapter.
ll132-the-whole-salvation-plan-inside-ge.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Was the rescue ever a late idea? Genesis alone says no. The Three were at work before the crisis walked in. The rescue was published in the sentence on the serpent, the covering was made by Yahweh's own hands, righteousness was credited for believing (Genesis 15:6), and a ram was offered in the stead of a son (Genesis 22:8, 13). So you can stop reading your own rescue as an emergency measure. It was announced the day the first man fell.

teen.open: Was saving us a last-minute plan? No. Right after the first sin, Yahweh promised a Rescuer who would crush the serpent's head.
teen.close: From the start of Genesis, the plan was already in motion. Your rescue was never Yahweh's backup plan.

senior.open: The title claims the rescue was never an afterthought. Genesis bears that out: the Three are at work from the opening verses, and the rescue is announced on the day of the fall (Genesis 3:15).
senior.close: So the plan of salvation is legible in the first book, from the coats of skins to the lamb provided on the mountain. Our rescue was published, not improvised.

ll134-divers-weights-when-the-question-k.reason: Opens on the video scene; the answer (name it as divers weights, you owe a rigged question nothing, keep your own scale exact, teach your children) is spread across Parts Two, Three, Six and Eight, with a long record list between.
ll134-divers-weights-when-the-question-k.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. How do you answer a question that changes its standard the moment you meet it? First, name it: two standards in one bag is divers weights, and the Word calls it an abomination (Proverbs 20:10). You were not failing a test. Then you are free: you do not owe a rigged question an answer, you keep your own scale exact, and you spend your best hours teaching your children. Here is how the Word sets your footing.
ll134-divers-weights-when-the-question-k.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. How do you answer a rigged scale without losing your footing? You stand on the Word, not on the scorner's approval. You name the moving goalpost for what it is. You answer or keep silent as the Spirit leads (Proverbs 26:4-5), the way Jesus read intent and owed bad faith nothing. You tell the record exactly, because a just weight is His delight. And you hand that record to your children. The truth makes you free of needing to win.

teen.open: What do you do when someone keeps moving the goalposts on you? Call it what the Bible calls it: an unfair scale. You were not failing.
teen.close: You do not have to win their argument. Be honest and exact, and teach the truth to the people who will listen.

senior.open: The title asks how to answer a scale that keeps shifting. The Word names it first: divers weights, a great and a small, an abomination to the LORD (Deuteronomy 25:13; Proverbs 20:10).
senior.close: So one keeps one's footing by refusing the rigged exchange as a verdict, keeping one's own weights honest, and giving the best hours to teaching the next generation.

ll133-how-to-see-the-whole-torah-at-once.reason: Opens on sight and the named-versus-confessed discipline; the patterns arrive one Part at a time and are only gathered into one picture in Part Nine.
ll133-how-to-see-the-whole-torah-at-once.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Can you spot the patterns in the Torah, not just the stories? Yes. Read the five books for what keeps repeating and they become one picture: the Three at work before any crisis, a Man seen who carries the Name, a likeness that gives itself for others, something dying in someone's place, and an enemy with the same three moves. One habit keeps it honest: know what the text names and what is our confession.
ll133-how-to-see-the-whole-torah-at-once.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Can you read the Torah like a map? You can, when you hold the patterns together: the Three already at work, the One seen who carries the Name, the likeness that stands in someone else's place, the blood that covers from the garden to the pole, and the enemy's question, contradiction and promotion. Keep what is named apart from what is confessed, and ask Yahweh for a heart to perceive (Deuteronomy 29:4), because sight is His gift.

teen.open: Can you see the big patterns in the first five books of the Bible? Yes. The same things keep showing up, like landmarks on a map.
teen.close: Look for the repeats, be honest about what the text actually says, and ask Yahweh to help you see. Then the stories become one picture.

senior.open: The title asks whether the Torah can be read for its patterns rather than only its stories. It can: the same truths recur across all five books, and together they form one picture.
senior.close: Held together, the patterns point to one Person: the Man at the ford, the provided Lamb, the King out of Judah. That is our confession, held with care, and the perceiving is His gift.

ll135-they-called-every-one-of-them-geor.reason: Opens on method and the Pullman history; the answer (Scripture's porters are ordained and named, He calls His own by name and sees them) only arrives in sections three to five; the ending lands it well.
ll135-they-called-every-one-of-them-geor.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Called by the wrong name? Passengers called every Pullman porter George, so no one had to learn who anyone was. Yahweh does the opposite. In His house the porters are ordained, named and trusted, and the One who comes through the door calls His own sheep by name (John 10:3). He sees you, and He has never been recorded taking a name away. Here is what the porter at the gate reveals.
ll135-they-called-every-one-of-them-geor.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. What does the porter at the gate reveal about being seen? That a name the world takes away, Yahweh gives back. The word used to make men interchangeable is the word Scripture uses for ordained, named servants at His door. He calls His own by name (Isaiah 43:1), a servant woman named Him the One who sees her (Genesis 16:13), and He raises what the builders refused. A company can decide what to call you. It cannot touch what Yahweh has written down.

teen.open: Ever been called by the wrong name, or treated like you were just a job? Yahweh does not do that. He calls His people by name.
teen.close: People may forget your name, but Yahweh sees you and has your name written down. Learn someone else's name this week too.

senior.open: The title asks what it means to be called by the wrong name, and whether Yahweh truly sees us. Scripture answers plainly: He calls His own by name (John 10:3; Isaiah 43:1).
senior.close: So the porters who were all called George are a picture of what Yahweh never does. He names, He sees, and what men set at nought He raises.

ll136-touched-with-the-feeling-the-high-.reason: Opens by splitting the question into three claims without answering; the no (never yielding means the full weight, made sin not felt like one, judgment rests on the Father) builds over twelve sections and is gathered only at the end.
ll136-touched-with-the-feeling-the-high-.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Does our High Priest need to sin to understand us? No. He was tempted in all points like we are, yet without sin (Hebrews 4:15), and because He never yielded, He felt the full weight that we escape by giving in. He was made sin for us while knowing no sin (2 Corinthians 5:21). And His judgment is true because it is righteous and the Father's, not because He sampled our experience. Here is how the Word shows it.
ll136-touched-with-the-feeling-the-high-.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Does our High Priest need to sin to understand us? No, and that is good news. He stayed to the end of every pressure, and He took the full damage our sin actually does, all the way to a grave. His judgment rests on the Father and on righteousness, so it never depended on living your case. His sympathy was given for another reason: so you can come boldly to the throne of grace for mercy and help (Hebrews 4:16).

teen.open: Did Jesus have to sin to understand you? No. He faced every kind of temptation and never gave in, so He felt the full weight of it.
teen.close: He gets it more than anyone. So you can come to Him boldly, even with the things you failed at.

senior.open: The title asks whether our High Priest must sin in order to understand us. Hebrews answers no: He was tempted in all points, yet without sin (Hebrews 4:15).
senior.close: So His understanding is not weaker for His sinlessness but fuller, and His judgment rests on the Father's righteousness. The sympathy is given so that we may draw near boldly.

ll138-exercised-senses-why-perception-is.reason: Opening gives the answer in one line (He is not withholding; perception is grown; tests are the growing); the gathered answer at the end drifts into diligence and education and stops on a half-quoted John 7:17.
ll138-exercised-senses-why-perception-is.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Does Yahweh hold back wisdom because He doubts us? No. He gives liberally and does not lecture (James 1:5). Perception is a sense, and senses are trained by use (Hebrews 5:14), so it comes as a dawn, not a switch. The tests are not exams of His trust; they are where that sense is exercised, for your profit. As your Ways line up with His Word, you grow, because doing is the exercise: "If any man will do his will, he shall know".

teen.open: Is Yahweh keeping wisdom from you because He does not trust you? No. He gives it freely, and it grows as you use it.
teen.close: Tests are practice, not a sign He doubts you. Each time you do what His Word says, you learn to see a little more.

senior.open: The title asks whether Yahweh withholds wisdom because He doubts us. James 1:5 answers that He gives liberally and upbraids not.
senior.close: So perception is grown, not rationed. The trials exercise it, obedience is the road it grows on, and the Spirit of truth has already been given to guide us.

ll140-the-people-of-judah-and-the-people.reason: Opens by restating Darrell's question and walks eleven sections; the gathered answer (who, where, whom to hear) only arrives in the last paragraph, after long asides on psyops, wages, nations and Tubman.
ll140-the-people-of-judah-and-the-people.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Who are Judah and the people of the Way, and whose voice should you trust? Judah is the tribe named praise, scattered among all nations but never lost: Yahweh keeps count of every grain. The people of the Way are those from every nation who believe all things written, grafted into Israel's tree, joined and never replacing it. The voice to trust is the King of Judah, heard in His Word, and every other voice is tested by that Word and by its fruit, never by its family line. Here is how the Word shows it.
ll140-the-people-of-judah-and-the-people.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Who are Judah and the people of the Way, and whose voice should you trust? Judah is a people Yahweh scattered and still counts, sealed by tribe at the end (Revelation 7:4). The Way is one people drawn from every nation, counted in the way Caleb, Ruth and Rahab were, by wholly following Him. You do not find them by the news or by anyone's lineage claim; you know them by love (John 13:35). And you trust one Voice: "hear ye him." Scattered, never lost. Joined, never replacing.

teen.open: Who are Judah and the people of the Way? Judah is a tribe Yahweh scattered but never lost. The Way is everyone, from every nation, who believes His Word. The voice to trust is Jesus.
teen.close: So here is the answer. Yahweh still counts Judah, the Way is one family from every nation joined to them, and you trust Jesus in His Word, testing every other voice by it.

senior.open: The title asks who Judah and the people of the Way are, and whose voice to trust. The plain answer: Judah is scattered among the nations yet known to Yahweh; the Way is the believers from every nation joined to Israel's tree; and the voice is the King of Judah, heard in His Word.
senior.close: So the question has its answer. Judah is scattered, never lost. The people of the Way are joined, never replacing. And every voice is weighed by the Word and by its fruit, never by its genealogy, while the one Voice we hear is His.

ll137-look-and-live-the-serpent-on-the-p.reason: Opening answers Darrell's analogy question (yes, it is the Son's own), not the title's why; the why (the look was believing His word over the liar, the cure shaped like the curse) is spread across sections two and three.
ll137-look-and-live-the-serpent-on-the-p.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Why did Yahweh tell a dying people to look at a serpent? Because the look was believing. The people had believed the liar's voice about Yahweh, and the bite followed. The cure was to take Yahweh at His word against every instinct, with poison in their veins. And the serpent on the pole was a picture Jesus Himself claimed: the cure shaped like the curse, the Son lifted up on the cross (John 3:14-15). Here is how the Word shows it.
ll137-look-and-live-the-serpent-on-the-p.example: ONE BITTEN MAN. Say a man in the camp is bitten and the poison is moving. His neighbour says it is only a piece of metal on a stick. His own heart says he does not feel faith enough. He turns his eyes to the pole anyway, half open, and he lives. Nothing in the brass healed him and nothing in the quality of his look did. He lived because "every one that is bitten, when he looketh upon it, shall live." That is the whole cure: the power is in the One looked at.
ll137-look-and-live-the-serpent-on-the-p.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Why did Yahweh tell a dying people to look at a serpent? Because He was teaching the whole world how saving faith works. The bite came after the people believed the liar's sentence about Him. The cure came by believing His sentence instead, with nothing in their hands but their eyes. The pole showed the curse judged in public, and the Son fulfilled it on the tree, so whosoever believes in Him should not perish (John 3:15-16). The serpents were not taken away; a place to look was given. Look to Him and live.

teen.open: Why would Yahweh tell dying people to look at a serpent? Because looking meant trusting His word instead of the liar's. Jesus said the pole pointed to Him on the cross.
teen.close: So that is why. Looking at the pole was believing Yahweh over the liar. Today you look to Jesus, lifted up on the cross, and you live.

senior.open: The title asks why Yahweh told a dying people to look at a serpent. The answer is that the look was faith: taking His word over the liar's, and Jesus named that pole as the picture of His own cross.
senior.close: So the question is answered. The bitten were told to look because looking was believing Yahweh against every contrary voice. The same holds now: whoever looks to the Son lifted up does not perish but has everlasting life.

ll141-separate-and-connect-working-throu.reason: Opening explains why the cut makes connection real, but the HOW (go to him alone to gain him, anger with a deadline, overcome evil with good) is spread over seven sections and only gathered in the last lines.
ll141-separate-and-connect-working-throu.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. How do we stay connected when truth hurts? By letting the Word cut first inside us, separating what is true from what we want, and then standing on that truth together. Two people on the same ground are joined; a peace that keeps the sword sheathed is only a truce. Then we work it out the way the Word lays down: go to the person alone, aiming to gain them, not to win. Here is how the Word shows it.
ll141-separate-and-connect-working-throu.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. How do we stay connected when truth hurts? We let the Word that cuts do its work in us first, and we refuse to settle for a truce that holds only while nobody says anything true. Then we go to the person alone to gain them, leave the gift at the altar until we are reconciled, put anger to bed before sundown, study to handle the Word rightly, and overcome evil with good. The cut is what makes the connection real, and the ones who keep it that way are called the children of Yahweh (Matthew 5:9).

teen.open: How do you stay close to people when the truth hurts? You let the truth set you right first, then go to the person yourself, aiming to keep them, not beat them.
teen.close: So the answer is this. Truth cuts so that people can stand on the same ground. Go to the person, forgive, and do good even to an enemy, and you stay connected.

senior.open: The title asks how we stay connected when truth hurts. The Word's answer is that the cut is what makes the connection real: truth first divides falsehood within us, and those who stand on it together are joined.
senior.close: So the question has its answer. We stay connected not by keeping truth quiet but by handling it the Word's way: privately, to gain the brother, without vengeance, overcoming evil with good. That is the peacemaker's road.

ll139-the-sceptre-of-judah-who-judah-is-.reason: The ruler is named (Shiloh is Jesus, the Lion of Judah) only at the end of section four, after long sections on Judah the man and tribe; later sections on media, church history and music drift before the gathered answer.
ll139-the-sceptre-of-judah-who-judah-is-.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Who is the ruler Judah still carries toward the end? Jesus, the Eternal Son of Yahweh. Jacob said the sceptre, the ruler's rod, would not leave Judah until Shiloh came, the One the people are gathered to (Genesis 49:10). The Word points to Him by name: the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, born in Bethlehem of Judah. And "until" marks His arrival, not the sceptre's end. It reached the hand it was made for. Here is how the Word shows it.
ll139-the-sceptre-of-judah-who-judah-is-.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Who is the ruler Judah still carries toward the end? Shiloh, He whose right it is: Jesus, the Lion of Judah who prevailed by being the Lamb. Yahweh gave Judah the sceptre by choice and by an oath He will not break, and through every attempt to destroy the line He kept it travelling toward one hand. When He came, the sceptre did not leave Judah; it arrived. His throne is for ever and ever (Hebrews 1:8), the gathering of the people is to Him, and the sceptre is not leaving His hand.

teen.open: Who is the ruler Judah carries to the end? Jesus. Jacob said the sceptre would stay with Judah until Shiloh came, and the Word shows Shiloh is Jesus, the Lion of Judah.
teen.close: So the ruler Judah carries is Jesus. The sceptre stayed in Judah until it reached His hand, and He reigns for ever. It is not leaving Him.

senior.open: The title asks who the ruler is that Judah carries toward the end. The Word's answer is Jesus: Shiloh, the One the people are gathered to, the Lion of the tribe of Judah and the Root of David.
senior.close: So the question is answered. The sceptre promised to Judah was always travelling toward one hand, and in Jesus it arrived. "Until" meant His coming, not its departure, and His throne has no end.

ll142-it-is-written-again-the-clause-tha.reason: The first half (a clipped verse turns truth into a lie) is shown early via Eden and Psalm 91; why His Name is no cover only arrives in plank four (Jeremiah 23, menstealers, the cut 1807 Bible); ends on an invitation, not the answer.
ll142-it-is-written-again-the-clause-tha.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. What happens when the rest of the page is left out? Nothing false is invented, but something is removed, and the truth bends into a lie: Eden's generosity became a rule, and Psalm 91's safety rail was cut off. And why is Yahweh's name never a cover for it? Because He is against everyone who puts His name on their own business (Jeremiah 23:31). Those who used the Word for slavery had to cut the Word to do it. Here is how the Word shows it.
ll142-it-is-written-again-the-clause-tha.example: ONE VERSE, TWO HALVES. Take the verse the friend in this lesson trusts most. Say someone tells you the whole Bible comes down to loving your neighbour as yourself. That is a real commandment. But Jesus was asked for the great commandment and gave two: love Yahweh with all your heart, soul and mind first, then your neighbour (Matthew 22:37-40). Quote only the second and call it the first, and you have done the very thing this lesson describes, in good faith, without one false word.
ll142-it-is-written-again-the-clause-tha.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. What happens when the rest of the page is left out? The Word gets turned against itself without a single lie told, and the destruction falls on the one doing the wresting, not on the Word. Why is Yahweh's name never a cover for it? Because He reads the heart, not the charter. Profession was never possession, and He names those who say "He saith" when He has not spoken. So the answer to a clipped verse is the one Jesus gave: "It is written again". Restore the whole page. Yahweh is not afraid of it; He wrote it.

teen.open: What happens when part of a verse gets cut off? The truth gets twisted without anyone saying a lie. And putting Yahweh's name on it does not make it His.
teen.close: So when someone hands you half a verse, do what Jesus did: read the rest of the page. Yahweh is against anyone who uses His name to cover their own plans.

senior.open: The title asks what happens when the rest of the page is left out, and why Yahweh's name cannot cover it. A trimmed verse bends truth into error without inventing anything, and Yahweh stands against those who claim His word for their own ends.
senior.close: So the question is answered. Leaving out the rest of the page lets a man use the Word against the Word, as slaveholders did. His name is no shelter for that; the remedy is always the whole page, read and checked.

ll143-yahwehs-will-be-done-on-earth-the-.reason: Opens on Darrell's directive and the grief of knowledge; release, restitution and the working community each appear in separate later sections and are never drawn together as the answer to the title before the closing 'build it here'.
ll143-yahwehs-will-be-done-on-earth-the-.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. What if Yahweh's economy was built to outlast ours? It was. His economy is real legislation with a clock in it: debts released every seventh year, no usury on your brother, the open hand lent into need, and stolen goods restored with a fifth added. And it carries a promise no human system attaches to itself: that there be no poor among you (Deuteronomy 15:4). Its aim was never the ledger. It was that your brother may live with you. Here is how the Word lays it out.
ll143-yahwehs-will-be-done-on-earth-the-.example: WHAT RESTITUTION LOOKS LIKE. Say a lender is found charging one neighbour more than another for reasons that have nothing to do with the loan, and the extra taken comes to $1,000. The Word's remedy is not an apology. It is the principal restored with the fifth part added: $1,000 plus $200, so $1,200 goes back to the one who was wronged (Leviticus 6:5). The tax collector who met Jesus went further on his own and restored fourfold. The harmed party ends up whole and ahead, holding ownership rather than a regret.
ll143-yahwehs-will-be-done-on-earth-the-.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. What if Yahweh's economy was built to outlast ours? Then the release, the honest balance and restitution with a fifth added are not old customs; they are the design. Ours turns debt into standing servitude and needs money more than love. His puts a clock on debt and measures success by whether anyone lacks. And it has already worked, from the early believers who had all things common to the mutual aid societies that built banks and insurers. So build it here, and let the builders keep the work of their hands (Isaiah 65:22).

teen.open: What if Yahweh's way of handling money was made to last longer than ours? It was. He built in debt release, fair weights, and paying back more than you took, so no one goes without.
teen.close: So Yahweh's economy does outlast ours, because it was built for people, not just profit. Release, pay back, share, and make sure nobody among you lacks.

senior.open: The title asks what it would mean if Yahweh's economy was built to outlast ours. The Word shows it was: a seventh-year release, a ban on usury between brothers, and restitution with a fifth added, all aimed at a people with no poor among them.
senior.close: So the question has its answer. His economy outlasts ours because its purpose was never the ledger but the life of the brother beside you. A community that releases, restores and refuses a false balance still works, and has worked before.

ll144-a-false-balance-capable-hands-and-.reason: Answers right after the directive (capital by ability, Matthew 25:15; divers weights an abomination), but ends on the two-ways choice and Psalm 1:6 without returning to ability versus lineage.
ll144-a-false-balance-capable-hands-and-.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Does Yahweh's standard allow capital to follow lineage, or only ability? Only ability. A loan asks one thing: can this borrower sustain the payments? In the parable the master entrusts his goods "to every man according to his several ability". A market that claims to weigh ability but sorts by lineage carries two weights in one bag, and the Word calls that an abomination (Proverbs 11:1). Here is how the Word shows it, and what the record shows.
ll144-a-false-balance-capable-hands-and-.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Does Yahweh's standard allow capital to follow lineage, or only ability? Only ability, weighed by one true stone for every borrower. Withholding capital from capable hands because of who their fathers were is the false balance, and it costs the whole nation: the food in the poor man's field is destroyed, and the jobs his business would have made never exist. The fix is not a scale leaned the other way (Leviticus 19:15). It is an honest measure, restitution of what was taken, and the pooled hand our own people carried here. Keep one weight in the bag.

teen.open: Should money be lent based on someone's family or on what they can do? Yahweh's answer is ability. Using a different measure for different people is a false weight, and He hates it.
teen.close: So Yahweh's standard is ability, not family line. One honest measure for everyone, no tilting it either way, and paying back what was wrongly taken.

senior.open: The title asks whether Yahweh's standard lets capital follow lineage or only ability. The Word answers plainly: goods are entrusted according to ability, and two weights in one bag are an abomination to Him.
senior.close: So the question has its answer. Capital rightly follows demonstrated ability, measured the same way for every person. Sorting by lineage is a false balance; the remedy is an honest weight and restitution, never a scale tipped the other way.

ll145-i-will-not-go-out-free-the-bondser.reason: Darrell's answer (bondservants He made and repurchased out of love) is stated in the first paragraph, but the lesson ends on a question for the friend rather than landing the plain answer to the title.
ll145-i-will-not-go-out-free-the-bondser.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Does Yahweh want slaves? No, not in the sense the laugh means. The word servant is really there, but His law defines it: freedom arrives free in the seventh year, the master must send the servant out with capital, and a servant stays for good only if he says aloud that he loves his master. Yahweh wants bondservants He created and bought back with His own blood, because He loves them, and He calls them friends and sons. Read the law first.
ll145-i-will-not-go-out-free-the-bondser.example: ONE MAN AT THE DOOR. Say a man has served six years. In the seventh, the law sets him free for nothing, and his master loads him with livestock, grain and wine on his way out (Deuteronomy 15:13-14). The door is open and his hands are full. He stops, turns, and says before the judges that he loves his master and his household and will not go out free. Only then is his ear marked, at the doorway. That mark does not record a capture. It records a choice made in love.
ll145-i-will-not-go-out-free-the-bondser.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Does Yahweh want slaves? He wants people who belong to Him by love, and His law proves it. Release comes on a clock, severance is paid from the master's own flock, and permanence needs the servant's own words: I love my master. Then He paid for us with Himself, not with silver or gold, and raised us from servant to friend to son to heir (John 15:15; Galatians 4:7). Everyone serves someone (Romans 6:16). The only real question is which master, and His yoke is easy.

teen.open: Does Yahweh want slaves? Read His law and the answer is no. He set servants free on a schedule, sent them off with plenty, and only kept those who chose to stay out of love.
teen.close: So Yahweh does not want slaves. He bought you with His own life because He loves you, and He calls you His friend and His child.

senior.open: The title asks whether Yahweh wants slaves. The law itself answers no: release on a fixed clock, severance from the master's own flock, and permanence only by the servant's declared love.
senior.close: So the question has its answer. The bondservant of the Word is not the slave of human history. He is one freely loved and freely loving, bought at the cost of the Lamb, and raised to friend, son and heir.

ll146-he-said-it-first-what-it-sounds-li.reason: Opens on the long directive and its verses; the test (game is talk a man cannot back, He paid before He spoke) arrives in movement one, and the verdict on the hard passages is split across movements three to six.
ll146-he-said-it-first-what-it-sounds-li.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. If someone said all this to you, would you believe them? Not from most people, because big promises are cheap until they are backed. But Yahweh is the one speaker whose lines were paid for before He said them: Christ died for us while we were still sinners (Romans 5:8). And He did not hide the hard passages. He told you His goodness and His severity together, to your face. That is why His love can be trusted. Here is the test, run on the Word.
ll146-he-said-it-first-what-it-sounds-li.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. If someone said all this to you, would you believe them? You can believe Yahweh, because He passes the test no flatterer can. He went first, He paid first, and He said it first. He told you the hard half too: a love that can be provoked, a fire He walks through with you, a loss that is bounded and never abandoned, and one life to answer for. A man who tells you only the sweet half is managing you. Yahweh told you the whole thing, then made Himself the way out (John 14:6). Believe Him now.

teen.open: If someone told you everything Yahweh says about loving you, would you believe it? With Him you can, because He proved it first: Jesus died for you before you ever loved Him back.
teen.close: So yes, you can believe Him. He did not just talk; He paid first, and He even told you the hard parts. Someone who tells you only the nice stuff is not being straight with you.

senior.open: The title asks whether you would believe someone who said all this to you. With men, words are cheap until backed. With Yahweh, the backing came first: Christ died for us while we were yet sinners, and He set His severity beside His goodness in plain view.
senior.close: So the question is answered. His love survives the test of the hard passages because He spoke them openly, bounded every trial, and paid the price before He asked for trust. That is a love a life can rest on.

ll147-the-due-he-is-owed-every-place-the.reason: Sets the standard (worship Yahweh only) first, but the answer (Jesus receives it and is never corrected, while Peter, Paul and the angel refuse) builds across moves two to four; ends on John 1 verses, not a stated answer.
ll147-the-due-he-is-owed-every-place-the.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Who gets the worship? Yahweh only; Jesus Himself said so (Matthew 4:10). And yet, scene after scene, people fall down and worship Jesus, and He never once stops them. When anyone else is worshipped, even Peter, Paul or a mighty angel, they refuse at once. So the worship belongs to Yahweh, and the Son receives it as His due, honoured even as the Father is honoured (John 5:23). Count the scenes and see.
ll147-the-due-he-is-owed-every-place-the.example: THREE FALLS IN ONE BOOK. Follow one man, John, through Revelation. He falls at the feet of an angel, and the angel refuses at once and sends his worship to Yahweh alone (Revelation 19:10). Near the end he falls before an angel again and is refused again, almost word for word (Revelation 22:8-9). But at the start of the book he falls at the feet of the risen Christ, and there is no refusal. There is a right hand laid on him and a voice saying, "Fear not; I am the first and the last" (Revelation 1:17). Two refusals, one welcome.
ll147-the-due-he-is-owed-every-place-the.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Who gets the worship? Yahweh alone, and the Word shows Jesus receiving it. Wise men, a leper, a grieving ruler, a desperate mother, a man born blind and the eleven all knelt to Him, and He accepted every knee that men and angels turned away. The Father commands the angels to worship the Son, and heaven sings to Him that sits on the throne and to the Lamb in one breath (Revelation 5:13). Giving the Son His due takes nothing from the Father. It is the road by which the Father is glorified (Philippians 2:11).

teen.open: Who should be worshipped? Only Yahweh. Yet people kept worshipping Jesus and He never told them to stop, while apostles and angels always refused it.
teen.close: So the worship goes to Yahweh, and Jesus receives it as His own. Heaven worships the Father and the Lamb together. Honouring Jesus honours the Father too.

senior.open: The title asks who gets the worship. The Word's standard is Yahweh alone, and the record shows Jesus accepting worship in every scene, where apostles and angels refused it without delay.
senior.close: So the question has its answer. The worship is Yahweh's, and the Son receives it as His due, even as the Father is honoured. Every knee will bow at His name, to the glory of the Father.

ll149-cultural-competency-the-same-word-.reason: The thesis (many ways to play, one Way to win) comes early, but the how of hearing before judging (Proverbs 18:13, searching, watching deeds, giving time) is spread through the middle and only gathered in the close.
ll149-cultural-competency-the-same-word-.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. How do you hear a true word before you judge it? Hear it all the way through first, because answering a matter before you hear it is folly and shame (Proverbs 18:13). Ask what the word meant in the mouth that said it, not only how it sounds. Then search it out, watch the deeds, and give time its work, and ask Yahweh for wisdom while you do. People play the game many ways, but there is one Way to win (John 14:6). Here is how the Word teaches the hearing.
ll149-cultural-competency-the-same-word-.example: ONE SENTENCE, THREE HEARINGS. Say a man tells a woman early on that he knew from the first time he saw her. If she carries only the first meaning of game, she files it as a line and feels wise for it. If she hears it the Word's way, she does not answer yet. She asks what kind of man is saying it, watches what he does over months, and asks Yahweh for wisdom. The disciples in Jerusalem did the same with Saul: Barnabas brought them evidence, and time did the rest (Acts 9:26-27).
ll149-cultural-competency-the-same-word-.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. How do you hear a true word before you judge it? Be swift to hear and slow to speak (James 1:19). Judge righteous judgment, not appearance (John 7:24). Let the neighbour come and search the first story. Then look for the deeds, because love is proved in deed and in truth, and give it time the way the churches did with Paul. Prove all things and hold fast the good. Different people play the game differently, but there is one Way to win: ask Yahweh, and read His Word.

teen.open: How do you know if something true is true before you judge it? Listen all the way first, look at what the person does over time, and ask Yahweh for wisdom.
teen.close: So do not decide too fast. Hear the whole thing, watch the actions, give it time, and keep the good. There are many ways to play, but only one Way to win: Jesus.

senior.open: The title asks how to hear a true word before judging it. The Word's answer is to hear the matter fully, weigh what it meant in the speaker's mouth rather than its surface, and let deeds and time supply the evidence.
senior.close: So the question has its answer. Hear first, search patiently, prove all things, and hold fast the good, asking Yahweh for the wisdom He gives freely. Many play the game; there is still only one Way to win.

ll148-remember-is-a-verb-what-the-word-s.reason: Opens on Darrell's framing about hell and the sea; the split answer (His knowing never fails; remember no more is a verdict, not amnesia) builds over several sections and is only stated plainly in the close.
ll148-remember-is-a-verb-what-the-word-s.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Can Yahweh forget your sin, or only choose not to act on it? The Word shows the second, and it is the stronger promise. His understanding is infinite, and no verse shows Him deleting a fact. But in Scripture, remember is an action word: when He remembered Noah, the wind moved. So "I will remember their sin no more" is a verdict: He will never again act against you on that account. Here is how the Word shows it.
ll148-remember-is-a-verb-what-the-word-s.example: WHAT GOES INTO THE SEA. Read Micah 7:19 slowly: He will cast all their sins into the depths of the sea. Not the people. The sins. Say you owed a debt and the lender tore up the record against you in front of witnesses. He has not lost his memory; he has settled the account, and no court can reopen it. That is the shape of every promise in this lesson: the charge sheet is removed, as far as the east is from the west (Psalms 103:12), and you stand.
ll148-remember-is-a-verb-what-the-word-s.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Can Yahweh forget your sin, or only choose not to act on it? He does not need to forget in order to forgive. He knows all things, and He has judged the matter and will never act on it again, which is firmer than forgetting, because what is forgotten can be recalled. He seals what He chooses and opens it on His own clock. And what He casts into the depths of the sea is your sins, never you. The only thing that keeps anyone out is a settled "ye would not". Seek Him while you are inside the window.

teen.open: Can Yahweh actually forget your sin? He knows everything, so He does not lose track. But when He says He will remember it no more, He means He will never hold it against you again.
teen.close: So Yahweh does not have to forget to forgive. He has decided the case for good. Your sins go into the sea, not you. Come to Him while the door is open.

senior.open: The title asks whether Yahweh can forget your sin or only chooses not to act on it. The Word teaches the second: His knowing is infinite, and His remembering no more is a covenant verdict that the account is closed.
senior.close: So the question has its answer. Forgiveness in the Word is not divine forgetfulness but a settled judgment that will not be reopened. That is the firmer comfort, and it is offered while He may be found.

ll151-the-tongue-death-and-life-in-a-lit.reason: Opens on Proverbs 18:21 (death and life) but never says plainly what the tongue controls; the bit/helm answer is scattered in James 3, and it ends on a string of verses, not the answer.
ll151-the-tongue-death-and-life-in-a-lit.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. What does Yahweh say the tongue really controls? Far more than tone or mood. He says death and life are in its power (Proverbs 18:21), and that like a bit in a horse's mouth or the small helm of a great ship, it turns the whole body and the whole course of a life (James 3:3-5). No man can tame it, but a heart filled from the Word can govern it. Here is how the Word shows it.
ll151-the-tongue-death-and-life-in-a-lit.example: ONE SENTENCE, TWO HARVESTS. Say a friend comes to you upset over a misunderstanding. You answer before you have heard the whole matter, with a few sharp words, and later repeat it to someone else. The grievous words stir up anger, and the whisper separates chief friends (Proverbs 15:1; 16:28; 18:13). Or you listen first, then give a soft answer, and the wrath turns away. Same mouth, same moment, two harvests, and you eat the fruit of the one you planted.
ll151-the-tongue-death-and-life-in-a-lit.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. What does the tongue really control? Yahweh's answer is death and life: the course of your friendships, your home and your own soul (Proverbs 21:23), steered by a little member the way a helm steers a ship. You cannot tame it by willpower, because the mouth only reads what the heart holds (Matthew 12:34). So fill the heart with His Word, ask Him to set a watch before your mouth (Psalms 141:3), and be swift to hear and slow to speak. Then the fruit you eat will be life.

teen.open: What does your tongue really control? Yahweh says death and life. Like a small steering wheel on a big ship, your words steer your friendships and your whole life.
teen.close: So your words steer a lot. You can't tame your tongue by trying harder, but you can fill your heart with Yahweh's Word, listen first, and ask Him to guard your mouth.

senior.open: The title asks what the tongue truly controls. Scripture's answer is sobering: death and life are in its power, and like a bit or a helm, this small member turns the whole course of a life (Proverbs 18:21; James 3:3-4).
senior.close: So the answer stands plain. The tongue governs death and life in a home and a friendship, and because it speaks from the heart's abundance, it is governed by keeping the heart in the Word and asking Yahweh to keep the door of our lips.

ll150-how-can-the-son-not-know-what-the-.reason: States the question at once, but the answer (He emptied Himself and took a real human mind, keeping the Father's order) arrives mid-lesson in pieces; it ends on application rather than restating it.
ll150-how-can-the-son-not-know-what-the-.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Can the Son truly not know the day and the hour? Yes, and He said so Himself (Mark 13:32). Yet He is still fully Yahweh, the One in whom all the fulness of the Godhead dwells. The not-knowing is something He did, not something He lacked: He emptied Himself, took a real human mind that grew in wisdom, and kept the Father's order. Here is how the Word holds both in one Person.
ll150-how-can-the-son-not-know-what-the-.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Can the Son truly not know? Yes, and it cost Him nothing of His deity. The Word holds both in one Person: the eternal Son who knows all things, who made Himself of no reputation, took a real human life that increased in wisdom, and left the times the Father put in His own power to the Father (Philippians 2:5-8; Luke 2:52; Acts 1:7). His not-knowing was humility, not lack. That same mind is handed to you: hold the hour you are not given in trust.

teen.open: Can Jesus really not know something? Yes, He said He didn't know the day of His return. But He is still fully Yahweh. He chose to set aside using His rights and live a real human life.
teen.close: So Jesus truly didn't name the hour, and He was still fully Yahweh. It was humility, not weakness. When you don't know what's coming, you can trust the Father the way He did.

senior.open: The title asks whether the Son could truly not know the hour. Scripture says yes (Mark 13:32), and it also says He knows all things. Both are true because He emptied Himself and took a real human life, without ever ceasing to be Yahweh.
senior.close: So the answer holds together. The Son truly did not name the hour, by taking the servant's form and keeping the Father's order, never by lacking deity. That same mind of trust is ours to carry when the timing is withheld from us.

ll152-crying-because-of-all-the-dying-sl.reason: Opens by settling that tears are not a failure of faith, but only hints why it feels that way; the 'where this lands' summary is good yet the lesson ends on an open question (Believest thou this?).
ll152-crying-because-of-all-the-dying-sl.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Why does grief over slow loss feel like failure? Because grieving believers are often told to stop, and because a slow loss gets renamed until no one else seems to mourn it. But the Word says the tears are not failure. Jesus wept, and those who sigh and cry are the ones marked (Ezekiel 9:4). Here is what Scripture says about the tears, the cause, and Yahweh's patience.
ll152-crying-because-of-all-the-dying-sl.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Grief over slow loss can feel like failure, but it is not. The tears are Christlike, and He keeps them in His bottle (Psalms 56:8). The slow dying is rejected knowledge compounding; Yahweh's slowness is longsuffering, holding the door open for repentance (2 Peter 3:9). So sorrow, but not as those with no hope. Let the grief become fuel to put true knowledge before people, with compassion, carried by the joy of the LORD as your strength, until death is swallowed up in victory.

teen.open: Ever feel like being sad about someone slowly dying means your faith is weak? It doesn't. Jesus cried too, and Yahweh notices every tear.
teen.close: So your tears are not failure. Yahweh is patient because He wants people to turn and live. Let your sadness push you to help others with the truth, and lean on His joy as your strength.

senior.open: The title asks why grief over a slow loss can feel like failure. Often it is because grieving believers are told to stop. Scripture answers otherwise: Jesus wept, and those who sigh and cry are the ones Yahweh marks.
senior.close: So the grief is no failure of faith. The slow loss comes from knowledge rejected, while Yahweh's own slowness is mercy leaving room to turn. We sorrow with hope, and His joy remains our strength.

ll153-precept-upon-precept-the-voice-tha.reason: Builds the program picture section by section; the home and the 'program or Word' answer (the Word runs like a program, the Author is a Person) only surfaces in the last two sections and is never stated plainly.
ll153-precept-upon-precept-the-voice-tha.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Does your home run on a program, or on a Word? The lesson's answer is that the Word is the program, and the Programmer is a Person. Yahweh spoke the world into ordered lines, still upholds it by the word of His power (Hebrews 1:3), and trains people the same way: precept upon precept, line upon line (Isaiah 28:10). A home runs well when it reads His Word and runs each line. Here is how the Word shows it.
ll153-precept-upon-precept-the-voice-tha.example: ONE LINE, READ AND RUN. Say a family reads Deuteronomy 6:7 and decides to run it, not just admire it. At breakfast one verse is read aloud. On the drive, someone says what it means. At bedtime a child says it back. Read from the top, jump to the line the day needs, then do it. The same rain and wind come to every house; the only variable is whether the line executes, and that is the house on the rock (Matthew 7:24).
ll153-precept-upon-precept-the-voice-tha.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Does your home run on a program, or on a Word? On a Word that runs like a program. The same Voice that spoke and it stood fast, that still holds every loop and every shoreline in place, writes people precept upon precept. Your part is the operator's: read from the top, jump to the line the moment needs, and run it, a doer and not a hearer only (James 1:22). And the Author is no machine. He loves the world He wrote, and He wrote you.

teen.open: Does your home run on a program or on a Word? Yahweh's Word works like a program: He spoke and the world ran, and He trains you one line at a time.
teen.close: So your home runs best on His Word. Read a line, then actually do it. And remember, Yahweh isn't a machine. He's a Person who loves you.

senior.open: The title asks whether a home runs on a program or on a Word. The lesson answers that Yahweh's Word works like an ordered program: He spoke the world into being, still upholds it, and trains hearts precept upon precept.
senior.close: So the answer is the Word, run line upon line. A household is kept in order the way He keeps the world, by hearing each line and doing it, while honouring the living Author who wrote it.

ll154-why-do-we-have-to-pay-for-our-fath.reason: Opens with the two-part answer (we don't pay; it needs what we do here), then Ezekiel 18:20; the tenth section restates the whole answer in order and ends on the Father running to the son who turns.

ll156-teach-yourself-anything-qualitativ.reason: Opens on the directive and Proverbs; the actual yes-and-how (the six-step loop of what kind, how much, compare, test, hold, repeat) is not assembled until the fifth section.
ll156-teach-yourself-anything-qualitativ.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Can you teach yourself anything? Yes, if you learn the way the Word lays it out. Start in the fear of the LORD. Ask what kind a thing is (that is qualitative), ask how much of it there is (that is quantitative), compare it to what you know, test it, hold what survives, and go again. Yahweh gives wisdom liberally to the one who asks and searches (James 1:5). Here is the method, Word first.
ll156-teach-yourself-anything-qualitativ.example: ONE BUDGET, EIGHT QUESTIONS. Say you pick the family budget. Qualitative: What is it? What kinds of spending are in it? What is it like and unlike last year? What is it for? Quantitative: How many bills? How much is each? How often does each come? Compared to what comes in? Answer the ones you can, search out the rest, and keep every figure honest, because a false balance is an abomination (Proverbs 11:1). Then put it in front of someone who will sharpen it (Proverbs 27:17).
ll156-teach-yourself-anything-qualitativ.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Can you teach yourself anything? Yes. The lesson gave you the loop: pick the thing, ask what kind until you can describe it to a child, ask how much until every part has a number, compare, prove all things and hold fast the good, then go again, line upon line. Keep your measures honest and let others sharpen your work. Do it heartily, as to the Lord, and competence grows while you stay a worshipper.

teen.open: Can you teach yourself anything? Yes. Ask what something is and what kind it is, then ask how much and how many. Test what you think, keep what holds, and go again.
teen.close: So yes, you can teach yourself anything this way. Ask, measure, test, keep the good, repeat. And do it for Yahweh, thanking Him for the mind He gave you.

senior.open: The title asks whether a person can teach himself anything. The lesson says yes: begin in the fear of the LORD, ask what kind a thing is and how much of it there is, then prove it and hold fast the good.
senior.close: So the answer is yes, by a patient loop: describe, measure, compare, test, keep, repeat, line upon line. Done heartily as to the Lord, it builds real competence and keeps the learner a worshipper.

ll157-what-is-love-in-depth-and-in-range.reason: Right after the directive, section one answers plainly (love is fifteen things a person does or declines to do, never a feeling); the close restates the whole answer and ends on 'do the next verb'.

ll155-yahweh-his-name-and-why-this-house.reason: Opens on Exodus 3:15 (my name for ever) but never says a plain 'no'; the core of the answer (god is a shared category, a name cannot be shared) only arrives in section two. The ending lands well.
ll155-yahweh-his-name-and-why-this-house.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Is Yahweh just one name among many? No. The word god is a category, and the Word itself uses it of judges, idols, the serpent's bait and even a departed spirit. Yahweh is not a category; it is His own name, given by Him for ever (Exodus 3:15), the One whose name alone is most high over all the earth (Psalms 83:18). He alone is the first and the last. Here is how the Word shows it.
ll155-yahweh-his-name-and-why-this-house.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Is Yahweh just one name among many? No. A category word can be shared by judges, idols and the fallen; a name cannot. He gave His name for ever, no god was formed before Him and none after (Isaiah 43:10), and the Son says the same of Himself (Revelation 22:13). So in our own voice we say Yahweh, never editing His Word to do it, so every listener knows exactly whom we mean. And His name is a strong tower the righteous run into (Proverbs 18:10).

teen.open: Is Yahweh just one name among many? No. Lots of things get called a god, but Yahweh is His own name, and He alone is the first and the last.
teen.close: So we say Yahweh on purpose. It makes clear exactly who we mean, the only One with no beginning and no end, and His name is a safe place to run.

senior.open: The title asks whether Yahweh is simply one name among many. The Word answers no: the generic word is a category used of judges, idols and the fallen, while Yahweh is the name He gave for Himself, for ever.
senior.close: So the answer is plain. Yahweh is not one name among many but the name of the only One who is first and last. We say it in our own voice for clarity, while quoting His Word exactly as written.

ll158-how-the-worlds-were-made-the-whole.reason: First paragraph gives the shape (one week, seven days, one Voice), section two says the answer is one word, He spoke, and the ending recites the whole order day by day and lands it.

ll159-we-are-all-children-of-yahweh-no-m.reason: The first paragraph states the answer outright (no matter how old we get, for ever children to Him), and the close gathers all ten sections and ends on that same sentence and a prayer to say Father.

ll160-pride-is-not-worth-him-and-is-ego-.reason: Opens on the cost of pride; the answer to the title (a sober self is commanded, pride is the self cut loose from its Maker, 'knowledge without the towel') only arrives in section six, and it ends on 'not worth Him'.
ll160-pride-is-not-worth-him-and-is-ego-.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Is pride just confidence gone too far? No. The Word commands you to think of yourself soberly, with a true measure (Romans 12:3), so knowing who you are is not pride. Pride is the self lifted above its measure and cut loose from its Maker: my power, my hand (Deuteronomy 8:17). Jesus knew all things were given into His hands, and took a towel. Pride is that knowledge without the towel. Here is how the Word shows it.
ll160-pride-is-not-worth-him-and-is-ego-.example: TWO SENTENCES AFTER A GOOD YEAR. Say a man has the best year his business has ever had. One sentence can form in him: my power and the might of my hand got me this. Or another: what do I have that I did not receive? (1 Corinthians 4:7). The year is the same size either way. The difference is whose hand gets the credit and what he does next. The first reaches for honour; the second gives thanks and serves someone in a way nobody will credit him for.
ll160-pride-is-not-worth-him-and-is-ego-.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Is pride just confidence gone too far? No. A sober, true knowledge of who you are is commanded, and a man who says he is nothing contradicts the price paid for him. Pride is something else: a heart lifted up that forgets who gave every gift, the Pharisee praying with himself, the king on his roof. Yahweh resists it and gives grace to the humble (James 4:6). So know who you are, give Him the credit, and take the towel. Pride is not worth Him.

teen.open: Is pride just being too confident? Not exactly. Knowing who you are is good. Pride is forgetting that everything you have came from Yahweh and lifting yourself above others.
teen.close: So confidence isn't the problem. Pride is taking the credit and forgetting the Giver. Jesus knew who He was and still washed feet. Do the same, and Yahweh gives you grace.

senior.open: The title asks whether pride is merely confidence carried too far. Scripture draws the line differently: a sober, true estimate of oneself is commanded, while pride is the self lifted above its measure and cut loose from its Maker.
senior.close: So pride is not excess confidence but a false account that forgets every gift was received. The remedy is the mind of Christ, who knew all was in His hands and took up a towel.

ll161-one-source-of-truth-his-voice-in-h.reason: The opening directive answers plainly (one source of truth: His voice in His Word, true as a Person), and the close restates every part (be still, love covers, stop judging, pray, build, move) before the evening practice.

ll162-do-not-take-a-death-so-personal-th.reason: Opens on the spoken directive; the answer (kept anger becomes a root that stops your feet; Job trusted, David kept walking) is spread across sections four to six; ends on a recap and a tonight step.
ll162-do-not-take-a-death-so-personal-th.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Your grief is real, but is your anger steering you off the road home? It can. The hurt is allowed and expected, and Jesus Himself wept. But anger at Yahweh that you keep, night after night and year after year, becomes a root of bitterness that stops your feet. Job and David grieved hard and kept trusting and walking. Here is how the Word shows it.
ll162-do-not-take-a-death-so-personal-th.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Is your anger steering you off the road home? Only if you keep it. Weep, and tell Him the anger honestly, because He would rather hear it than have it hidden. Then do what Job did and trust Him though He slay you, and what David did and wash your face and keep walking toward the one you lost. He is still Him, so what He said still stands. Let Him be Him, and the road home stays open.

teen.open: It is okay to hurt when someone dies, and even Jesus cried. The real question is whether staying angry at Yahweh will make you stop following Him.
teen.close: So be honest with Him about the hurt and the anger, but do not hold onto it. Keep doing what He said, like David did. That keeps you on the road home.

senior.open: Grief after a death is real, and the Word honors it. The question this lesson asks is whether anger at Yahweh, held over the years, has quietly turned you from the road home.
senior.close: The answer is plain. Hurt is allowed, and anger may be poured out to Him, but kept anger becomes a root that stops our walking. Trust Him as Job did, rise as David did, and let Him be Him.

ll163-the-build-we-are-going-for-and-why.reason: Title asks why a church teaches fractions; the answer (the Word is the pattern, skill comes from Yahweh, an untaught generation is lost) is scattered over ten sections and fractions appear once near the end.
ll163-the-build-we-are-going-for-and-why.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Why would a church teach fractions? Because the Word itself names engineers, science and skilled work, and says the skill comes from Yahweh. Wisdom builds the house, and Knowledge fills the rooms, so the school teaches math inside the Word, never apart from it. And one untaught generation is all it takes to lose the way. Here is the blueprint the Word gives.
ll163-the-build-we-are-going-for-and-why.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Why would a church teach fractions? Because the pattern is His. Bezaleel was filled with wisdom and skill for his work, Daniel understood science, and Jesus grew in wisdom, stature and favor. A people is destroyed for lack of knowledge, and a whole generation can forget Him. So this house teaches every capable child the count and the Word together, from Little Learners up, so that each one grows whole and becomes a workman that needeth not to be ashamed.

teen.open: Why would a church teach math? Because the Word names builders and scientists, and it says their skill came from Yahweh.
teen.close: So math in this school is not off topic. It is part of growing the whole you, mind, body, spirit and friendships, with the Word under all of it.

senior.open: You may wonder why a house of faith teaches fractions. The Word answers by naming craftsmen and scholars, Bezaleel and Daniel among them, and by tracing their skill to Yahweh.
senior.close: So the answer holds. The church teaches mathematics because the pattern is His, because skill is His gift, and because a generation left untaught can forget Him entirely.

ll165-i-always-had-love-gratitude-measur.reason: Opens on the coworker story; what to count (the love that was always there, given by Yahweh) and the seat for the lonely only come clear in sections two, three and the coworker section; the ending practice does land it.
ll165-i-always-had-love-gratitude-measur.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. What would you count if someone asked about your family? Count the people Yahweh gave you, and above all the love that was there the whole way, because every good gift comes from Him. Then remember the one who has no one to count. Yahweh sets the solitary in families, so your count becomes a seat you make for them. Here is how the Word shows it.
ll165-i-always-had-love-gratitude-measur.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. What would you count if someone asked about your family? Count it honestly and do not un-see it: the people, the hard and interesting places, and the love that never left. Name Yahweh as the One who gave it, and give thanks in every thing. Then let the count turn outward. For the coworker with no contact, the answer is not sympathy but a seat on the team, because whoever does the will of the Father is brother, sister and mother.

teen.open: If someone asked about your family, what would you count? Count the people and the love Yahweh gave you, and remember the friend who has nobody.
teen.close: So count your blessings out loud and thank Yahweh for them. Then make room at your table for someone who is alone. That is a real family move.

senior.open: When someone asks about your family, the honest count is a measure of gratitude. The love you were given came from Yahweh, and He also sets the solitary in families.
senior.close: So the count you keep is not for pride. It is thanksgiving to the Giver, and it becomes a seat you offer to the one who has no family to name.

ll166-life-is-disrespectful-so-think-on-.reason: The why (unfiltered disrespect makes you what you rehearse) comes in section one, but how the Servant-King makes filtering possible is never said plainly; it is implied across sections three to seven; ends on a practice list.
ll166-life-is-disrespectful-so-think-on-.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Why does Yahweh say to filter what you think? Because life keeps pouring disrespect into you, and as a man thinks in his heart, so is he. Left unfiltered, you slowly become the evil version of yourself. The Servant-King makes the filter possible: your old self was crucified with Him, He bought you with His own blood, and He gives grace to the humble. Here is how the Word lays it out.
ll166-life-is-disrespectful-so-think-on-.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Your mind is being shaped whether you notice or not, so Yahweh tells you to guard the gate: think on what is true, honest, just, pure, lovely and of good report. You cannot do that by improving self; you deny self daily, because Christ lives in you. You are twice-bought, first made and then redeemed with His blood, so you do not take orders from whoever disrespected you last. Humble yourself under His mighty hand, and He keeps your mind in peace.

teen.open: Whatever you let into your head shapes who you become. Yahweh says to filter it, and Jesus, the King who served, gives you the strength to do it.
teen.close: So check your thoughts against Philippians 4:8 before you react. You belong to Jesus, who bought you with His blood, so rude people do not get to steer you.

senior.open: A mind left open to a disrespectful world will be shaped by it. Yahweh commands a filter, and the Servant-King, who bought us with His blood, is the One who makes that filter workable.
senior.close: So the answer stands. We filter our thoughts because we become what we rehearse, and we can do it because self was crucified with Christ and we belong to Him twice over.

ll164-our-voice-builds-as-his-voice-crea.reason: The yes (death and life are in the tongue; Adam named, Ezekiel prophesied as commanded) arrives in section six after long sections on perfect truth and prompts; the limit and the Son pattern come later still.
ll164-our-voice-builds-as-his-voice-crea.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Can your words build something real? Yes. Adam named the animals and the names stood, and death and life are in the power of the tongue. But your voice is obviously not just like His. Yahweh spoke and the worlds were made; your words build only what He breathes on. They build best when you test every question against His perfect Word and speak what the Father gives. Here is how the Word shows it.
ll164-our-voice-builds-as-his-voice-crea.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Can your words build something real? They can, the way Ezekiel prophesied as he was commanded and the breath came from Yahweh. So ask the Word rigorous questions, let any tool be a scribe and never the source, and add nothing to the text. Keep your mouth clean and your words few, because they will be weighed. Then speak what the Father gives, as the Son did, and your voice will build what lasts while you become, by beholding, more like Him.

teen.open: Can what you say actually build something? Yes, but only when your words follow what Yahweh already said in His Word.
teen.close: So ask the Word hard questions, keep your words clean, and say what He gives you. That is how your voice builds something real.

senior.open: The Word says death and life are in the power of the tongue, so our words do build. Yet our voice is not His, and it builds rightly only when it is tested against His perfect Word.
senior.close: So the answer is yes, with the line kept. Our words build what lasts when we search the Word carefully, add nothing to it, and speak only what the Father gives, as the Son did.

ll168-the-king-through-the-warriors-lens.reason: Who was watching (angels, Job 38:7) comes after a rendering note; what programming the mind does only arrives in section nine, after the warrior, furnace and double-minded sections.
ll168-the-king-through-the-warriors-lens.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Before the earth had a floor, who was already watching? The "sons of God," the beings we call angels, who shouted for joy when Yahweh laid its foundations, while He Himself stood outside it all as the One who framed it. And what happens when you program your mind with His Word? You are transformed by its renewing, you become single-minded, and you stand fast the way His spoken world stands fast. Here is how the Word shows it.
ll168-the-king-through-the-warriors-lens.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Before the earth had a floor, the "sons of God" were there to watch Yahweh speak it into being, and He held it all together then as He does now. That same King has given you His Word. When you put it in your mouth day and night and hide it in your heart, it rewrites your reactions and makes you one-minded, like the three men who settled their obedience before the fire. He spoke and the worlds stood fast; program your mind with His Word, and you stand fast too.

teen.open: Before the world existed, angels were already there, cheering as Yahweh made it. And when you fill your mind with His Word, it changes how you think and act.
teen.close: So pick one verse and say it every day this week. Yahweh spoke and the world stood strong, and His Word in your mind helps you stand strong too.

senior.open: The Word tells us the "sons of God," the angels, shouted for joy when Yahweh laid the foundations of the earth. It also tells us what His Word does when we let it reshape the mind.
senior.close: So the answer is twofold. Witnesses were present when He spoke the world into being, and that same Word, kept day and night, renews the mind until it is single and steady before Him.

ll169-pour-it-out-every-seat-worked-feed.reason: Opens on the directive and two rendering notes; the three whys (faithful in least becomes ruler over much, love is handed a flock, work as to the Lord) are spread over sections one, four and eight.
ll169-pour-it-out-every-seat-worked-feed.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Why does Yahweh promote the faithful worker, feed the flock, and call for full effort? He promotes the one who is faithful in the least seat, because that is how He builds anyone He will trust with more. He asks those who love Him to feed His sheep, because love is handed a flock. And He calls for full effort because you serve the Lord Christ, not men. Here is how the Word shows it.
ll169-pour-it-out-every-seat-worked-feed.example: ONE LADDER, EVERY SEAT. Darrell started at Rent-A-Center as an account manager, then became assistant manager, then general manager. He worked every position and came away with a story from each one. That is faithful in least, faithful in much, in a real life. And because he sat in every chair, he can know the state of the flock, which is the knowledge he now pours out to the people coming behind him.
ll169-pour-it-out-every-seat-worked-feed.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Why does every seat count? Because Yahweh promotes the one who is faithful over a few things, and the reward is a bigger trust, not a bonus. What you learn in each seat is meant to be poured out, fed willingly to people who want to understand the King, as Peter was told to feed His sheep. And full effort is simply obedience: you work heartily as to the Lord, and the doer is blessed in his deed. So be the best in this too.

teen.open: Why does every job matter, even the small ones? Because Yahweh trusts more to people who are faithful in little things, and He wants you to do it all for Him.
teen.close: So work hard wherever you are, share what you learn with others, and give Yahweh your best. Every seat you sit in counts.

senior.open: Every position a person holds is training. The Word says the one faithful in the least is trusted with much, and that love for Jesus is shown by feeding His sheep.
senior.close: So the answer holds across a whole working life. Be faithful in each seat, pour out what Yahweh taught you there, and give full effort as to the Lord, because the doer is the one who is blessed.

ll170-through-the-eyes-of-the-people-clo.reason: Title asks if witnesses would risk all on a story; the lesson never speaks of their deaths, but its answer (eyewitnesses, not fables; runaways who would not stop speaking) sits in section seven; ends on the sealed tomb.
ll170-through-the-eyes-of-the-people-clo.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Would the witnesses stake their lives on a story? The men who saw Him did not treat it as a story. Peter, who had run and denied Him, later wrote, "we have not followed cunningly devised fables," but were eyewitnesses. His doubting brothers came to believe, the frightened disciples could not stop speaking, and the burial details were things a hostile party could check. Here is the record, person by person.
ll170-through-the-eyes-of-the-people-clo.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Would the witnesses stake their lives on a story? These were not storytellers. They were a denier restored by name, brothers who did not believe until He was seen of James, a doubter given the nail prints to touch, and above five hundred people, most still alive to be asked. Men who once ran away said, "we cannot but speak the things which we have seen and heard." Their enemies sealed the stone, paid for a cover story, and never produced a body.

teen.open: Would people risk everything for a made-up story? The people closest to Jesus said plainly that they were not telling a story. They saw Him alive.
teen.close: Peter ran away, then could not stop talking about what he saw. His brothers went from doubt to belief. That is what real witnesses look like.

senior.open: It is fair to ask whether the witnesses could have been repeating a tale. The record shows a denier, doubting brothers and frightened followers all turned into steady eyewitnesses.
senior.close: So the answer is that they were not telling a story. They spoke what they had seen and handled, while most of the five hundred were still alive to confirm it, and no body was ever produced.

ll171-trend-it-against-the-shoreline-poi.reason: Long control-system teaching comes first; who holds the shoreline (Yahweh, by His settled Word) appears mid-lesson and what the trend says (fruit, direction over samples) later; ends on a seven-day practice.
ll171-trend-it-against-the-shoreline-poi.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Your life is charting something right now. What does the trend say about where you are heading? Look at the fruit, what actually reached reality, and look at the direction over time, not one bad day. And who holds the shoreline? Yahweh does. His Word is settled and does not move, so it is the fixed line you read your trend against. Here is how a control engineer and the Word both show it.
ll171-trend-it-against-the-shoreline-poi.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. What does your trend say about where you are heading? Read your fruit, not your intentions, against the one line that never moves: Yahweh holds the shoreline, and His Word is settled in heaven. He keeps the record with no gap between samples, and His voice behind you names the way rather than the crime. The path of the just shines more and more, so judge the slope, not today. There is no condemnation in reading the chart. Look at the gap, and turn.

teen.open: Your choices are drawing a line over time. Yahweh's Word is the fixed line you compare it to, and it never moves.
teen.close: So track one real habit for a week and check it against the Word. Do not beat yourself up. Just see the gap and turn back toward Him.

senior.open: Every life leaves a record, the way a building leaves a trend log. The Word teaches that Yahweh holds the fixed reference, His settled Word, and that fruit shows our true direction.
senior.close: So the answer is plain. Our heading is shown by our fruit over time, measured against His unmoving Word, and we read that record without condemnation, ready to turn where He shows the gap.

ll172-the-spirit-of-your-mind-dust-breat.reason: The plain answer (the spirit of your mind is what your thoughts come out of, so renewal starts there) sits in the second section; the closing summary and practice return to dust, breath and candle but not to the question.
ll172-the-spirit-of-your-mind-dust-breat.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Is your mind the real problem, or what is behind it? What is behind it. The spirit of your mind is not your thoughts; it is the settled disposition your thoughts come out of, and the heart is the seat they flow from. That is why the Word does not say think better thoughts. It says be renewed in the spirit of your mind. Here is how Yahweh built you, from dust and breath to the candle He set inside you.
ll172-the-spirit-of-your-mind-dust-breat.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Is your mind the real problem? The thoughts are only what comes out. Behind them is the spirit of your mind, and behind that the heart, which only Yahweh can fully search. So the fix is upstream: put off the old man, be renewed in the spirit of your mind, and put on the new. You are dust and His breath, and your spirit is the candle of the LORD searching your inward parts. Let His Word divide what you cannot, and the renewed mind will prove His will.

teen.open: Is the problem your thoughts, or something deeper? The Word says something deeper: the spirit of your mind, where your thoughts come from.
teen.close: So do not just try to think nicer thoughts. Ask Yahweh to renew you on the inside, and let His Word show you what is really going on in your heart.

senior.open: Many of us try to repair our thinking one thought at a time. The Word points behind the thoughts, to the spirit of the mind and the heart they flow from.
senior.close: So the answer is that the mind is not the root. The disposition behind it must be renewed, and Yahweh, who formed the spirit within us, searches the heart and renews the inward man day by day.

ll173-humility-is-the-strength-no-shame-.reason: Opens on certifications testimony and its limits; the yes (strength made perfect in weakness; the humble manager gets the real data) arrives at the thesis a third in; the end summary and final line do land it.
ll173-humility-is-the-strength-no-shame-.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Can being weak make you stronger at work and in life? Yes, when weak means humble. Yahweh said His strength is made perfect in weakness, so humility is the intake of strength, not its price. At work, the humble manager hears the real data and finds the real cause. Failure carries no shame for you, and your feelings are allowed to catch up later. Here is how the Word shows it.
ll173-humility-is-the-strength-no-shame-.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Can being weak make you stronger? Paul says, "when I am weak, then am I strong." Humility is thinking soberly about yourself, so you can be wrong, learn the real cause, and fix the real thing. When something goes wrong, keep the sorrow that gets up and acts, refuse the shame, and do not let the event author you, because you are His workmanship. Recall what is true and your feelings will follow. The strength shows up exactly where you stopped supplying your own.

teen.open: Can admitting you are weak actually make you stronger? Yes. Yahweh says His strength works best right where yours runs out.
teen.close: So when you mess up, skip the shame. Ask what you can learn, and keep going. Your feelings will catch up, and Yahweh will make you strong.

senior.open: It sounds backward that weakness could strengthen anyone. The Word teaches that it does when weakness becomes humility, because His strength is made perfect there.
senior.close: So the answer is yes. The humble person hears the truth, learns from failure without shame, lets feelings follow faithfulness, and finds that Yahweh supplies strength exactly where self-reliance ends.

ll174-the-levels-of-disrespect-and-the-g.reason: Opens on a list of what will be covered; the answer (His name is His published character, so careless words misstate Him, as with Malachi's priests and Job's friends) is spread across the name, levels and gap sections.
