senior.open: Scripture recorded long ago what happens when a land loses its smiths. It also tells us how to rebuild: count the cost first, prepare the field before the house, and place our trust in the right hands.
senior.close: So the answer is this. Count honestly, prepare patiently, and build the means of defence well, while knowing that no capacity is the same thing as safety. Safety is of the LORD.

ll217-the-holy-spirit-brings-a-sound-min.reason: Darrell's directive states the answer up front and THE WHOLE restates it, but the lesson never names the title's noise directly and its last lines drift into family prompts rather than the answer.
ll217-the-holy-spirit-brings-a-sound-min.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Is your mind running on noise? If it is, that confusion is not coming from Yahweh, because He is not the author of confusion (1 Corinthians 14:33). The Holy Spirit gives a sound mind: clear, self-governed thinking. He brings clarity by bringing the Word home to you, and the eyes of your heart open as His words enter. Every source outside the Word, however spiritual it sounds, has no light in it.
ll217-the-holy-spirit-brings-a-sound-min.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Is your mind running on noise? Then treat the noise as a warning light, not a doorway to depth. The Holy Spirit gives power, love and a sound mind. He teaches by bringing back what Jesus said, and He turns your eyes to the Father and the Son, never to yourself. The light enters with His words, so the eyes of your heart see by the Word and by nothing else. Turn from the counterfeits, take up the Word, and ask for wisdom. He gives it liberally.

teen.open: If your head feels full of noise and confusion, that is not Yahweh. The Holy Spirit gives a clear, steady mind, and He does it through His Word.
teen.close: So when your mind is loud, go to the Word. The Holy Spirit uses it to clear the noise and help you see what is true.

senior.open: Many minds today run on a steady hum of confusion. The Word says plainly that confusion does not come from Yahweh, and that the Holy Spirit gives a sound mind instead.
senior.close: So the answer is this. Confusion is a warning, not a sign of depth. The Holy Spirit brings clarity through the Word alone, and the heart sees rightly when the Word is what it sees by.

ll218-do-not-switch-up-on-his-way-yahweh.reason: Never says plainly why things fall apart under pressure; the reasons (bending costly principles, double-mindedness, carried offense, building on sand) are scattered through five sections.
ll218-do-not-switch-up-on-his-way-yahweh.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Why do good plans fall apart under pressure? Usually not because we abandon Yahweh outright, but because we adjust Him: we keep the principles that cost nothing and bend the ones that cost something. Often an offense we picked up becomes the reason. The bending does not stay in one place; a double minded man is unstable in all his ways (James 1:8). What holds is His Way, written down and hidden in the heart, with the fight left to Him.
ll218-do-not-switch-up-on-his-way-yahweh.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Why do good plans fall apart under pressure? Because under pressure we switch up, and the house we built on the mood of the moment cannot stand the storm. Holding steady is simpler than bending. Yahweh does not change, so stand on Him. Write His Way down and hide it in your heart so it cannot be renegotiated in the dark. Put offense down, because the Judge has the case. And let Him win the fight. The house on the rock stood, and that is how we win.

teen.open: Why do people cave when things get hard? Usually they bend the rules that cost them something. That one bend makes everything shaky.
teen.close: So do not switch up. Yahweh never changes, so stand on Him, let offenses go, and let Him fight for you. That is how you stay standing.

senior.open: Plans and convictions rarely collapse all at once. The Word shows they give way when we start adjusting the principles that cost us something, often after an offense we chose to carry.
senior.close: So the answer is clear. Things fall apart when we switch up under pressure. They hold when we stand on the unchanging Yahweh, keep His Way written in the heart, release offense, and let Him win.

ll219-prudence-and-leaning-not-on-our-ow.reason: Opens on the loop (leaning on Him tells you to be careful), but why our understanding cannot carry full weight (His is infinite, higher in kind) waits for section four; ends on a measuring warning and prompts.
ll219-prudence-and-leaning-not-on-our-ow.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Why does Yahweh say not to trust your own understanding? Because His understanding is infinite and ours is not; His ways are higher than ours by the distance of the heavens from the earth (Isaiah 55:9). That is a difference of kind, not of effort. The command is not to stop thinking. It is to stop putting your full weight on your own thinking. And leaning on Him is the very thing that tells you to think carefully.
ll219-prudence-and-leaning-not-on-our-ow.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Why does Yahweh say not to trust your own understanding? Because your understanding is a rung you have not fully tested, and His is the highest authority in every dimension. Lean on Him, and He directs your paths into careful steps: count it before you commit, hear it before you answer, look at the real state rather than your memory of it, and prove it against one standard that does not move. Leaning on Him is not the end of thinking. It is what makes your thinking prudent.

teen.open: Why not just trust your own smarts? Because Yahweh sees everything and you do not. Leaning on Him actually makes you more careful, not less.
teen.close: So lean on Yahweh, not just your own thinking. Then count the cost, listen first, check what is real, and test your work honestly.

senior.open: Proverbs 3:5 is often heard as a call to stop thinking. It is not. It warns against resting our full weight on our own understanding, because His understanding is infinite.
senior.close: So the reason is plain. His Knowledge is the highest authority, and ours is limited. Leaning on Him leads to prudence: counting, hearing, looking at the real state, and proving our work by one honest measure.

ll220-every-thought-captured-and-tested-.reason: The answer (you choose, by capturing and testing each thought against His Word) is buried mid-sentence in a long directive and only made practical in section eleven; ends on the honest limit and prompts.
ll220-every-thought-captured-and-tested-.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Who chooses your thoughts? You do. Thousands of thoughts arrive in a day, and you cannot stop them arriving, but you can choose what is allowed to stay. You notice a thought, test it against Philippians 4:8, take it captive to Christ instead of arguing with it, and turn to a verse already hidden in you. And you read the Word daily, so His thoughts, not your old assumptions about Him, set the standard.
ll220-every-thought-captured-and-tested-.example: ONE THOUGHT IN A KITCHEN. Say a thought arrives while you are washing dishes: a sharp remark about someone who hurt you. Notice it instead of letting it pass unseen. Test it: it may be true, but is it lovely, is it of good report? Capture it rather than rehearse the argument. Redirect to a verse you have hidden in your heart. The whole sequence takes less time than the dishes, and that thought does not go down into the deep part to begin becoming you.
ll220-every-thought-captured-and-tested-.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Who chooses your thoughts? You do, under Christ. The carnal mind cannot govern itself, so each thought is handled by custody, not conversation: notice it, test it, capture it, redirect it. Whatever you allow inside becomes who you are, because as a man thinks in his heart, so is he. So keep His Word highest by reading it every day for the gaps between what He said and what you assumed. Most thoughts will slip past. The ones you catch are the ones that would have shaped you.

teen.open: Who decides what you think about? You do. Thoughts pop up all day, but you get to choose which ones stay.
teen.close: So catch the thought, test it with Philippians 4:8, and swap it for something true from the Word. What you keep thinking is what you become.

senior.open: We cannot stop thoughts from arriving, but the Word says we can decide which ones stay. That choosing is the work of capturing and testing each thought by His Word.
senior.close: So the answer is that you choose, with His help. Notice, test, capture and redirect, and read the Word daily so His meaning, not our assumption, keeps the highest place in the heart.

ll221-owning-the-light-instead-of-rentin.reason: The verdict on the bargain (it can be, at your own rate, if you count the cash price and total repayment) is assembled from sections six, seven and twelve; ends on the talk prompts, not the answer.
ll221-owning-the-light-instead-of-rentin.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Is solar really a bargain? It can be, but only when you count it honestly. Owning replaces a rising bill that leaves nothing in your hand, yet payback depends mostly on your own electricity rate, and a low loan rate can hide a dealer fee added to what you owe. Risk is in all things. So count the real cost, carry the risk honestly, and let His Wisdom have the last word.
ll221-owning-the-light-instead-of-rentin.example: THE PRICE OF A TWO PERCENT RATE. The lesson works it out. A system has a cash price of $26,000. The low-rate loan carries a dealer fee of twenty-five percent, so the amount financed becomes $32,500, and interest runs on that larger number for the whole term. The low rate was bought with your own principal. That is why the two questions come first: what is the cash price in writing, and what is the total repayment, not the rate?
ll221-owning-the-light-instead-of-rentin.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Is solar really a bargain? For some families it is, and for others it is not, and the five kitchen-table questions tell you which: the cash price in writing, the total repayment rather than the rate, the payback at your own rate, what happens if you move or the roof needs work, and counsel from someone who earns nothing either way. Count it as Luke 14:28 commands. Then hold the plan loosely, because the light was His before it was yours, and His Wisdom decides.

teen.open: Is buying solar panels a good deal? Sometimes. It depends on the real total cost and what your family pays for power now.
teen.close: So solar can be a good deal, but only if you count everything honestly first. Then ask Yahweh for wisdom before you sign anything.

senior.open: Owning solar instead of renting power can save a family money, but the brochure rarely tells the whole story. This lesson counts the cost honestly and lets His Wisdom govern the decision.
senior.close: So the answer depends on honest arithmetic: the cash price, the total repayment, and payback at your own rate. Weigh those with counsel, acknowledge the risk, and let Yahweh direct the steps.

ll223-the-storm-you-can-see-coming-and-t.reason: Frames the question in section one, but what a warning asks (act on all of it before it lands; in judgment, search both sides) is only stated in WHAT BOTH STORIES ASK OF YOU near the end.
ll223-the-storm-you-can-see-coming-and-t.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. What do warnings ask you to do before it is too late? They ask you to act, and to act fully. A prudent man sees the trouble coming and takes cover; the simple walk on and are punished (Proverbs 22:3). Noah did all that he was commanded, not the part that suited him. And when a life or a reputation is in the balance, a warning asks you to search the matter carefully before you settle it.
ll223-the-storm-you-can-see-coming-and-t.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. What do warnings ask you to do before it is too late? For the storm you can see coming, name it and do the one prudent thing before it lands, all of it, because the same storm hits both houses and only the foundation differs. For the small courts you hold every week, hear the other side before the first version settles into a verdict. Do justly, love mercy, and walk humbly, as Micah 6:8 says. That is what a warning asks, and it asks it now.

teen.open: When you get a warning, what are you supposed to do? Act on it, all the way, before the trouble arrives.
teen.close: So when you see a storm coming, do the wise thing now, not later. And before you judge someone, hear their side first.

senior.open: A warning given in advance is a mercy, but only if it is acted on. The Word asks two things of anyone warned: prudent action, and careful judgment.
senior.close: So the answer is plain. Act on the warning fully before it is too late, and in every judgment you hold, search the matter before you decide, as Micah 6:8 asks.

ll224-accountability-every-soul-answers-.reason: The opening paragraph answers well (every soul answers, sized to what was given, with mercy), but the lesson ends on a to-do list and family prompts instead of landing who answers and how much.
ll224-accountability-every-soul-answers-.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Who gets held accountable, and how much? Every soul: man, woman and child, each for himself, before the One who sees every secret thing. How much is sized to what you were given; more given, more required, less given, less required, never nothing. Teachers and leaders answer at the higher level. And because whom the Lord loves He corrects, accountability is not a threat. Confess, forsake, keep the practice daily, and grace lets you look straight at your account and be forgiven.

teen.open: Who has to answer to Yahweh? Everyone, including kids. But He asks each person only about what they were given.
teen.close: So you are accountable too, at your size. Own what you did, tell Yahweh, and let a friend help you stay on track. His grace covers you.

senior.open: Teaching on accountability often aims only at those in charge. The Word gives every soul an account, sized to what each was given, with mercy to make it bearable.
senior.close: So the answer is this. Every soul answers to Yahweh, in proportion to what was entrusted to it, and those who lead answer more. Grace makes honest accounting possible, and daily practice keeps us submitted.

ll222-the-only-incorruptible-one-every-o.reason: Darrell's directive holds the answer in his words, but the plain answer (only Yahweh is incorruptible; everything else holds because He holds it) waits until section five; ends on his prayer and prompts.
ll222-the-only-incorruptible-one-every-o.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Can anything be trusted to hold? Only Yahweh holds on His own. Every other being, angels and humans, was corruptible, and fell wanting to be as wise as He is. Yet the chair you sit on and the air you breathe do hold, because all things consist by Him (Colossians 1:17). So you already trust Him every moment. His proof of goodness is not a command shouted at you, but an invitation: taste and see.
ll222-the-only-incorruptible-one-every-o.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Can anything be trusted to hold? Nothing in creation holds by itself; the angels fell and so did we, corrupted by wanting to be the one who knows. Only Yahweh is incorruptible, and everything else holds because He holds it. He is light with no darkness at all, and He is proving it on the road: letting wheat and tares grow until harvest, working patience, experience and hope through the turmoil. He can be trusted to hold. Taste and see that the LORD is good.

teen.open: Can anything really be trusted? Only Yahweh never fails. Everything else, even angels, went wrong somewhere.
teen.close: So trust the One who holds everything together. Yahweh is good with no darkness in Him, and He invites you to taste and see.

senior.open: Every created thing, however high, has proven corruptible. The Word names one exception: Yahweh alone, who never changes, and by whom all things hold together.
senior.close: So the answer is that only He can be trusted to hold, and He is proving His goodness through the very road we walk. The fitting response is the one Darrell gave: thanks to the King.

ll216-a-life-full-of-everything-yahweh-i.reason: The answer sits in the heading and Darrell's quoted directive, but 3 John 1:2 and the soul-first order are only taught in the sixth section; the final lines turn to family prompts.
ll216-a-life-full-of-everything-yahweh-i.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Can you prosper when your soul leads the way? Yes. In fact, that is the order Yahweh wills: that you prosper and be in health even as your soul prospers (3 John 1:2). The soul comes first and the rest follows it. He helps make things happen after His Will is done, and consistency in His Word is the key that keeps the soul prospering, through every season of a full life.
ll216-a-life-full-of-everything-yahweh-i.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Can you prosper when your soul leads the way? That is the only way the Word describes it. A full life holds pain and success alike, and Yahweh is good in every season of it. Seek His Will first, and the additions follow. Stay planted in the Word day and night, filling the mind with His thoughts until lesser mindsets have no room. Let the soul prosper first. The rest is His to add, and He adds it.

teen.open: Can you really do well in life by putting your soul first? Yes. Yahweh wants you to do well in the same way your soul is doing well.
teen.close: So put your soul first. Read the Word every day, put His Will before yours, and trust Yahweh to add the rest.

senior.open: A long life holds every kind of season. Through all of them, the Word sets one order for prosperity: the soul first, and the rest following as the soul prospers.
senior.close: So the answer is yes, and in that order. Yahweh is good in every season, consistency in His Word keeps the soul prospering, and what we need He adds after His Will is done.

ll225-spiritual-knowledge-is-the-most-im.reason: Section one answers early (the soul is the measure, 3 John 1:2), but the lesson ends on a to-do list and family prompts rather than returning to whether money is the measure of a good life.
ll225-spiritual-knowledge-is-the-most-im.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Is money the measure of a good life? No. The Word measures prosperity by the soul (3 John 1:2), and a man's life does not consist in what he owns (Luke 12:15). The most important factor is spiritual Knowledge of Yahweh and His ways. Money comes in a season with Him, and He gives the power to get it, but a lean season is a season, not a verdict.
ll225-spiritual-knowledge-is-the-most-im.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Is money the measure of a good life? It is not. Wisdom and money both defend, but only wisdom gives life. Joseph was called a prosperous man in a prison before he ever held a coin, because the LORD was with him. So measure your life by the soul first, get spiritual Knowledge on purpose, work heartily in the lean season, and when plenty comes, say where it came from and give the first part back. The highest quality of life is a soul submitted to Him, with money or without it.

teen.open: Is having money what makes a life good? No. The Bible says the real measure is how your soul is doing with Yahweh.
teen.close: So money is not the scoreboard. Knowing Yahweh is. With a lot or a little, a life close to Him is a good life.

senior.open: Our age weighs a life by its bank balance. The Word weighs it by the soul, and ranks spiritual Knowledge as the most important factor of all.
senior.close: So the answer is no. A good life is measured by a prospering soul. Lean seasons and full ones both come from His hand, and in either one, Knowledge of Him is what gives life.

ll226-the-mind-of-christ-is-our-identity.reason: Opens on a long rendering of Darrell's directive; identity, where you stand and where nations are headed are answered across sections three, four, six and seven, and the end drifts to a to-do list.
ll226-the-mind-of-christ-is-our-identity.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. How does the Mind of Christ shape who you are, where you stand, and where every nation is headed? It is who you are: an identity handed to you, not one you go looking for (1 Corinthians 2:16). It is where you stand: in the whole armour, focused on the mission, in your own lane, with a sound mind the Holy Spirit gives. And it shows where the nations are going: into His Kingdom Ways. Your mind is the battlefield, and this is how you hold it.
ll226-the-mind-of-christ-is-our-identity.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. How does the Mind of Christ shape who you are, where you stand, and where every nation is headed? Ego wars against the mind, but the Mind of Christ is your identity: humble, obedient, renewed. You stand in the whole armour with the Word as your sword, taking every thought captive, staying in the lane you were called in. And you stand inside the direction of history: all nations flowing into His ways, a host from every people in the body He died to make. The battle is real, and the outcome is already written.

teen.open: Your mind is where the real fight happens. The Mind of Christ tells you who you are, how to stand strong, and where the whole world is headed.
teen.close: So you already have the Mind of Christ. Put on the armour, catch bad thoughts, stay in your lane, and remember every nation is coming to Jesus.

senior.open: The mind is contested ground, and ego is the oldest enemy on it. The Word answers with an identity, a stance, and a direction for history, all found in the Mind of Christ.
senior.close: So the answer comes in three parts. The Mind of Christ is who we are, the whole armour and our own calling are where we stand, and His Kingdom Ways are where every nation is going.

ll227-read-the-word-for-the-spirit-do-th.reason: The opening names the gotcha reading and the better aim early, but the close is a to-do list and family prompts; the reader does not finish on why the Word gives life or what doing it produces.
ll227-read-the-word-for-the-spirit-do-th.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Are you reading to win an argument or to be changed? Read to be changed. Jesus said His words are spirit and life (John 6:63), and a living Word reads you while you read it. Reading to win produces a person who can quote and cannot follow. Reading to become better His Way, and then doing His Way, produces gracious speech and a growing skill for learning.
ll227-read-the-word-for-the-spirit-do-th.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Are you reading to win an argument or to be changed? The ones who searched the Scriptures to win knew the text and would not come to Him. The hearer who does not do deceives his own self. But the one who reads for the Spirit and then does the Word is like the man who dug deep and built on rock. His speech grows seasoned with grace, able to answer every man, and his learning increases. Open the Book to be changed. Then do what it says.

teen.open: Do you read the Bible to prove someone wrong, or to let it change you? It is meant to change you.
teen.close: So read to be changed, not to win. Then go do one thing it says, and your words and skills will grow from that.

senior.open: It is possible to know Scripture well and still miss the One it testifies of. This lesson asks why we open the Book: to win, or to be changed.
senior.close: So the answer is to read for the Spirit and then do the Word. The doing is what makes conversation gracious and learning sure, and the house built that way stands.

ll228-can-a-man-be-taught-by-a-woman-kno.reason: Opens on Darrell's question and the method; the plain answer (yes, the Word shows men learning from women; pride is what blocks it) only arrives in section six; ends on practice and talk-together.
ll228-can-a-man-be-taught-by-a-woman-kno.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Can a man learn from a woman? Yes. The Word shows a preacher mighty in the Scriptures, a king, and a high priest each receiving a true word about Yahweh from a woman. The order verses (1 Timothy 2:11-14; 1 Corinthians 14:34-35) stand as written, but they never say a man cannot learn from a woman. When a man cannot, the Word names the cause as pride, and knowing Him outranks any question about the messenger. Here is how the Word answers first.
ll228-can-a-man-be-taught-by-a-woman-kno.example: ONE MAN, ONE WIFE, ONE CORRECTION. Apollos was eloquent and mighty in the Scriptures, yet he knew only the baptism of John (Acts 18:24-25). Priscilla and her husband Aquila heard him, took him aside, and expounded the way of Yahweh to him more perfectly (Acts 18:26). He received it, and the Word records it without a word of rebuke. David did the same with Abigail and blessed the Lord, her advice, and her (1 Samuel 25:32-33). Neither man lost anything by learning. Both were kept from error.
ll228-can-a-man-be-taught-by-a-woman-kno.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Can a man learn from a woman? The whole Word says yes, and shows it: Apollos from Priscilla, David from Abigail, Josiah's men from Huldah, Timothy from Lois and Eunice. The order verses govern a woman teaching so as to usurp authority over the man and order in the churches, and they stand. They give no man a licence to refuse a true word about Him. What blocks that learning is pride, and Yahweh gives grace to the humble (James 4:6). Knowing Him is life eternal (John 17:3), so receive the truth about Him from whomever He sends.

teen.open: Can a guy learn about Yahweh from a woman? Yes. The Bible shows men doing it again and again, and it says pride is what gets in the way.
teen.close: So yes, a man can learn from a woman. Apollos did, David did, and Timothy did from his mom and grandma. If it feels hard, that is pride talking, and Yahweh helps the humble.

senior.open: The title asks whether a man can learn from a woman. The Word answers yes, by its own record, and it names pride, not the woman, as the thing that makes it hard.
senior.close: So the answer is plain. The order verses stand as written and govern what they say they govern, yet the Word shows kings, priests and preachers learning from women about Yahweh. Knowing Him matters most, and the humble receive it from whomever He sends.

ll229-the-word-is-spirit-and-life-what-i.reason: The answer is built across nine sections; the bread/seed/fire/sword pictures sit in section six and the one-line summary arrives only at the end of section nine before the practice list.
ll229-the-word-is-spirit-and-life-what-i.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. What does it mean that the Word gives life, and why read it for the Spirit? It means the Word is first a Person, Jesus, and the Scriptures are His words, breathed by the Holy Spirit. That living Word does what bread, seed, fire and a sword do: it feeds, grows, burns and cuts, and it raises what was dead in you. Read only as letters, it stays flesh and profits nothing (John 6:63). Read with the Spirit who breathed it, you meet Him. Here is how the Word says it of itself.
ll229-the-word-is-spirit-and-life-what-i.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. What does it mean that the Word gives life? The Word is Jesus, the Son of Yahweh, and His words were breathed by the same Spirit who breathed life into Adam and into Ezekiel's valley of bones. So they do not sit on a shelf: they feed like bread, grow like seed, clean like water, burn like fire, and cut like a sword. That is why you read it for the Spirit and not as letters only. When you let Him in, the Person on the page quickens, makes alive, what was dead in you.

teen.open: What does it mean that the Bible gives life? It means Jesus Himself is the Word, and when the Holy Spirit opens it to you, it actually changes you.
teen.close: So the Word gives life because it is Jesus speaking, breathed by the Holy Spirit. Read it like food, not homework, and let Him bring alive what feels dead in you.

senior.open: The title asks what it means that the Word gives life. The Lord's own answer is that His words are Spirit and life (John 6:63): the Word is a Person before it is a page, and the Spirit who breathed it is the One who opens it.
senior.close: So the meaning is this. The Word gives life because it is Jesus speaking by the Spirit, and it works like bread, seed, fire and a sword. Read for the Spirit, not the letter alone, it still quickens what was dead.

ll230-competence-before-submission-the-s.reason: The plain answer (neither skill arrives on the wedding day; both are built in the years before it) is stated only in the closing section on competence; ends on practice lists, not the answer.
ll230-competence-before-submission-the-s.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Can a wife or husband be ready before the wedding? Yes, and the Word expects it. A husband needs the study skill to wash his house with the Word (Ephesians 5:25-26) and the doing skill to work and rule his house well. A wife's chapter, Proverbs 31, is a list of study and doing skills too. Neither skill arrives on the wedding day. Both are built in the years before it, and weighed before the vow. Here is how the Word lays it out.
ll230-competence-before-submission-the-s.example: BUILT BEFORE THE VOW. Say a young man reads Ephesians 5 every week for two years until he can explain it in words a wife could actually hear, and he finishes work no one checks. Say a young woman marks the study verses and the doing verses in Proverbs 31 and builds one of each this year. When they meet, there is something to weigh, with counsel and in the Lord (Proverbs 15:22; 1 Corinthians 7:39). That is Proverbs 24:27 in a life: the work prepared first, then the house built.
ll230-competence-before-submission-the-s.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Can a wife or husband be ready before the wedding? The Word says yes, and it shows how. The study skill is learned by reading when no one is watching. The doing skill is learned by finishing work no one is checking. Ezra's order holds: seek it, do it, then teach it. Weigh one another before the vow, and keep growing after it. Tomorrow is not promised (Proverbs 27:1), so the skill is built today, and the house is built on it: Wisdom builds it, Understanding establishes it, Knowledge fills it (Proverbs 24:3-4).

teen.open: Can you get ready to be a good husband or wife now, before you ever marry? Yes. The Bible shows the skills, and you can start building them today.
teen.close: So yes, you can be ready before the wedding. Learn the Word when no one is watching, finish work no one is checking, and keep growing. Those skills do not show up on the wedding day.

senior.open: The title asks whether a wife or husband can be ready before the wedding. The Word's answer is yes: it names the study skills and doing skills of each, and puts the weighing of them before the vow.
senior.close: So the answer stands. Neither skill arrives on the wedding day; both are built in the years before it and keep growing after. A house built that way rests on Wisdom, Understanding and Knowledge, as Proverbs 24:3-4 describes.

ll231-does-yahweh-rank-a-wife-over-a-wom.reason: Section one answers plainly (a ring is not a rank; the fear of the LORD is), but the lesson ends on fruitful relationships, practice lists and talk-together rather than landing the rank question.
ll231-does-yahweh-rank-a-wife-over-a-wom.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Does a ring change your rank before Yahweh? No. He is no respecter of persons, and what He praises is the fear of the LORD (Proverbs 31:30), open to a wife, an unmarried woman, and every man on the same terms. Marriage is a gift and a calling, not a promotion. The Proverbs 31 woman runs real systems, and she still submits as unto the Lord, because order is about function, not worth. Here is how the Word shows each part.
ll231-does-yahweh-rank-a-wife-over-a-wom.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Does a ring change your rank before Yahweh? No. Acceptance with Him rests on fearing Him and working righteousness (Acts 10:34-35), and the woman Proverbs 31 praises is praised for that. Marriage is honourable, and so is the unmarried life given to the Lord. Inside marriage, a wife may be the more skilled of the two and still submit as unto the Lord, the way the Son submits to the Father and is not one degree less (1 Corinthians 11:3). Order is function between equals. Rank in His eyes is the fear of the LORD.

teen.open: Does getting married make you more important to Yahweh? No. What He looks at is whether you honor Him, married or not.
teen.close: So a ring does not raise your rank with Yahweh. Fearing Him does. A wife can be super skilled and still follow His order in marriage, the same way Jesus honors the Father without being less.

senior.open: The title asks whether a ring changes your rank before Yahweh. The Word says no: He is no respecter of persons, and the fear of the LORD is what He praises in a wife, a widow, or anyone.
senior.close: So the answer holds. Marriage is a gift, not a promotion. A capable wife submits as unto the Lord because of His order, not because she is less, just as the Son submits to the Father as an equal. Rank before Him is the fear of the LORD.

ll232-the-woman-at-the-well-and-the-sama.reason: Section two answers it (her saying opened the door; His own Word settled it, John 4:41-42), but the lesson moves through archaeology, sacrifices and kingship and ends on practice, not that answer.
ll232-the-woman-at-the-well-and-the-sama.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. One woman's testimony opened the door, but what settled a whole city? His own Word. Many Samaritans believed because of her saying (John 4:39). Then Jesus stayed two days, and many more believed because of His own word, and they told her they now knew for themselves that He is the Christ (John 4:41-42). Her testimony brought them; His Word settled it. The scroll they already held, the books of Moses, had pointed them to Him. Here is the whole account.
ll232-the-woman-at-the-well-and-the-sama.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. What settled a whole city? Not her saying alone, though the Word honours it by name. The Samaritans heard Him themselves, and His own Word settled it: this is indeed the Christ, the Saviour of the world (John 4:42). The scroll in their hands had already pointed to the Prophet like Moses, and no sacrifice on any mountain could do what the Lamb did once. That is the pattern for you too. Tell people what He has done, then put His Word in their hands, and let Him do what no testimony can.

teen.open: A woman told her whole town about Jesus, and many believed. But what really settled it for them? Hearing Jesus for themselves.
teen.close: So her story opened the door, but Jesus' own words settled it. Share what He has done for you, then point your friends to His Word so they can hear Him themselves.

senior.open: The title asks what settled a whole city. John 4 answers it: her testimony brought many, but many more believed because of His own word, and they said they now knew for themselves.
senior.close: So the answer is His own Word. Her saying opened the door and is honoured for it, but the Samaritans were settled by hearing Him. Our testimony brings people near; His Word is the Highest Authority that settles them.

ll233-yahweh-speaking-with-yahweh-every-.reason: The lesson gathers the passages well, but what the overheard conversation shows (love, delight, never a quarrel, and it is about us and open to us) is only drawn out in sections six and seven.
ll233-yahweh-speaking-with-yahweh-every-.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Have you ever overheard the conversation inside the Godhead? You can, because Yahweh let it be written down. The one LORD speaks within Himself: the counsel before creation, the Father's words to the Son in the Psalms and at the Jordan, the Son's prayers in John 17 and from the cross, and the Holy Spirit who hears and speaks. Listen, and it is never a quarrel. It is love and delight said out loud, and much of it is about you. Here is where the Word lets you listen.
ll233-yahweh-speaking-with-yahweh-every-.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Have you overheard the conversation inside the Godhead? Now you have. Before the world, He said, "Let us make man in our image" (Genesis 1:26). The Father says, "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased" (Matthew 3:17). The Son prays for you in John 17, and the Spirit intercedes for you with groanings (Romans 8:26). It is speech that gives, never speech that wins. And it is still going on, with a place in it for you: the Spirit of His Son in your heart, crying Abba, Father (Galatians 4:6).

teen.open: Did you know the Bible lets you listen in on the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit talking? It does, in lots of places.
teen.close: So yes, you can overhear Them. The Father delights in the Son, the Son prays for you, and the Spirit prays for you too. And you are invited in: you can call Him Abba, Father.

senior.open: The title asks whether we have overheard the conversation inside the Godhead. The Word records it, from the counsel in Genesis 1:26 to the Son's prayer in John 17 and the Spirit's intercession in Romans 8.
senior.close: So the conversation can be heard, and it is full of love, honour and delight, never rivalry. The Son still intercedes for you and the Spirit still prays for you, and through Him you have access to the Father.

ll234-will-we-have-angel-like-experience.reason: The opening states the three-part answer (like angels in some ways, never angels, like Him), and section three says plainly you will never be an angel; the ending moves to judgment, practice and talk-together.
ll234-will-we-have-angel-like-experience.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Will you become an angel when you die? No. Angels are a different order of His creatures, sent to serve the heirs of salvation (Hebrews 1:14), and the Son took on the seed of Abraham, not the nature of angels. Jesus named the likeness: the raised will not marry and cannot die (Luke 20:36). But the higher promise is this: you stay the very person you are, present with the Lord, and when He appears you will be like Him, with a body fashioned like His glorious body (1 John 3:2; Philippians 3:21). That is better than becoming an angel.

teen.open: Do people turn into angels when they die? The Bible says no. Something better is promised.
teen.close: So you will not become an angel. You stay you, with the Lord, and one day you get a body like Jesus' own. Angels actually serve and marvel at what Yahweh does for His people.

senior.open: The title asks whether we become angels when we die. Jesus said the raised are like the angels in two ways, no marriage and no death, but the Word never says we become them.
senior.close: So the answer is no, and the truth is better. The one who belongs to Him is kept as the very person they are, present with the Lord, waiting for a resurrection body made like His. That is the hope to grieve with and to live by.

ll237-his-knowledge-is-the-highest-and-t.reason: The title asks who decides which thoughts stay; the plain answer (you choose the tenants, measured against His Knowledge with Philippians 4:8) arrives only two-thirds through, and it ends on homework.
ll237-his-knowledge-is-the-highest-and-t.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. With roughly six thousand thoughts passing through a day, who decides which ones stay? You do, but not by your own measure. You cannot stop the traffic, but you choose what gets a room. The standard for choosing is His Knowledge, the highest and the Standard (2 Corinthians 10:5). Philippians 4:8 is the written test, and daily reading of His Word is how you see the gap between what He said and what you assumed. Here is how the Word lays it out.
ll237-his-knowledge-is-the-highest-and-t.example: ONE THOUGHT AT THE GATE. Say a thought arrives at work: I have to handle this my own way, no one else understands it. Notice it. Test it against the eight: is it true, honest, just, pure, lovely, of good report? It leans on your own understanding, which Proverbs 3:5 forbids. So it does not get a room. Capture it and redirect it: In all thy ways acknowledge Him, and He shall direct thy paths (Proverbs 3:6). One thought, four steps, and the tenant changes.
ll237-his-knowledge-is-the-highest-and-t.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Who decides which of your thoughts stay? You do, and the Word tells you how. You cannot govern what arrives, but you govern what gets a room. Measure each thought against His Knowledge, not your own understanding, and run it through Philippians 4:8: notice, test, capture, redirect. Read His Word daily to find the gaps between what He said and what you assumed. What you let in becomes who you are (Luke 6:45), so keep the gate with all diligence (Proverbs 4:23). His thoughts are higher than yours (Isaiah 55:9), and the mind stayed on Him is kept in perfect peace.

teen.open: Your brain runs through thousands of thoughts a day. Who decides which ones stay? You do, but you use Yahweh's Word as the measure, not your mood.
teen.close: So you choose which thoughts get to stay. Test them with Philippians 4:8: true, honest, pure, lovely. Keep the good ones, swap out the rest, and read the Word daily. What you let in becomes you.

senior.open: The title asks who decides which of our many daily thoughts are allowed to stay. The Word's answer is that we choose, but we choose by His Knowledge as the Standard, not by our own understanding.
senior.close: So the decision is ours, and the measure is His. Capture each thought, test it by Philippians 4:8, and read His Word daily to find where our assumptions differ from what He said. What we admit becomes who we are.

ll239-the-king-sits-down-first-a-shipyar.reason: Opens on the shipyard news and claims; the answer (count and consult, prepare the horse, but safety is of the LORD, Proverbs 21:31) arrives two-thirds through; ends on disclaimers and homework.
ll239-the-king-sits-down-first-a-shipyar.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. When billions are committed in one day, does counting the cost include counting on Yahweh for safety? Yes. Jesus says the builder and the king sit down first: they count the cost and they consult (Luke 14:28-31). Preparation is required. But the Word moves the credit off it: the horse is prepared against the day of battle, but safety is of the LORD (Proverbs 21:31). Honest counting writes down both. Here is how a shipyard announcement shows it.
ll239-the-king-sits-down-first-a-shipyar.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Does counting the cost include counting on Yahweh for safety? It does. Sit down first and count: the real cost, the measured record, not only the claims of those who gain from being believed. Consult a multitude of counsellors, not a narrow few (Proverbs 11:14). Then plan, holding tomorrow loosely, because the counsel of the LORD is what stands (Proverbs 19:21). Prepare the horse; it is in the verse and it is not optional. But never confuse the horse with the safety. Some trust in chariots and some in horses; remember the name of the LORD (Psalms 20:7).

teen.open: When people make huge plans, is counting the cost enough? The Bible says count it, get good advice, prepare well, and then trust Yahweh for the safety.
teen.close: So yes, counting the cost includes counting on Yahweh. Do your homework and get wise advice. But the safety comes from Him, not from how ready you are (Proverbs 21:31).

senior.open: The title asks whether counting the cost includes counting on Yahweh for safety. The Word answers yes: Jesus' king sits down to count and consult, and Proverbs 21:31 says the horse is prepared, but safety is of the LORD.
senior.close: So the answer stands. Count the real cost, seek many counsellors, and plan diligently without boasting of tomorrow. Then write under all of it who gives the safety. Preparation is our part; safety is His.

ll236-the-bill-you-cannot-read-honest-we.reason: The pieces of the answer (a bill you cannot read cannot be checked; the scale is Yahweh's; a reckoning should be plain) are spread across six sections after a long survey preamble; ends on talk-together.
ll236-the-bill-you-cannot-read-honest-we.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Can you read your own power bill? You should be able to, because a bill you cannot read is a bill you cannot check, and a cost you cannot check is carried on trust alone. Yahweh cares how things are measured because the scale is His: a just weight is His delight (Proverbs 11:1; 16:11). A meter is a scale, and the bill is its reading. And the first number in counting any cost is the one on your own bill. Here is how the Word shows it.
ll236-the-bill-you-cannot-read-honest-we.example: THE FIRST NUMBER. Say your bill shows 900 kilowatt-hours used and a total of $135 once the delivery charges, riders and taxes are added. Divide: $135 divided by 900 is 15 cents per kilowatt-hour. That is your own cost per unit, and it is the very first number any comparison of owning panels against renting power needs. Without it, the whole comparison runs on somebody else's figure. One evening with a bill, line by line, until you can say what each line is for.
ll236-the-bill-you-cannot-read-honest-we.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Can you read your own power bill? Make sure you can, line by line, until you can say what each line is for. The meter is a scale, and the scale is Yahweh's; a false balance is abomination to Him and a just weight is His delight. A reckoning is meant to be plain enough to read at a run (Habakkuk 2:2), and you cannot count a cost you cannot read (Luke 14:28). Keep the same honest weight in anything you bill to others. Then, with His Wisdom first, the reading, the counting and the decision can be trusted.

teen.open: Could you read your family's power bill? It matters, because you can't check what you can't read, and Yahweh cares a lot about honest measuring.
teen.close: So learn to read the bill. The meter is like a scale, and Yahweh says honest scales are His delight. You can't count a cost you can't read, so start there, and ask Him for Wisdom.

senior.open: The title asks whether you can read your own power bill. The Word gives the reason it matters: a meter is a scale, the scale is Yahweh's, and a reckoning is meant to be plain.
senior.close: So read the bill until every line is clear. It is the first step in counting any cost, and honest measuring is His delight. Keep that same honest weight in anything you bill to others, and let His Wisdom govern the decision.

ll240-he-said-it-and-did-not-do-it-the-o.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Did the promise fail? No. Yahweh said it and did not do it to Moses, because Moses stood in the breach. teen.open: Yahweh offered to make Moses into a great nation, and Moses said no. Did that mean the promise failed? Not at all.
teen.close: So the promise did not fail. Moses stood up for the people, the doubting adults missed out, and their kids, the ones they gave up on, got the land. Today Jesus stands in the gap for you.

senior.open: The title asks whether the promise failed when Moses refused Yahweh's offer in Numbers 14. The Word shows it did not: it was simply fulfilled another way than through Moses.
senior.close: So the answer is no. Moses' intercession turned the sudden judgment, that generation fell in the wilderness, and their children inherited the land. The same pattern is written for our warning, and Jesus now holds the breach and never leaves it.

ll241-advice-with-no-name-on-it-the-paid.reason: Opens on the newsletter's findings and caveats; the plain answer (trust only counsel you can name and weigh, unhurried, brought near a friend) is gathered only in 'The test' near the end, then talk-together.
ll241-advice-with-no-name-on-it-the-paid.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Who would you trust with your money? Only counsel you can weigh. The Word commands counsel (Proverbs 11:14), but a counsellor is someone you can name and look at: his life, what he gains if you act, and whether his last word came true. An anonymous paid room offers a counsellor's authority with a stranger's accountability. Watch for haste and for the cherry-picked win, which is a crooked weight. Here is how the Word teaches you to weigh every voice.
ll241-advice-with-no-name-on-it-the-paid.example: ONE SCREENSHOT, FIVE QUESTIONS. Say a handle you have never met posts a screenshot of one large win on an option that expires in three days, and the room costs $100 a month. Run the test. Can I name this person and look at their life? No. Do they gain if I act? Yes, by my subscription. What is my loss if they are wrong? Possibly all of it. Is this gathering or haste? Haste. Would I show it to my household and one friend first? If not, that answers all five.
ll241-advice-with-no-name-on-it-the-paid.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Who would you trust with your money? Someone you can weigh. Not a handle with no name on it, not a screenshot with the losses lifted off the pan, and not a voice that hurries you toward a thing that expires on Thursday. Trust counsel whose life you can see, ask what they gain when you act, and bring it near a friend who can see your face (Proverbs 27:17). The Word is not against profit; it is against the haste that eats the man. Wealth gotten by vanity is diminished, but he that gathereth by labour shall increase (Proverbs 13:11).

teen.open: Who should you trust with money advice? Someone you can actually name and whose life you can see, not a random account selling fast wins.
teen.close: So trust people you can know and check, who are not rushing you. A screenshot of one big win hides the losses. Ask a real friend before you act, and build slowly by honest work.

senior.open: The title asks whom you would trust with your money. The Word's answer is counsel you can weigh: a named person whose life and gain you can see, not an anonymous voice in a paid room.
senior.close: So the answer is plain. Seek many counsellors, but only ones you can name and examine. Beware of haste and of the cherry-picked win, which is a false balance. Gather by labour, and talk it over with someone who knows you before you act.

ll238-who-holds-the-wind-the-warning-the.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. What does Scripture say about the storm? The One who raises the wind is the One who stills it, so start with Him. teen.open: When a big storm is coming, what does the Bible say to do? Trust Yahweh, who holds the wind, get ready wisely, and help your neighbors.
teen.close: So prepare like Noah, don't pretend to know tomorrow, and build your life on doing what Jesus says. When you are scared, trust Him anyway. And go help the neighbor who can't get ready alone.

senior.open: The title asks what Scripture says about storm warnings, a sure foundation, and the neighbour in the storm's path. It begins with who holds the wind: Yahweh raises it and stills it.
senior.close: So the counsel is whole. Heed the warning and prepare, without claiming to know the outcome. Stand on the rock of doing His sayings, for the same rain falls on every house. Trust Him while still afraid, and let your care for your neighbour be in deed.

ll242-shyness-can-be-pride-the-omitted-t.reason: The opening states the claim (shyness can be pride; the omitted term is a Person), and section eleven lands it, but the lesson ends on talk-together and a homework list rather than the answer.
ll242-shyness-can-be-pride-the-omitted-t.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Is your shyness hiding something? It can be. Not your temperament, which Scripture never rebukes, but a sentence: I am too small, too slow, too young. Moses, Jeremiah, Gideon and Saul each said it, and each left out the same term, the One who made them and sends them. That omission can be pride in modest clothes. And what it hides is usually something entrusted to you and buried. Here is how the Word shows it.
ll242-shyness-can-be-pride-the-omitted-t.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Is your shyness hiding something? It may be hiding the Maker you left out of your sentence about yourself, and a talent you have buried. Yahweh did not argue with Moses' slow tongue; He named Himself as its Maker and promised to be with his mouth (Exodus 4:11-12). Put His name back into the sentence, and shew your works out of a good conversation, with meekness (James 3:13).

teen.open: Could being shy be hiding something? Sometimes it hides Yahweh, when we say I can't and forget that He made us and goes with us.
teen.close: So shyness itself is not a sin, and you don't have to become loud. But don't bury what Yahweh gave you. Add Him back into your I can't, and quietly use your gift where people can see it.

senior.open: The title asks whether your shyness is hiding something. The Word answers that it can: the self-smallest sentence leaves out the Maker, and it can bury what He entrusted to you.
senior.close: So the answer is careful and plain. Scripture never rebukes a temperament; it rebukes withheld obedience. Put the Maker back into the sentence, ask Him to shew you His ways, and let what you have been given be seen in how you live.

ll243-the-stork-knows-her-appointed-time.reason: Opens on the BirdReturns post; the why (the land and creatures are His, so He built rest, margin and season into law, with blessing attached, not funding) is reasoned out piecemeal and stated only near the end.
ll243-the-stork-knows-her-appointed-time.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Farmers are now paid to flood fields at the right weeks, and the birds come back. And He wrote it so His people would keep their appointed times as faithfully as the stork keeps hers.
ll243-the-stork-knows-her-appointed-time.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Why did Yahweh write the schedule into His law first? Because He made the land, the rain in his due season, and the stork that keeps her appointed times. He wrote rest, margin and season into statute, the land's sabbath feeding the ground, the poor and the beasts, with the blessing fastened to the sheaf you leave lying (Deuteronomy 24:19). So dress the land and keep it, under its Owner, and keep the appointed time you already know about.

teen.open: Farmers flood fields at just the right time and birds come back. Why was that kind of timing already in Yahweh's law? Because He made the land, the seasons, and the birds.
teen.close: So Yahweh wrote rest and good timing into His law because it is His world, and He already built a calendar into the birds. The stork is never late. What appointed time are you skipping?

senior.open: The title asks why Yahweh wrote into His law the same pattern farmers are now paid to follow. The earth is His, and He built rest, margin and due season into the land and into the creatures before any programme noticed it.
senior.close: So the answer is ownership and design. His law gave the land its sabbath and left margin for the poor and the beasts, with a blessing that outlasts any subsidy. We are rediscovering His engineering. The stork keeps her appointed times; the question is whether we keep ours.

ll244-the-heavens-declare-and-the-timeta.reason: A very long lesson; the 'which clock' answer (sort every claim into three buckets, hold the timetable open, rest confidence on the Creator) is set out early-middle, then buried under dating, brain and mind material; ends on Job and talk-together.
ll244-the-heavens-declare-and-the-timeta.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. The sky preaches, but which clock are you reading? Sort every claim into three buckets. What Scripture states, that He created and it was very good, is held firmly and does not move. What is measured is weighed by its method and its range. What is reasoned on top is a model, and must be labelled as one. The age of the earth is held open here, because the Word does not make the timetable the point. Confidence rests on the Creator, not on a chronology. Here is how to sort it.
ll244-the-heavens-declare-and-the-timeta.example: THE WRONG CLOCK. Radiocarbon dates once-living material, bone, wood, cloth or charcoal, and what it dates is a death. Its ceiling is roughly fifty to sixty thousand years; past that, an honest laboratory reports that the sample is beyond the range of the method. So if someone uses carbon dating to argue about millions of years, in either direction, they have picked up the wrong instrument. That is bucket two read outside its range, which the lesson calls a false balance (Proverbs 11:1).
ll244-the-heavens-declare-and-the-timeta.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Which clock are you reading? Read Scripture's plain words as the fixed clock: He created, it was very good, and man bears His image. Read measurements honestly, inside their range, and give weight where independent methods agree. Read models as models, and say so out loud. Hold the timetable open where the Word does not make it the point (Deuteronomy 29:29). Then you can hold a telescope and a Bible in the same hands and lose nothing, because your confidence rests on the One who calls the stars by name, and not one faileth (Isaiah 40:26).

teen.open: Creation shouts that Yahweh made it. But when people argue about how old things are, which clock should you trust? Sort what the Bible says from what is measured and what is guessed.
teen.close: So read the Bible's plain words as the sure clock: Yahweh made it all, and it was very good. Treat measurements and theories honestly, label them, and don't let them shake you. Your confidence is in Him, not a date.

senior.open: The title asks which clock we are reading when creation is discussed. The lesson's answer is to sort every claim: what Scripture states, what is measured, and what is reasoned on top, with the timetable held open.
senior.close: So the clock to stand on is what the Word plainly says: He created, and it was very good. Measurements are weighed within their range, and models are named as models. Our confidence rests on the Creator, not on a chronology.

ll245-deductive-reasoning-is-the-words-w.reason: The thesis is stated up front, but the title's serpent question is answered only implicitly in section two, and the final lines blend practice with a summary that never returns to the garden.
ll245-deductive-reasoning-is-the-words-w.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Did the serpent win with a misquote? In the garden, yes. He did not open with a lie about the fruit but with a question that bent Yahweh's words. The woman added words He never said, "neither shall ye touch it", and only then did he deny Him outright. She reasoned well from a corrupted premise, and the conclusion was death. Yahweh's exact words guard every conclusion because they are the only safe premise. Here is how the Word shows it.
ll245-deductive-reasoning-is-the-words-w.example: TWO PREMISES, TWO ENDINGS. What He said: of every tree you may freely eat, except one (Genesis 2:16-17). What she remembered: we may not eat of it, neither touch it (Genesis 3:3). One added clause. It sounded careful, even devout, and it moved the premise off His words. In the wilderness the same tempter quoted a psalm, and Jesus answered, It is written again (Matthew 4:7): the rest of what He said governed the verse pulled loose. Same tempter, same method, opposite ending, decided by the premise.
ll245-deductive-reasoning-is-the-words-w.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Did the serpent win with a misquote? In the garden he did: distort what He said, add to it, deny it, and careful reasoning carried a bent premise all the way to death. In the wilderness he lost, because Jesus answered three times, It is written. That is how Yahweh's exact words guard your conclusions. Write what He said, word for word, with what stands around it. Mark your own steps as yours. Check them against another place He spoke. Stop where He stopped (Deuteronomy 29:29). Reason from His words and nothing else, and you will think His thoughts after Him.

teen.open: Did the serpent trick Eve with a twisted quote? Yes. He bent what Yahweh said, she added to it, and then he denied it outright.
teen.close: So the serpent won in the garden by changing Yahweh's words, but lost against Jesus, who said It is written. Check what He actually said before you decide anything. His exact words keep you safe.

senior.open: The title asks whether the serpent won with a misquote. In the garden he did: he distorted Yahweh's words, the woman added to them, and then he denied them, and the conclusion followed from the bent premise.
senior.close: So the answer is yes, and the guard is plain. Reason only from what He actually said, word for word, check it against the rest of the Word, and stop where He stopped. That is how Jesus answered the same tempter, and how we think His thoughts after Him.

ll246-doing-the-word-comes-first-and-our.reason: The answer (no: do first, understanding follows, John 7:17) sits among four 'breaths' in the opening and section one; the manna link waits for part four; stories follow the ending.
ll246-doing-the-word-comes-first-and-our.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Do you need to understand the Word before you do it? No. Doing comes first, and understanding is made in the doing. That is understanding made in the doing, the kind the Word promised and the only kind there is.
ll246-doing-the-word-comes-first-and-our.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Do you need to understand it first? Caleb called the giants bread and was still eating it at eighty-five. So do the Word before you understand it. The understanding is waiting on the other side of the doing, and Yahweh is the One who makes it there.

teen.open: Do you have to understand the Word before you obey it? No. You do it first, and the understanding comes while you are doing it.
teen.close: So you don't have to figure it all out first. Do what the Word says today, and Yahweh will grow your understanding through it.

senior.open: The title asks whether we must understand the Word before we do it. The Word's answer is no: Jesus said that whoever does His will shall know of the doctrine (John 7:17).
senior.close: So understanding is not the entry fee for obedience; it is the harvest of it. Do what you already know to do, and Yahweh makes the knowledge in the doing, as He did with the manna.

ll247-your-ways-show-your-god-know-yours.reason: Opens on six of Darrell's sentences; the yes and the how (count the real record, ask the nine fruits present or absent) arrive in sections two and five; ends on Psalm 139.
ll247-your-ways-show-your-god-know-yours.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Can you measure yourself by your fruit? Yes, and the Word says it is the honest way. Jesus said you shall know them by their fruits (Matthew 7:20), and that includes you. Measure yourself in number, from the real record of your days, dollars and hours, and in kind, by asking the nine fruits of the Spirit one at a time. What your ways show is the truth about who you follow. Here is how the Word shows it.
ll247-your-ways-show-your-god-know-yours.example: ONE CLAIM, COUNTED. Say you tell yourself you are generous. Longsuffering, or did you keep count? Mark each present or absent without pleading. If the record and the claim disagree, the claim is the thing that is wrong.
ll247-your-ways-show-your-god-know-yours.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Can you measure yourself by your fruit? Yes. Your own eyes will call every way right (Proverbs 21:2), but the record will not flatter you. And whatever your ways serve is your god. So let the measure lead you to turn, until what you do shows Yahweh.

teen.open: Can you really measure yourself by your fruit? Yes. Jesus said a tree is known by its fruit, and that goes for you too.
teen.close: So check what you actually did this week, not just what you say about yourself. Your actions show who you follow, so let them show Yahweh.

senior.open: The title asks whether a person can measure himself by his fruit. The Word says yes: the tree is known by its fruit (Matthew 12:33), and the honest measure is taken both in number and in kind.
senior.close: So the measure is plain. Count from the real record, ask the nine fruits of the Spirit, and let the claim give way wherever the record disagrees. What our ways serve is our god.

ll248-his-ways-are-higher-so-he-gives-th.reason: The how (Isaiah 55:10-11: the higher thought comes down as bread, received by eating) is in section two of eleven; glory, suffering and meekness follow; ends on John 6:68.

ll248-his-ways-are-higher-so-he-gives-th.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Your plans are not the final word, because you do not know what the morrow holds (James 4:14). His thoughts are higher, and they come down to you as bread: His Word, and the situations He gives you to go through. You eat it daily, like manna, often before you understand it, meekly and with the glory given back to Him. Then comprehension comes, and it is never what you thought it was. That is how His higher thought becomes yours: not by reaching up, but by eating what He sends down.

teen.open: Can you figure out Yahweh's plan just by thinking hard? No. His thoughts are higher than ours, so He sends them down to us as bread: His Word, and the days He gives us.
teen.close: So don't try to predict everything. Eat today's bread: read the Word, obey what you can see, give Him the credit, and the understanding will come.

senior.open: The title says our plans are not the final word, and asks how His higher thoughts reach us. Isaiah answers in the next breath: His word comes down like rain that gives bread to the eater (Isaiah 55:10-11).
senior.close: So we do not climb to His thoughts; He sends them down. We receive them as bread, by taking His Word and walking through what He gives, meekly and giving Him the glory, and comprehension follows the eating.

ll249-nothing-of-myself-the-way-is-the-w.reason: Opens on Darrell's questions; the direct yes (the branch that draws nothing from itself bears much fruit, John 15:5) arrives in section four; ends on John 3:30, not on the fruit.
ll249-nothing-of-myself-the-way-is-the-w.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Can you become nothing and still bear much fruit? Yes, and it is the only way. Becoming nothing does not mean being worth nothing; it means drawing nothing from yourself as the source, as Jesus did nothing of Himself (John 5:30). A branch that abides in the vine brings forth much fruit, and without Him it can do nothing (John 15:5). Here is how the Word shows it.
ll249-nothing-of-myself-the-way-is-the-w.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Can you become nothing and still bear much fruit? Yes, because the nothing is where the fruit starts. Jesus emptied Himself, served, obeyed, and was lifted up (Philippians 2:7-9). He drew nothing from Himself, sought no glory, and did what He heard. When you do the same, you are a branch on the Vine: you want no glory, you do the verb in each of His names, and the fruit comes through you. That rule does not change, because He does not change. He increases, you decrease, and much fruit follows.

teen.open: Can you be nothing and still do great things for Yahweh? Yes. Like a branch on a vine, the fruit comes from staying connected to Jesus, not from being big yourself.
teen.close: So stop trying to be the source. Stay connected to Jesus, give Him the credit, and do what He says. That is how a branch bears much fruit.

senior.open: The title asks whether a person can become nothing and still bear much fruit. Jesus answers it in John 15:5: without Him we can do nothing, but the branch that abides in Him brings forth much fruit.
senior.close: So emptying self is not loss; it is the condition of fruit. Draw nothing from yourself, seek no glory, abide in the Vine, and the fruit He promised comes, the same way every time.

ll250-they-which-do-hunger-shall-be-fill.reason: The promise is quoted early, but why it runs on doing (hunger proven by coming and eating; the sluggard desires and has nothing; the undone is sin) is spread over sections two, five and six.
ll250-they-which-do-hunger-shall-be-fill.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. If you are hungry for righteousness, why can you still feel stuck? Because in the Word, hunger is not a feeling you announce; it is something you do. They which do hunger shall be filled (Matthew 5:6). The sluggard desires and has nothing, while the diligent is made fat (Proverbs 13:4). Yahweh's promise reads what you do and what you leave undone, not what you say. Here is how it works.
ll250-they-which-do-hunger-shall-be-fill.example: ONE UNDONE LIST. Say a woman tells her friends she is hungry for the Word, but her Bible has not been opened in a month, and the visit she meant to make to a sick neighbor is still unmade. Her desire is real. Her Undone list is the evidence. Writing both down, treating them as real, and doing the first one today is what turns desire into the hunger Jesus called blessed.
ll250-they-which-do-hunger-shall-be-fill.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Hungry, yet stuck? The promise has not failed; it runs on doing. Hunger that gets up and eats is filled, as surely as the crowd was filled with the loaves (Matthew 14:20). Desire that will not move has nothing, and the good you know to do and leave undone is sin (James 4:17). So put the first task first: seek His kingdom and His righteousness, make your Undone list, and do the first item now. Yahweh's shall does not change. They which do hunger shall be filled.

teen.open: Want to grow closer to Yahweh but feel stuck? His promise to fill the hungry is for people who act on their hunger, not just talk about it.
teen.close: So don't just say you're hungry. Do the next thing He has shown you, today. The ones who do hunger are the ones who get filled.

senior.open: The title asks why a hungry person can still be stuck. The Word's answer is that hunger after righteousness shows in what we do; desire alone, Proverbs says, has nothing (Proverbs 13:4).
senior.close: So the promise of Matthew 5:6 is sure, and it reads our doing, including what we leave undone. Seek Him first, act on the first undone thing today, and expect to be filled.

ll251-that-rock-was-christ-identity-not-.reason: Opens on the episode summary; the plain no (identity is born of the Rock, Christ, not of blood; lineage is a gift, not the foundation) is built across sections three to six.
ll251-that-rock-was-christ-identity-not-.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Is your roots story the foundation of who you are? No. Your family history is real and worth honoring, but it is not the foundation. The foundation is the Rock, and the Word says that Rock was Christ (1 Corinthians 10:4). Those who receive Him are born not of blood but of Yahweh (John 1:12-13). Identity is born of the Rock, not of a bloodline. Here is how the Word shows it.
ll251-that-rock-was-christ-identity-not-.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Is your roots story the foundation? No. In the wilderness Israel drank from the Rock, and the Rock begat them before any genealogy counted them (Deuteronomy 32:18). That Rock was Christ, Yahweh in the flesh. Every Israelite there had the bloodline, and it was unbelief, not descent, that kept many out (Hebrews 3:19). So keep your family's story as a gift, and stand on the Rock as your foundation. Whoever comes to Him is born of Yahweh, and the water from the Rock flows to all who come.

teen.open: Is where your family comes from the base of who you are? It matters, but it isn't the foundation. Jesus is the Rock, and your identity is born from Him.
teen.close: So learn your family's story and be thankful for it. But build on the Rock. You belong to Yahweh's family by trusting Jesus, not by blood.

senior.open: The title asks whether our roots story is the foundation of who we are. The Word honors lineage, yet it says those who receive Christ are born not of blood but of Yahweh (John 1:12-13).
senior.close: So our history is a gift, and the Rock is the foundation. That Rock was Christ (1 Corinthians 10:4), and an identity built on Him holds where any bloodline would not.

ll252-this-life-is-the-curriculum-made-t.reason: A long opening lists fifty-three messages; the answer (no deception, freedom by His Word, directed paths, choosing the Son) sits in section three and is scattered after; ends on Revelation 3:20.
ll252-this-life-is-the-curriculum-made-t.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Your life is a course, and Yahweh is the Teacher. What happens when you learn from Him, the One who cannot lie (Titus 1:2)? You stop learning from a place of deception. You start with His Word, let every man be a liar, yourself included, and the truth makes you free (John 8:31-32). He directs your steps, makes you His temple, and leads you to the one decision the course is for: agreeing with the Son and living. Here is how the Word shows it.
ll252-this-life-is-the-curriculum-made-t.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. What happens when you learn from the Teacher who cannot lie? Nothing in your course rests on a guess. You start with the Word, and its entrance gives light (Psalms 119:130). You see your own beam first and humble yourself to His account. Opposition becomes bread, your body becomes His temple, and your life becomes the evidence others can read. And the course reaches its purpose: you settle the one decision, agree with the Son, and live. Then you open the door when He knocks, and He comes in.

teen.open: Your life is like a class, and Yahweh is the Teacher. He cannot lie, so when you learn from Him, you are learning what is really true.
teen.close: So start each day with His Word, trust it over your own guesses, and say yes to Jesus. That is how this course ends well: with Him living in you.

senior.open: The title says life is already a course, and asks what happens when we learn from the Teacher who cannot lie. We learn without deception: His Word is settled, and continuing in it makes us free (John 8:31-32).
senior.close: So the curriculum has a sure Teacher and a sure end. Begin with the Word, let Him correct the picture in our own heads, and settle the one decision that matters: agree with the Son and live.

ll255-all-things-work-together-the-integ.reason: Section one answers (all things work together for good to those who love Him, toward the Son's likeness; for or against by alignment), but it ends on family discussion steps.
ll255-all-things-work-together-the-integ.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Does every hard day really work toward good? For those who love Yahweh and are called according to His purpose, yes (Romans 8:28). The good is not a feeling; it is being shaped into the likeness of the Son (Romans 8:29). But the same events can run for you or against you, depending on whether you walk in His will and His Way. Here is how the Word shows both.
ll255-all-things-work-together-the-integ.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Does every hard day really work toward good? Yes, when you love Yahweh and walk in His will and Way. The hard day is not pleasant, and the Word never says it is, but it works for you a far more exceeding weight of glory (2 Corinthians 4:17) and forms the Son's likeness in you. Joseph's brothers meant evil, and Yahweh meant it for good. So choose life, hold The Way you know, let Him direct the path you cannot see, and trust Him with the details. Nothing is running loose.

teen.open: Does every hard day really turn out for good? For those who love Yahweh and follow His Way, yes. It may not feel good, but He is using it to make you more like Jesus.
teen.close: So on a hard day, stay on His Way and trust Him. He is into every detail, and He is working it toward good.

senior.open: The title asks whether every hard day truly works toward good. Romans 8:28 says it does for those who love Yahweh and are called according to His purpose, and the next verse names the good: the likeness of His Son.
senior.close: So the promise holds, and its condition holds with it. Keep His will and His Way, let Him direct the route day by day, and every hard day is worked into the Son's likeness in you.

ll256-the-lords-release-is-for-a-neighbo.reason: Opens on the Deuteronomy 15 release; the answer (Jesus defines the neighbor by mercy shown across the line, so be one) comes in section two; ends on family discussion steps.
ll256-the-lords-release-is-for-a-neighbo.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Who counts as your neighbor when the crowd is mixed? Jesus turned the question around. In His story the neighbor was the Samaritan, the one who showed mercy across the line between peoples (Luke 10:36-37). So the question is not who qualifies for your care, but whether you will be the neighbor. In a mixed multitude, everyone on your road who needs mercy is someone to love as yourself. Here is how the Word shows it.
ll256-the-lords-release-is-for-a-neighbo.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Who counts as your neighbor when the crowd is mixed? Everyone on your road who needs mercy, and the real question is whether you will be a neighbor to them. Yahweh wrote one law for the homeborn and the stranger, and He told His people to seek the peace of the city (Jeremiah 29:7). Love speaks the truth about sin, refuses revenge, opens its hand and binds the wound. Then it leaves the harvest to the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, who are always working. Go, and do thou likewise.

teen.open: Who is your neighbor when the people around you are so different? Jesus said it is anyone who needs mercy, and your job is to be the neighbor.
teen.close: So don't ask who deserves your help. Show mercy to whoever is in front of you, tell the truth kindly, and trust Yahweh with the rest.

senior.open: The title asks who counts as a neighbor in a mixed multitude. Jesus answered with the Samaritan: the neighbor is the one who shows mercy, across the line (Luke 10:36-37).
senior.close: So the neighbor is not a smaller circle we draw but a role we take up. Open the hand, speak the truth in love, refuse revenge, and leave the harvest to Yahweh, who is always working.

ll254-laziness-is-a-character-matter-the.reason: First line says laziness is a character matter, but the why (sin to repent of, worship withheld, made in a working image) is spread through the lesson; it ends on practice steps.
ll254-laziness-is-a-character-matter-the.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Is laziness really just a habit? No. The Word treats it as a matter of character: a sin to repent of, not a personality trait to file away. You were made in the image of a working Yahweh, and work done heartily as to the Lord is worship (Colossians 3:23). So slothfulness is not only lost output; it is worship withheld. Here is how Proverbs shows its five marks.
ll254-laziness-is-a-character-matter-the.example: ONE UNFINISHED THING. Say a report has sat half-written for three weeks. The reason given is always sensible: too busy, the wrong time, wait until the details settle. That is the lion in the road. The draft is opened every morning and closed every night without moving: the door on its hinges. It is nearly done: the hand that will not come back to the mouth. The practice is simple: finish it today, and tell one person, so the fourth mark has nowhere to hide.
ll254-laziness-is-a-character-matter-the.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Is laziness really just a habit? No. It is a character matter, and Proverbs shows its five marks plainly: the lion in the road, the door on its hinges, the hand that never comes back, the man wiser in his own conceit, and the one who needs a ruler to start. You were made in the image of a Yahweh who works, and your work is worship. So repent of it as sin, not as personality, and lean on Him who works in you both to will and to do (Philippians 2:13). Then finish the one thing that has waited longest.

teen.open: Is being lazy just a habit? The Bible says it is more than that. It is about character, because Yahweh made you in His image, and He works.
