ll336-the-lie-the-fear-and-the-last-adam.reason: Opening hints (broken trust and broken law, the cross answers both) but the second half of the title, whether trust can be restored, is only answered in sections five to seven; ends on weekly practices.
ll336-the-lie-the-fear-and-the-last-adam.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Did sin start with a lie, and can trust be restored? Yes to both. The serpent first questioned what Yahweh said, then called Him a liar; the heart stopped trusting before the hand took the fruit, and fear came in. Sin is also a broken law with a real sentence. Jesus, the Last Adam, trusted where Adam doubted, and His Blood paid that sentence, so trust can be restored. Here is how the Word shows it.
ll336-the-lie-the-fear-and-the-last-adam.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Did sin start with a lie, and can trust be restored? It did: a lie about Yahweh's goodness was believed, and the first man hid among the trees saying, I was afraid. And sin is a transgression of His law, with death as its wages. But the Last Adam trusted the Father all the way to His last breath, bore our sins on the tree, and destroyed the power of death. For the one who believes, the guilt is gone, a new heart is given, and perfect love casts out fear (1 John 4:18). When you sin, come out of hiding the same day. Trust is restored by the Blood.

teen.open: Did sin start with a lie, and can trust in Yahweh be fixed? Yes. Adam and Eve believed a lie, then hid in fear. Jesus trusted the Father perfectly and died for our sin, so trust can be restored.
teen.close: So, did sin start with a lie? Yes. Can trust be restored? Yes, through Jesus. His Blood takes away our guilt, His love drives out fear, and we never have to hide from Yahweh again.

senior.open: The title asks whether sin began with a lie and whether trust can be restored. Scripture answers yes on both counts: the lie broke trust and brought fear, and Christ's obedience and Blood restore what was lost.
senior.close: So the answer stands. Sin is both broken trust and broken law, and the cross answers both. Justified by faith, we have peace with Yahweh, and the love that loved us first casts out fear.

ll335-not-done-in-a-corner.reason: Opening states plainly that Yahweh did not raise His Son in secret, and the body names witnesses, the early creed and James; but it ends on memory-work practices instead of landing the answer.
ll335-not-done-in-a-corner.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Was the Resurrection ever hidden? No; it was not done in a corner (Acts 26:26). The first thing passed on was a short word: Christ died for our sins, was buried, rose the third day, and was seen. He was seen by Peter, the twelve, over five hundred at once, and by His own brother James, who had not believed until the risen Jesus appeared to him. Here is how the Word shows it.
ll335-not-done-in-a-corner.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Was the Resurrection ever hidden? Never. It was preached in public to people who could check it, with most of the five hundred witnesses still alive to be asked. The first word handed on named the death, the burial, the rising and the people who saw Him. The witnesses were not expecting it; they had to be convinced. James, who had once thought his brother was beside himself, saw Him and later called Him Lord. These things are written that you might believe and have life through His name (John 20:31). When someone asks, give them the witnesses.

teen.open: Was Jesus' rising from the dead kept secret? No. Hundreds of people saw Him alive, and even His brother James, who did not believe in Him before, believed after he saw Him.
teen.close: So was the Resurrection hidden? No. It happened in the open, with real witnesses, and even doubters were convinced. It was written down so that you can believe and have life in Jesus.

senior.open: The title asks whether the Resurrection was ever hidden. The Word answers that it was not done in a corner: it was handed on early, with named witnesses, many still living to be questioned.
senior.close: So the answer is plain. The rising of Jesus was public, attested by Peter, the twelve, five hundred brethren, James and Paul, men not inclined to believe. It is recorded so that we may believe and have life through His name.

ll337-not-far-from-the-kingdom.reason: Opening plainly answers (he drew near several truths but did not come to Christ), and section seven lands near-is-not-in; but the lesson ends on talk and weekly practices, not the answer.
ll337-not-far-from-the-kingdom.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Can a person be near the kingdom yet outside it? Yes. The scribe answered well and was told he was not far; Agrippa was almost persuaded. Malcolm X saw true things: hidden sin comes out, trust in a man breaks, truth costs, and people are of one blood. Yet seeing those truths is not salvation, and being a good person is a test none of us passes. The door is a Person: there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved (Acts 4:12). We do not judge his heart. We take the warning, and the hope, for ourselves.

teen.open: Can someone get close to the truth about Yahweh and still miss Him? Yes. This lesson looks at a man who learned true things but did not come to Jesus.
teen.close: So can you be near the kingdom and still outside? Yes. Knowing some true things is not the same as trusting Jesus. He is the only way in, so make sure you are not just close, but in.

senior.open: The title asks how one may be near the kingdom yet outside it. A life that came to see true things about leaders, truth and one blood, yet did not come to Christ, shows the difference.
senior.close: So the answer is sobering and hopeful. Nearness to truth is not entrance; salvation is in no other name than Jesus. We leave the man's heart to Yahweh and pray for all who are near and not yet in.
